title: Jadeveon Clowney: I could have made more money elsewhere, I want a Super Bowl in Houston
summary: "It's Year 13, I started here, go back here, try to win, and see how the rest of my career goes," Clowney said.
full_text: ''' Jadeveon Clowney says he's back in Houston for one reason: To win a championship with his original team. Clowney said after officially signing his contract with the Texans that he had better financial offers from other teams, but he wants to win a title with the team that selected him with the first overall pick in the 2014 NFL draft. "Trying to chase that Super Bowl with the Texans," Clowney said. "It wasn't about money because I could have went other places for a little bit more money than this. But I'm like, it's Year 13, I started here, go back here, try to win, and see how the rest of my career goes." Clowney said he's a very different person now at age 33 than he was when he arrived as a 21-year-old rookie, and he hopes to impart some wisdom on the younger players. "I was a big kid when I first got here," Clowney said. "I grew up different than a lot of these guys. When I was born my dad was in jail, single-parent home, I grew up a lot different. I got here, never seen Houston, I enjoyed my time, it was fun, I came up with a great group of guys. Coming back now, I'm a veteran, a lot older, a lot smarter than I was before." Clowney said he was touched by how loudly the Houston fans cheered for him when he took the field for training camp practice on Tuesday. "It's a great feeling after all these years to come back and they still got love for you and happy that you're back here," Clowney said. "It's a blessing."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Tua Tagovailoa on training camp with Michael Penix: "It's definitely a competition"
summary: Both of the Falcons' quarterbacks are limited with injuries, but Tagovailoa says that isn't stopping them from competing.
full_text: Falcons quarterbacks Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix are both limited by injuries in training camp, but that isn't stopping them from competing for the starting job. Tagovailoa said on NFL Network that while he rests an injured back and Penix rehabs the torn ACL he suffered in November, they continue to compete. "I view it as a competition. I understand he can't take some team reps right now because of what he's going through, but he's still being able to compete in seven-on-seven, he's still able to go through some plays," Tagovailoa said. "It's definitely a competition." Tagovailoa said his own back injury won't limit him for much longer. "Nothing too serious, just a caution kind of thing where we're not rushing it. It was just a flare-up, nothing big, not anything long-term. We'll be fine," Tagovailoa said. The Falcons have to hope at least one of their quarterbacks will be 100 percent when they open the season on September 13 against the Steelers.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Shedeur Sanders, Deshaun Watson will each get a preseason start
summary: The leader after two preseason games is expected to start the third preseason game.
full_text: Browns coach Todd Monken originally hoped to name a starting quarterback by the offseason program. That didn't happen, with the competition continuing into training camp. Monken finally has revealed his timeline for a decision. He told Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network that Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson will each start a preseason game. The next week will determine who starts Aug. 15 at Chicago and who starts the Aug. 22 home game against the Bills. The leader likely starts the final preseason game on Aug. 27 against the Patriots. Watson has played only 19 games since arriving in Cleveland in 2022. He hasn't played since October of 2024, twice tearing his Achilles since. Sanders earned Pro Bowl honors as a rookie despite starting only seven games and completing 56.6 percent of his passes for 1,400 yards, with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions.
author: Charean Williams

title: Dr. Anthony Fauci's lawyer says Aaron Rodgers "should stick to football"
summary: The ball is back in Rodgers's court.
full_text: On Monday, Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers relentlessly attacked Dr. Anthony Fauci. The Rodgers assault, launched on ESPN, included calling Fauci an " absolute criminal " and repeatedly labeled Fauci an "absolute coward." At one point, Rodgers promoted a false conspiracy theory that Fauci's wife's sister is Ghislaine Maxwell. On Tuesday, Fauci's lawyer responded to Rodgers. Via Saad Yousuf of The Athletic , David Schertler said this via email: “Aaron Rodgers doesn’t know what he’s talking about. He should stick to football .” The other target of Rodgers's ire — ESPN — has repeatedly declined comment on Rodgers's comments. And so, as to Fauci, the ball returns to Rodgers's court. It remains to be seen whether he continues the dialogue at a league-required press conference, or during a resumption of his habit of appearing on McAfee's show on a regular basis. Last year, Rodgers stopped his Tuesday visits. This year, it's possible that he's just getting warmed up .
author: Mike Florio

title: A.J. Epenesa not inclined to discuss "weird situation" with Browns
summary: Before Eagles defensive end A.J.
full_text: '' Before Eagles defensive end A.J. Epenesa landed in Philadelphia, he had a one-year deal worth up to $5 million in place with the Browns. Until he didn't. The Browns pulled out of the agreement , due to concerns regarding his physical. Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Epenesa didn't want to say much about the Browns. He made it clear that he's happy to be with the Eagles. "Cleveland, you know, it was a weird situation," Epenesa told reporters. "But I don't necessarily want to go back and talk on that in just a weird sense but I'll just leave that in the past and just be happy that I'm not a Brown and that I'm an Eagle." Is Epenesa healthy now? "Very healthy," he said, "feeling good, and happy to be here." His contract with the Eagles pays much less than his contract with the Browns would have entailed — one year, $1.402 million. A second-round pick in 2020, Epenesa spent his first six seasons with the Bills.
author: Mike Florio

title: Aaron Rodgers had undisclosed illness before playoff loss to Texans
summary: "He looked terrible" before the game, said former Steelers offensive coordinator Arthur Smith.
full_text: If Aaron Rodgers was looking a little pale before Pittsburgh's playoff loss to the Texans, it wasn't because he was about to face the best defense in the NFL. As explained by Mike Silver of The Athletic , Rodgers was sick before the 30-6 home loss to Houston in the wild-card round. “I wasn’t feeling good, and I actually came over to the team hotel, and they sent me home — probably because I was pale and looked like shit,” Rodgers told Silver on Saturday from training camp. Silver said Rodgers's symptoms included fever and vomiting. He insisted that he had recovered before kickoff. “He’s definitely downplaying it,” former Steelers offensive coordinator Arthur Smith told Silver. “There was never a question he was gonna play, and he’s never one to complain, but he looked terrible [before the game].” It's not a great look nearly six months after the game, because the Steelers didn't disclose that Rodgers had an illness. Against the Texans, Rodgers completed 17 of 33 passes for 146 yards, no touchdowns, and one interception. His passer rating was a postseason career-low 50.8, with his final throw turning into a pick-six. Smith knows all too well the potential consequences of failing to disclose an illness. In 2023, Smith received a $25,000 fine (the Falcons separately had to fork over $75,000) for not disclosing that running back Bijan Robinson was ill on the morning of a game. (Robinson played in the game.) And so, in a week that has caused plenty of commotion regarding things Rodgers said publicly, what he (and, more specifically, the Steelers) failed to say before the playoff loss could cause a bit of a ruckus, as far as the league office is concerned.
author: Mike Florio

title: NFL declines comment on the Steelers' failure to disclose Aaron Rodgers' illness before playoff loss
summary: Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers recently disclosed to Mike Silver of The Athletic that Rodgers was ill before the January playoff loss to the Texans.
full_text: '' Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers recently disclosed to Mike Silver of The Athletic that Rodgers was ill before the January playoff loss to the Texans. The illness was not disclosed by the Steelers. In response to an inquiry from PFT on the situation, the NFL declined comment. In 2023, the NFL fined the Falcons $75,000 and then-coach Arthur Smith $25,000 for failing to disclose that running back Bijan Robinson had an illness on the morning of a game against the Buccaneers. The fact that the NFL has declined comment doesn't mean the league will ignore it. How can they? In this age of legalized and normalized betting, the failure of the Steelers to update their injury report to reveal that Rodgers had an illness is a problem on its face. The league has no choice but to investigate. If the reporting is true (and it is, we've confirmed), the league will have no choice but to act. Any other approach amounts to the league looking the other way on the Steelers concealing an important piece of inside information. Given the various ways in which inside information has allegedly or actually been misused in multiple sports (the NFL recently suspended a Cardinals executive for allegedly sharing information about the team's draft picks), inaction is not acceptable. If the league is going to profit from gambling, either directly through sponsorships or indirectly by owners owning up to five percent of companies that operate sportsbooks, the NFL cannot ignore clear instances of teams having inside information about a player's health and failing to reveal it.
author: Mike Florio

title: Free agent TE Zach Ertz cleared for football activities
summary: Free agent tight end Zach Ertz said in April that he didn't want his torn ACL to be the final act of his NFL career.
full_text: Free agent tight end Zach Ertz said in April that he didn't want his torn ACL to be the final act of his NFL career. He still is seeking an opportunity to make that wish come true. Doctors have cleared Ertz for all football activities, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. That should clear the way for Ertz to find a new team. He is working out at Stanford with his former college quarterback, Andrew Luck. Ertz, 35, tore the ACL in his right knee in a Dec. 7 game against the Vikings while playing for the Commanders. In his 13th NFL season, Ertz made 50 catches for 504 yards and four touchdowns for Washington. He has also played games for the Eagles and Cardinals and has spent time with the Lions.
author: Charean Williams

title: After rushing title, James Cook is looking forward to even bigger things
summary: Bills running back James Cook led the league in rushing last season with 1,621 yards.
full_text: Bills running back James Cook led the league in rushing last season with 1,621 yards. It came after a hold-in during training camp as he sought a new contract that he received after more than a week of not practicing. Last year, though, was last year. “I don’t like to talk about last year, because last year is in the past . This year is a new year,” Cook said, via John Wawrow of the Associated Press. “Put last year behind me, and just come out here to do it again.” Only two players since 2001 have won back-to-back rushing titles — Derrick Henry (2019-20) and LaDainian Tomlinson (2006-07). “I expect James Cook to take another step this year in different elements of his game and continue to be the workhorse as a runner,” new coach Joe Brady said. “And he wants it, right? He had such an incredible season last year. And without diving into exactly what, this is what I told him: He has got to get better. We can’t take steps backward.” Cook, 26, said he is "looking forward to doing even bigger things." He concedes his ball security has got to improve after losing four of seven fumbles last season, including one at the Denver 30 in a 33-30 overtime loss in the divisional round. “I fumbled, so I just got to fix it,” Cook said. “The ball is everybody’s job, and that’s my job. I’m willing to protect it.” The Bills are only 5-4 in the postseason in Cook's four seasons, losing in the divisional round three times and the AFC Championship Game once. They are the first team in NFL history to win a playoff game in six consecutive postseasons without reaching a Super Bowl. “It’s on us. The ball is in our hands,” Cook said. “We control our own destiny. So whatever we do is on us. Eventually, it’s going to happen.”
author: Charean Williams

title: Carson Beck excited to start the Hall of Fame Game
summary: Carson Beck had "no clue" he was going to start the Pro Football Hall of Fame Game until this week.
full_text: ' Carson Beck had "no clue" he was going to start the Pro Football Hall of Fame Game until this week. He was the last to know. As (almost) everyone knows, veteran quarterbacks don't generally play in the Hall of Fame Game. The third-round rookie is new to this thing, though. "I thought I was going to play, but I had no expectations ," Beck said Tuesday, via Darren Urban of the team website. "Obviously our schedule has been crazy right now. But I'm looking forward to it." Coach Mike LaFleur has not publicly addressed playing time for his quarterbacks, but with Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew expected to spend the night on the sideline, Beck likely sees most of the playing time. Fourth-stringer Kedon Slovis also could play. Beck said he hasn't been nervous for a game since he was 8 years old and playing for his Pop Warner city championship, and that won't change Thursday night. "It's a game at the end of the day," Beck said. "Not really any nerves. More excitement than anything." Beck, 24, spent six seasons in college and played in the national championship game last season for the University of Miami. So, he should be unfazed playing a preseason game against the Panthers on Thursday. "That's one of the best things about him, all of his experience," offensive coordinator Nathaniel Hackett said. "His age, his understanding that things are going to go good, [and] they are going to go bad. You can never get too excited; you can never get too frustrated."
author: Charean Williams

title: Patriots claim WR Tejhaun Palmer off waivers
summary: The Patriots claimed wide receiver Tejhaun Palmer off waivers on Tuesday, the team announced.
full_text: '' The Patriots claimed wide receiver Tejhaun Palmer off waivers on Tuesday, the team announced. The Cardinals waived Palmer on Monday. In a corresponding move, the Patriots released rookie tight end Jeremiah Franklin. Palmer, 26, entered the NFL as a sixth-round draft pick by Arizona in 2024 out of UAB. He spent the majority of his first two NFL seasons on the practice squad. He signed with Arizona's active roster on Jan. 3 and saw action in the regular-season finale. Franklin, 22, signed with the Patriots as a rookie free agent from Boston College on July 24. He appeared in 41 games during his four seasons at Boston College and finished with 93 receptions for 1,010 yards and six touchdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Aaron Donald looks to establish a media and entertainment footprint
summary: As defensive tackle Aaron Donald focuses for now on whether he'll end a two-year playing hiatus in pursuit of a second Super Bowl ring, he's activating a longer-term vision for his post-football future.
full_text: As defensive tackle Aaron Donald focuses for now on whether he'll end a two-year playing hiatus in pursuit of a second Super Bowl ring, he's activating a longer-term vision for his post-football future. Via Ryan Glasspiegel of Front Office Sports , Donald has hired Jon Rosen of Envisionary to "grow his businesses, brand partnerships, and overall profile in the media and entertainment industries ." Per Glasspiegel, Donald is currently developing a docuseries. Earlier this year, Donald served as a guest analyst for NBC's Super Bowl pregame show. He has otherwise kept a fairly low profile since retiring after the 2023 season. It appears that Donald will be re-entering the public eye in a significant way. All that's left to be determined is whether it's as a player, as a media personality — or both. Still, another season as a high-profile player on a franchise that will play at least seven prime-time games in 2026 will go a long way towards increasing his profile generally. Which becomes an even better way to fuel his looming foray into media and entertainment.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bengals' offensive players and coaches say Dexter Lawrence is dominating practices
summary: The Bengals' offense has a problem in training camp: Dexter Lawrence.
full_text: The Bengals' offense has a problem in training camp: Dexter Lawrence. Lawrence, the defensive tackle who arrived in Cincinnati in a trade with the Giants this offseason, has been a menace, even though he's not allowed to touch the quarterback. Bengals guard Dalton Risner told Jori Epstein of Yahoo Sports that Lawrence is bringing intensity to training camp. "There's certain guys in this league like Dexter who wreck a whole game play and you have to do everything around them and you change everything you're doing," Risner said. "You're going to have to change how you block against certain guys. He's just making us do it really early and really often." Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase said Lawrence is causing the Bengals' offense problems. "Honestly, he's been terrorizing practice," Chase said. "I can honestly say that." Bengals offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher said Lawrence is pressure testing the Bengals' offensive line. "When you have a man as big as [Lawrence], the quick twitch and the speed they're able to play with just disarms you," Pitcher said. "I don't know what you do to counteract that other than you just really focus on the technique of this interior line and you got to be really cognizant of what types of schemes you're trying to run and how often that guy's truly one-on-one."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Lions sign RB Raheem Blackshear
summary: The Lions added a running back to the roster while they wait for Jahmyr Gibbs to get on the practice field.
full_text: The Lions added a running back to the roster while they wait for Jahmyr Gibbs to get on the practice field. The NFL's daily transaction report shows that they signed Raheem Blackshear after a tryout. Wide receiver Lawrence Keys was waived with an injury designation. Blackshear played 41 games for the Panthers from 2022-2024, but did not see any regular season action last year. He ran 52 times for 203 yards and three touchdowns and saw time as a returner during his years in Carolina. The Lions also worked out running backs Clyde Edwards-Helaire, Hassan Haskins, and Kylin James on Tuesday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Browns claim DT Coziah Izzard off waivers
summary: The Browns claimed defensive tackle Coziah Izzard off waivers, the team announced Tuesday.
full_text: The Browns claimed defensive tackle Coziah Izzard off waivers, the team announced Tuesday. The Cardinals cut Izzard on Monday. In a corresponding move, the Browns waived wide receiver Aaron Anderson with an injury designation. Anderson signed with the team as an undrafted free agent on May 19. Izzard is in his first NFL season out of Penn State. He entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2025, signing with the Chiefs. Izzard has spent time on the practice squad of the Chiefs and Cardinals.
author: Charean Williams

title: Packers sign TEs McCallan Castles, Drew Biber
summary: The Packers signed tight ends McCallan Castles and Drew Biber on Tuesday, the team announced.
full_text: The Packers signed tight ends McCallan Castles and Drew Biber on Tuesday, the team announced. In corresponding moves, the Packers waived tight end RJ Maryland and waived tight end Luke Lachey with an injury designation. Castles, a first-year player out of the University of Tennessee, spent the second half of last season on the Packers’ practice squad. He signed a futures contract and was in Green Bay this offseason until the Packers waived him April 17. He entered the league with the Eagles as an undrafted free agent in 2024. Castles spent time on the Chargers' practice squad in 2024 before they waived him early in the 2025 training camp. He spent the rest of 2025 training camp with the Rams before they cut him. Biber is a rookie who played four seasons for Purdue (2021-24) and one season at the University of Minnesota (2025). Overall, he saw action in 50 games, recording 33 receptions for 271 yards and a touchdown. Last season, Biber set career highs in games played (13), receptions (18) and receiving yards (136).
author: Charean Williams

title: Panthers put DL LaBryan Ray on reserve/retired list
summary: The Panthers will be playing in the Hall of Fame Game on Thursday night, but defensive lineman LaBryan Ray won't be getting any snaps against the Cardinals.
full_text: The Panthers will be playing in the Hall of Fame Game on Thursday night, but defensive lineman LaBryan Ray won't be getting any snaps against the Cardinals. Ray won't be getting any snaps in the rest of the team's preseason games either. The Panthers announced on Tuesday that they have placed Ray on the reserve/retired list. Ray played in 46 games for the Panthers over the last three seasons. He had 73 tackles and a sack on over 1,100 defensive snaps. The Panthers also announced that they have signed wide receivers Roc Taylor and Elijah Cooks. Wideouts Gabriel Benyard and Ainias Smith were waived, which leaves Carolina with one open roster spot.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jeffery Simmons pulled out of Titans practice for throwing a punch
summary: Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons made an early exit from Titans practice on Tuesday, but it wasn't because of an injury.
full_text: Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons made an early exit from Titans practice on Tuesday, but it wasn't because of an injury. Simmons was sent off by head coach Robert Saleh for throwing a punch at right tackle JC Latham. Simmons was wrapped up with center Austin Schlottman before throwing the punch and he was taken out of the fracas by assistant defensive line coach Tanzel Smart. “Our policy is if you throw a punch you’re ejected in the game, same thing with practice,” Saleh said, via Teresa Walker of the Associated Press. “If you throw punch, you’re out of practice. But rather than going to the locker room, he went to the other field. He still got his work in. So the projected reps and the work that he would have gotten, he got in off to the side.” Saleh said that he wants the Titans to "toe a line of being aggressive and call it instigating if you want." Simmons crossed that line on Tuesday and the Titans were down a key player on their defense for the rest of the workout.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cowboys TE Princeton Fant tears ACL
summary: Cowboys tight end Princeton Fant, who was carted off from Monday's practice, will miss the season with a left knee injury.
full_text: Cowboys tight end Princeton Fant, who was carted off from Monday's practice, will miss the season with a left knee injury. Fant tore his anterior cruciate ligament and partially tore his medial collateral ligament and will undergo surgery in the next couple of weeks, head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Tuesday. Fant injured his knee when he was blocked backward into running back Israel Abanikanda during the Cowboys' first full-pads practice Monday. Fant signed with the Cowboys as an undrafted free agent out of Tennessee in 2023. He has appeared in 11 games in three seasons, playing mostly on special teams. The Cowboys also have Jake Ferguson, Brevyn Spann-Ford and Luke Schoonmaker at the position.
author: Charean Williams

title: Steelers sign WR Jakobie Kenney-James
summary: The Steelers signed wide receiver Jakobie Kenney-James, the team announced Tuesday.
full_text: '' The Steelers signed wide receiver Jakobie Kenney-James, the team announced Tuesday. In a corresponding move, the Steelers waived wide receiver Cole Burgess with an injury designation. Burgess went down with a lower-body injury earlier this week. Keeney-James was among the players who worked out for the team last week. He originally signed with the Lions as a college free agent following the 2025 draft. Kenney-James spent time with the Packers as a rookie, initially signing to the practice squad on Sept. 23 before being elevated to the active roster for the Week 18 game against Minnesota. He started one game and recorded two receptions for 15 yards. He also returned two kicks for 47 yards. Kenney-James played his final season of college football at the University of Massachusetts, where he appeared in nine games. He had 40 receptions for 603 yards and five touchdowns. He transferred to UMass from Eastern Washington and appeared in 49 collegiate games, with 111 receptions for 1,664 yards and 10 touchdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bears agree to four-year deal with OT Darnell Wright
summary: The Bears have locked up one of their key offensive players.
full_text: The Bears have locked up one of their key offensive players. Offensive tackle Darnell Wright has agreed to a four-year deal with Chicago, according to a joint report from ESPN and NFL Network. The contract is reportedly worth $116 million with $93 million guaranteed, making him one of the league's highest-paid offensive linemen. Wright, a first-round pick in 2023, was an AP second-team All-Pro in 2025. He’s started 49 games over his first three seasons. The Bears had exercised Wright’s fifth-year option in the spring, which had put him under contract through 2027. Now the team has a key pillar locked in for several years to come.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Report: Falcons fear Jalon Walker suffered torn ACL
summary: The Falcons have a serious injury concern.
full_text: The Falcons have a serious injury concern. Per a joint report from NFL Network, Atlanta fears edge rusher Jalon Walker tore his ACL during Tuesday's practice. He's set to have an MRI to confirm the injury. Walker was carted off the field on Tuesday, with players around him taking a knee as he was loaded onto the cart. The No. 15 overall pick of the 2025 draft, Walker registered 5.5 sacks with five tackles for loss, nine quarterback hits, and two forced fumbles in his 15 games as a rookie.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Micah Parsons: Don't worry about when I'm back, worry about how I'll be
summary: It remains unclear when Packers defensive end Micah Parsons will be back on the field, but he doesn't think anyone should be focused on the calendar when thinking about his return from last year's torn ACL.
full_text: It remains unclear when Packers defensive end Micah Parsons will be back on the field, but he doesn't think anyone should be focused on the calendar when thinking about his return from last year's torn ACL. Parsons is not expected to be ready to go at the start of the regular season and he called it " very realistic " that he'll be back for a Week 6 home game against the Cowboys while speaking to reporters on Tuesday. He also said that the actual date of his return is of less importance than the player he is when he does make his next appearance in the Green Bay lineup. Parsons made it clear that he's expecting to be just as disruptive to offenses as he was before the injury. "When you come out of these situations, you’re either going to be better or worse ," Parsons said, via Matt Schneidman of TheAthletic.com. "For me, I’ve done everything I possibly can to be better. People are worried about if I come back. People should worry about how I’m gonna be when I come back. That’s my mentality and how I feel, how I’m gonna approach when I’m back. People worried about the knee, they should be worried about how I'm gonna play when I get back. The anger, the frustration, the things that I'm about to let out because of how long it's been since I've played. So I think that's what people should really worry about. How great is Micah gonna be when he gets back? Not about when I get back because that's the short term.” The Packers know Parsons's long-term value to the team is greater than what a few early season games are worth, so everyone should be on board with Parsons getting as much time as needed to feel like he can be the defensive force that the Packers need him to be this season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jaxson Dart scored rushing TD in red-zone drill, threw ball at Greg Newsome's helmet
summary: Things are getting a little chippy for the Giants at The Greenbrier.
full_text: Things are getting a little chippy for the Giants at The Greenbrier. Via Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News , a rushing touchdown from quarterback Jaxson Dart during a red-zone drill resulted in Dart throwing the ball at cornerback Greg Newsome's helmet. Newsome, per Leonard, didn't appreciate the gesture. After practice, coach John Harbaugh was asked what he thought of it. " I think it’s a 15-yard penalty for taunting ," Harbaugh said. As a result, Harbaugh pushed the extra-point attempt back by 15 yards. Harbaugh added that he shouldn't have to say anything to Dart about it, because the in-game ramifications of such a maneuver are obvious.
author: Mike Florio

title: Rashawn Slater exits practice with apparent injury
summary: The Chargers may have another injury concern along their offensive line.
full_text: The Chargers may have another injury concern along their offensive line. Via multiple reporters on the scene, left tackle Rashawn Slater exited practice with an apparent injury and did not return. While he was briefly in the medical tent, he came out of it and watched the rest of practice. Trey Pipkins and Branson Taylor played left tackle in Slater’s stead for the rest of practice. While head coach Jim Harbaugh spoke to the media before practice, quarterback Justin Herbert did not seem overly concerned after the session. “He said he wanted to be out there, so I think that’s OK ,” Herbert said, via Kris Rhim of ESPN. Slater is returning from a torn patellar tendon suffered during last year’s training camp, which kept him out for the entire 2025 season. The No. 13 overall pick of the 2021 draft, Slater signed a four-year contract extension with the club prior to his injury last summer.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Patriots rookie Gabe Jacas: What happened in the past doesn't matter, I'm 100 percent now
summary: Patriots second-round pick Gabe Jacas was the final member of the 2025 draft class to sign an NFL contract, but the linebacker wasn't interested in discussing the reason why it took until camp was underway for that deal to get done.
full_text: '' Patriots second-round pick Gabe Jacas was the final member of the 2025 draft class to sign an NFL contract, but the linebacker wasn't interested in discussing the reason why it took until camp was underway for that deal to get done. Jacas did not participate in the offseason program either, but said "it doesn’t matter" why there was a prolonged delay and that he's just looking toward the future now that he is on the field with the team. Jacas had a surgical procedure on his left knee at some point in the offseason and the Patriots included an injury waiver in the rookie's contract to protect against any future issues. Jacas wasn't willing to share any details about the issue with his knee beyond saying that all is well now. “Whatever might’ve happened , I’m good now,” Jacas said, via Nicole Yang of the Boston Globe . “I’m grateful to be out here. . . . I’m fine. All that stuff is behind me. I’m 100 percent." Jacas will have to make up for the time he missed fairly quickly, but doing so well enough to make an impact on the field will make the rocky start to his Patriots run a distant memory.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jalon Walker carted off at Falcons practice
summary: The Falcons will be hoping for some positive news about linebacker Jalon Walker's condition on Tuesday afternoon.
full_text: The Falcons will be hoping for some positive news about linebacker Jalon Walker's condition on Tuesday afternoon. Walker was carted off the field during practice at training camp. Reporters at the workout said that Walker appeared to suffer a left leg injury and that other players took a knee as he was helped to the cart. Walker was a first-round pick last year and he finished his rookie season with 36 tackles, 5.5 sacks, two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery. The Falcons drafted Walker and James Pearce in the 2025 first round to bolster their pass rush. Pearce is facing a possible suspension as a result of a domestic violence arrest this offseason, so bad news on Walker could leave the Falcons without both players for the start of the season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Tyler Guyton will remain with the Cowboys' first-team at LT
summary: The Cowboys went into their offseason program with a competition between Tyler Guyton and Nate Thomas for the left tackle job.
full_text: The Cowboys went into their offseason program with a competition between Tyler Guyton and Nate Thomas for the left tackle job. The job appears about decided after one padded practice in training camp. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said at his news conference Tuesday that the competition isn't over, but Guyton is the clear leader. Thomas had been scheduled to take first-team reps in practice Tuesday. The Cowboys started camp with the left tackle spot as the only question on offense from last season with every starter returning, and Guyton was expected to win the job. The Cowboys drafted Guyton with the 29th overall pick in 2024, 204 picks before selecting Thomas. Guyton, though, has struggled with inconsistency and injuries. He has missed nine games in two seasons. In 2025, Guyton’s knee injury in training camp gave Thomas reps with the first-team offense in practice. Thomas ended up making his first four career starts in 2025, but Pro Bowl left guard Tyler Smith started the final four games at left tackle when Guyton was out with a high-ankle sprain. Guyton played primarily right tackle at the University of Oklahoma.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jordan Addison: I'm just putting in work, contract will take care of itself
summary: Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers agreed to a four-year contract extension on Tuesday and another wideout selected in the first round of the 2023 draft was asked about his own contract hopes later in the day.
full_text: Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers agreed to a four-year contract extension on Tuesday and another wideout selected in the first round of the 2023 draft was asked about his own contract hopes later in the day. The Vikings selected Jordan Addison one pick after the Ravens selected Flowers, but Addison did not make it sound like he's expecting anything to happen in the near future. "I'm being where my feet are ," Addison said. "I'm just putting in work right now, going through camp, making sure I'm becoming a better receiver and I feel like everything is going to take care of itself, work itself out." Addison has 175 catches for 2,396 yards and 22 touchdowns so far in his career and those numbers would likely be higher if not for the three-game suspension he served to start the 2025 season. They weren't helped by the team's quarterback issues either and Addison — who had his fifth year option for 2027 exercised this offseason — would benefit from either Kyler Murray or J.J. McCarthy improving the Vikings' lot on that front.
author: Josh Alper

title: Kevin Stefanski: Bijan Robinson is "beyond eager" to get back in there
summary: The Falcons got their deal done with Bijan Robinson on Tuesday, locking up the running back with a lucrative four-year contract extension.
full_text: The Falcons got their deal done with Bijan Robinson on Tuesday, locking up the running back with a lucrative four-year contract extension. Head coach Kevin Stefanski told reporters in his Tuesday press conference that the vibe between Robinson and the team remained "very amicable" as Robinson staged his hold-in while awaiting his second pro contract. "I know you guys saw the news on Bijan, obviously very excited for him, for us ," Stefanski said. "[We] just knew throughout this process that there would be a process and felt good about where we were. But, I think everybody understands how we feel about Bijan the person, Bijan the player." Robinson has not been practicing, which means he'll need a little time to get up to speed. But that shouldn't be much of an issue with over a month before Week 1. "He’s eager — beyond eager — to get out there," Stefanski said. "So, on that note, we’ll slowly get him back in there. It won’t be full go and let him go — we’ll have a plan here over the next, call it, week to ramp him up." Robinson led the league with 2,298 yards from scrimmage last season, having recorded 1,478 yards rushing and 79 catches for 820 yards.
author: Myles Simmons

title: A vindicated Aaron Rodgers primed for one last run at elusive second ring in walk-off season with Steelers
summary: Rodgers' final season is setting up to be one of his best
full_text:
LATROBE, Pa. -- Does Aaron Rodgers still have what it takes to finally capture that elusive second Super Bowl ring? For Steelers defensive back Brandin Echols , that question is downright laughable.
"Oh yeah, of course," Echols told CBS Sports following Tuesday's training camp practice. "Sometimes, he calls out stuff I'm doing, and I'm like, 'Bro, how'd you even call this out? I didn't even show an inch of what I'm gonna do!' That just shows the type of IQ he has for the game."
New Steelers running back Rico Dowdle , who previously played with Dak Prescott in Dallas, hasn't needed much time with Rodgers to come to a consensus on how good Rodgers is heading into his age-42 season.
“That’s the best quarterback I’ve stepped on a field with.” Rico Dowdle on Aaron Rodgers pic.twitter.com/qoKH41HKls
Clearly, Rodgers' teammates still see greatness in the future Hall of Fame quarterback. Their belief appears to be well warranted, as there are several reasons to believe that a special season may be in store for the Steelers and Rodgers, who has already announced that the upcoming season will be his last .
"There's no 99.9. This is 100 percent the end," Rodgers told CBS Sports NFL analyst Bryant McFadden . "I am savoring it, but it doesn't have a charged feeling to me. ... I'm not overly nostalgic or dramatic about, 'Oh this is my last August 4 practice or whatever.' There's none of that going on. I'm just enjoying my time with the guys."
"This is 100% the end." Aaron Rodgers tells @BMac_SportsTalk there is no doubt this is his final season. pic.twitter.com/OlReKuK0qh
The biggest story so far from Steelers training camp took place about 200 or so yards away from the practice field on Monday afternoon, when Rodgers went on a fiery diatribe that included challenging his critics to find another way to try to dent his armor.
"I'm pleading the Fifth 😂😂 You've gotta be kidding me" ~ @AaronRodgers12 #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/kg3y0uMxxR
Based on his comments on "The Pat McAfee Show," it's safe to say that Rodgers feels vindicated and either no longer feels the sting of past criticisms or simply doesn't care anymore. He's at peace with who he is on and off the field and the legacy that he's built across a lengthy and decorated career. Mental clarity is a valuable thing, and it's something that Rodgers appears to have in spades.
Rodgers enters his final NFL season a happily married man . He's reunited with his family after a prolonged estrangement. And based on his comments on Monday, he clearly feels that his stance on COVID -- and the handling of it -- has been justified.
From a football standpoint, Rodgers has quelled the narrative that he hasn't been a good teammate during his time in Pittsburgh. He's playing for a team that believes in his ability to lead it to the promised land, and for a coach whom he reached the mountaintop with during the crowning moment of their careers.
"That's the reason I'm back," Rodgers said when asked about reuniting with Mike McCarthy. "Last year, I wanted to play for Mike Tomlin, and I loved my experience. And when that came to an end, I thought, I don't know if I want to just like relearn an offense. You know, that's a whole process. And then Mike got hired. I said, 'Well, I know that offense. I think I can play in that offense.'"
"[Mike McCarthy is] the reason I came back." Aaron Rodgers tells @BMac_SportsTalk he is looking forward to the 2026 campaign with Mike McCarthy. 😤 pic.twitter.com/dx6LbtArJz
Rodgers also has two other things at his disposal: his legendary throwing touch and the mind of a four-time league MVP who has seen every conceivable scenario one can envision on a football field.
Unfortunately for athletes, the body often goes well before the mind does. If anything, a player's mental prime is later than their physical one. Fortunately for Rodgers, his ageless arm and razor-sharp mind have helped him overcompensate for some of the physical things one loses with age.
Aaron Rodgers throwing some 🎯s at #Steelers practice. pic.twitter.com/IQ9cz6pCU2
Rodgers is trying to become the fourth starting quarterback over 38 to win a Super Bowl, joining Tom Brady , Peyton Manning and John Elway. Manning largely leaned on his mind when he and the Broncos won Super Bowl 50. Brady still had plenty of physical gifts when he won two Super Bowls after turning 40, but he also relied greatly on his football IQ during those last championship seasons. Elway walked away at age 38 after winning back-to-back titles. Rodgers has both the physical and mental tools to join all three.
Rodgers also has the leadership qualities that will undoubtedly be needed if the Steelers are going to make a serious Super Bowl run. Clearly comfortable in his own skin, Rodgers isn't afraid to be direct with his teammates, who by all account are embracing his leadership style.
"A-Rod takes every day the same," Echols said. "High intensity, very vocal. From an offensive or defensive side, he's trying to bring out everybody's best."
Common scene at #Steelers training camp: Aaron Rodgers working with his young teammates, especially the quarterbacks. pic.twitter.com/T7YMs4bJin
Obviously, Elway, Manning and Brady were on talented teams that helped them win those Super Bowls. The Steelers are nobody's pick to win the Super Bowl, but they still have the talent to complement Rodgers.
While it was a year late, the Steelers finally upgraded their receiving corps this offseason with Michael Pittman , Dowdle (who is expected to be a key component in the passing game) and rookie Germie Bernard . Rodgers has also continued to strengthen his rapport with DK Metcalf (who continues to be Rodgers' unquestioned primary option) and tight end Pat Freiermuth . Roman Wilson , after two tumultuous seasons, has had a strong training camp and at this point has a firm hold of the starting slot position.
Rodgers also has a young, promising offensive line in front of him and the talented running back duo of Dowdle and Jaylen Warren behind him. Warren told CBS Sports that his individual goal is to run for over 1,000 yards for the first time, and he feels that Dowdle is capable of topping 1,000, too.
"Great addition for us," Warren said of Dowdle, who has run for over 1,000 yards each of the last two seasons. "He's definitely a dude. I'm excited to work him him. ... Our O-line, they've definitely built that chemistry. Everybody's on the same page."
Defensively, the Steelers don't appear to be negatively impacted by the fact that they no longer have a defensive-oriented head coach. In fact, it appears to be the opposite.
Led by new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham, the Steelers' defense made a bevy of notable plays during the first two days of padded practice. That was the case even with the absence of defensive backs Jalen Ramsey and Joey Porter Jr .
From a coaching standpoint, McCarthy has given the Steelers the revitalization that Mike Tomlin himself acknowledged might be needed when he decided to step away after 19 seasons. But while the coach might be different, the goal remains the same.
"It's different, but ultimately it's the same message," Warren said. "Everybody is trying to win the Super Bowl."
Super Bowl? For a team that hasn't won a playoff game in a decade? While that is indeed a lofty goal, it's worth noting that Manning's Broncos and Brady's Buccaneers weren't trendy Super Bowl picks. In fact, the defending champion Seahawks were not a popular choice to win it all this time a year ago. The NFL has achieved its goal of parity, and the result is that more teams than ever are capable of hoisting the Vince Lombardi Trophy.
That may be true, but it's also still true that -- in this era of passing -- you need a talented quarterback if you are going to have a chance at climbing the mountaintop. Rodgers has already done that once, and he is more than capable of doing it one more time for a franchise that is hoping to recapture its past glory.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Titans' Jeffery Simmons ejected from practice for throwing punch at JC Latham
summary: Tennessee coach Robert Saleh established boundaries for his hard-nosed defense
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans ' coaching staff ejected star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from Tuesday's practice after he threw a punch during a skirmish with right tackle JC Latham . Simmons spent the remainder of the day working on a side field with a strength coach.
Early in team drills, the offensive and defensive lines converged in a post-play tussle. Simmons and center Austin Schlottmann were initially involved in the tangle, then the former took a swing at Latham in the middle of a scrum, according to ESPN . Assistant defensive line coach Tanzel Smart stepped in and pulled Simmons out of the fight, then coach Robert Saleh stopped practice, gathered the players and held a talk to cool them down.
Simmons was the only player ejected from practice as Saleh made an example out of his crossing the line.
"Our policy is if you throw a punch, you're ejected in the game," Saleh said after practice . "Same thing with practice, if you throw a punch out at practice. But rather than go to the locker room, he went to the other fields. He still got his work in. So the projected reps and the work that he would have gotten in, he got in off to the side."
This is not the first time Simmons and Latham went after each other in training camp. The two were at the center of a fight in 2024 on the first day of full-pad practice, and while then-coach Brian Callahan said the team would not accept fighting at practice, he did not eject Simmons like his successor did on Tuesday.
"It's the second day of pads," Saleh said. "It's hot. It's muggy. You're expecting it, especially with the way the O-line and D-line get after it. It's just a reminder that we've got work to do. It's OK. I've got brothers. We fight all the time, but at the end of the day, we still take care of one another, make sure we're getting the work done we need to get."
Simmons is the face of a new-look defensive front which Saleh reconstructed ahead of his first year as the Titans' coach. He returned to the unit in 2026 on the heels of a career year in which he earned a first-team All-Pro selection and made his fourth Pro Bowl in five years.
The highly renowned tenacity Simmons brings to both the pass rush and run-stopping scheme on the interior defensive line spilled over into extracurricular activity at practice, and while Saleh does not condone the level to which his star defensive tackle raised the skirmish, he said he does approve of Simmons' competitive drive.
"Our O-line and D-lines, we want them playing with an edge," Saleh said. "We want them to toe the line. We just gotta learn how to draw the penalty, not give the penalty. We're always going to toe the line of violence. We're always going to toe the line of being aggressive. Call it instigating if you want; it's just the nature of who we're going to be. But we've gotta be disciplined enough to make sure that we always find our way back to the huddle without giving the other team freebies."
author: Carter Bahns

title: Jalon Walker injury: Falcons EDGE feared to have torn ACL in latest blow to Atlanta's defense, per report
summary: Atlanta could be down two starting edge rushers for at least part of the 2026 season
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons ' promising young defensive front might have taken a significant blow on Tuesday with an injury to second-year edge rusher Jalon Walker . The No. 15 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft is feared to have torn his ACL during the team's non-padded practice and will undergo an MRI to confirm the extent of his injury, according to ESPN/NFL Network .
Walker sustained the ailment during an 11-on-11, two-minute drill period at the Aug. 4 practice. He hit the ground in the backfield and remained there while teammates surrounded him on their knees. After evaluation from the Falcons' training staff, Walker was carted off the field and the team called off the rest of practice.
If Walker did indeed tear a ligament in his knee, he will almost certainly miss the entire 2026 season. Such an absence would come as an untimely hiccup in his young career, as he was set to enter Year 2 as an up-and-coming force off the edge with a high ceiling as a former first-round pick.
Walker appeared in 15 games as a rookie and started nine. He flashed his upside during a particularly prolific midseason run in which he accumulated four sacks in four games from Weeks 9-12. At season's end, the Georgia product had logged 36 tackles, 5.5 sacks, nine QB hits and two forced fumbles.
The splendid start to his career made Walker a projected every-week starter in Atlanta this year, so his looming absence leaves a sizable hole in the starting lineup. Samson Ebukam and Cameron Thomas are next in line and will be tasked with stepping into a larger role than expected.
Atlanta used two first-round picks last year to address its edge rusher group and appeared to hit on both of them as Walker and James Pearce Jr . delivered promising rookie campaigns. That tandem projected as a rising one-two punch that could join the ranks of the best passing-rushing tandems in the NFL this year , but the Falcons could suddenly go from boasting an enticing young unit to placing both Walker and Pearce on the bench for an extended period.
Pearce awaits a potential league-imposed suspension for the off-field trouble in which he was involved during the offseason. If the NFL determines he violated its personal conduct policy, he may open the campaign on the sidelines.
Police arrested Pearce on Feb. 7 for a domestic dispute with his ex-girlfriend, WNBA star Rickea Jackson. He was charged the following month with aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police, resisting an officer with violence to his or her person and aggravated stalking.
Pearce entered into a pre-trial intervention program that resulted in all charges being dismissed. That cleared the way for him to join the team in time for training camp. While he continues to practice with the team and figures to be ready physically for the season opener, the NFL could levy a suspension before Week 1 that would delay his season debut.
Any action that Pearce misses will dramatically hinder the Falcons' pass-rushing abilities considering the other half of the starting tandem appears poised to miss significant time, if not the entire season.
author: Carter Bahns

title: NFL training camp injuries tracker: Latest updates on Jalon Walker, Kenyon Sadiq, Coby Bryant and more
summary: Keep track of every major injury, setback, and recovery timeline across the league as teams prepare for the upcoming season
full_text:
NFL training camp is typically a time for optimism. Hope abounds that all the changes a team made during the offseason -- whether hiring a new coach, signing players in free agency, acquiring them via trade or selecting them in the draft -- will lead to a better season than the year before.
The one thing every team needs to avoid for that to happen, of course, is injuries. A major injury can derail plans for the entire year, especially if it happens to a key player. Alas, injuries happen every year, and it's important to keep track of who's hurt, when and how the injury happened, and how long they might be sidelined.
With that in mind, consider this your one-stop shop for all the injury news coming out of NFL training camps during July and August.
New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn delivered some troubling news on Tuesday, as first-round pick tight end Kenyon Sadiq is going to miss some time after "having a little setback." There's not an exact timetable for his return, although Glenn doesn't think Sadiq will miss the season opener. The rookie had offseason hernia surgery.
The No. 16 overall pick was the top tight end in his past draft, setting career highs with 51 catches for 560 yards and eight touchdowns for the Oregon Ducks last season. No FBS tight end caught more touchdowns than Sadiq. He was expected to make an immediate impact on this Jets offense, but New York does have another capable tight end in Mason Taylor.
Pearsall is expected to undergo season-ending surgery on his ongoing PCL injury that has been an issue since last season. Niners general manager John Lynch said that Pearsall is expected to make a full recovery.
James is expected to miss time after he suffered a rib fracture during Monday's practice. The 49ers have yet to offer a timeline for his possible return.
Mustapha sat out Wednesday's practice as he is dealing with a hamstring strain. Like James, Mustapha's injury occurred during Monday's practice.
Allen, who had been enjoying a strong start to his first NFL camp, was carted off the field on Saturday after colliding with Kaiir Elam on a special teams drill. ESPN later reported that test conducted on Allen revealed a shin bruise. Nothing was torn or broke, so he appears to have dodged a bullet.
Worthy suffered a shoulder injury on the same day Allen was injured. Andy Reid described the injury as a sprain and said Worthy should return to practice the following week.
During Saturday's practice, Johnson went down and was unable to put any weight on his right leg as he was aided off the field. He was also seen clutching the area around his Achilles. Despite being carted to the locker room, ESPN reports that Gardner-Johnson merely suffered a lower calf strain, so he avoided any serious injury.
Johnson, 28, was enjoying a solid start to training camp. A seven-year veteran, Johnson's NFL accolades includes a Super Bowl win with the Eagles and leading the NFL in interceptions back in 2022.
Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski that Tagovailoa is working through an injury and will the early portions of training camp. With Tagovailoa sidelined, the Falcons have signed veteran backup Cooper Rush .
Regarding fellow quarterback Michael Penix's status, Stefanski recently said that he still hasn't been cleared for full team activities. Penix is still working his way back from a torn ACL that was sustained during Week 11 of the 2025 season.
Atlanta brought its Aug. 4 practice to a close after Walker went down with a leg injury. It is feared to be a torn ACL for the second-year edge rusher. His Falcons teammates took knees and surrounded him while trainers evaluated him, and he was then carted off the field. Walker sustained the injury in an 11-on-11 two-minute drill at the Falcons' non-padded practice.
The Panthers placed Scourton on injured reserve after he suffered a torn ACL in his right knee on the first day of training camp . Scourton was reportedly in tears as he left the field, and his teammates came over to hug him as he exited.
Head coach Dave Canales said at the time that Scourton would undergo an MRI to determine the severity of the injury, and the results confirmed the second-year edge rusher had torn his ACL.
While the initial plan was for Brazzell to recover without surgery, a second opinion determined that a procedure to repair the moderate LCL tear in his left knee is the best course of action, according to The Athletic . The surgery will force Brazzell to miss his entire rookie season, which is a much longer timeline than the eight weeks that was presented in the immediate wake of his injury. The LCL tear does not appear to be related to the knee issue the third-round pick dealt with leading up to training camp.
Former first-round pick Xavier Legette reportedly went down hard on his back and head while attempting to make a catch during drills on Tuesday. After remaining on the turf for some time, the wideout was helped up and carted off the field, per WCNC .
While it doesn't appear Legette suffered a serious, season-ending injury, it was another scare for a team that has already suffered too many losses in training camp. Legette is still looking to live up to his No. 32 overall pick billing. In 15 games played last year, he caught 35 passes for 363 yards and three touchdowns.
The Saints were hit with awful news on Wednesday as it appears that Bresee suffered a season-ending ACL tear during Wednesday's practice. A former first-round pick, Bresee has quietly become one of the NFL's best defensive linemen. The Saints will now look to try to find his replacement for the upcoming season.
The 2025 first-round pick's Wednesday practice came to an abrupt end after his leg buckled . Stewart -- who played in just eight games during his rookie season -- was carted off the field shortly after sustaining the injury. According to ESPN , Stewart suffered a hyperextended knee with no ligament damage, which seems like best-case scenario given the initial reporting around the injury.
McNeill left Friday's practice with a neck injury suffered in a pile-up during 11-on-11 drills, according to the Detroit Free Press . The Lions are already shorthanded in the secondary and can scarcely use an injury up front. McNeil wasn't himself last season after returning from a torn ACL and it's not a great sign to see him banged up early in camp this year.
Brown told NFL Media that he dislocated his thumb at a Patriots practice. Brown returned to practice and caught several passes. "Thumb out of place," he said. "You keep going." This is certainly going to be an important injury to monitor.
Bryant suffered a hyperextended knee, bone bruise and small fracture during the Bears' practice on Monday and is expected to miss 8 to 10 weeks, per ESPN . It's a brutal blow for a Bears secondary that was already one of the thinner units on the team. It's also rough for Bryant, who signed a big free-agent deal with Chicago this offseason.
Benson experienced discomfort and flaring in his surgically-repaired knee, according to head coach Mike LaFleur. He was feeling better on Monday August 3, which LaFleur said was good news, and added that it's not likely to be a multi-week issue. Still, it's never a good sign when a player who had surgery experiences "discomfort" in the body part that was repaired.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Highest-paid players at every NFL position: Darnell Wright joins top earners with historic RT contract
summary: A look at the markets by position for 2026
full_text:
NFL training camps are well underway, and not only does that mean that the season is fast approaching, but the paydays are coming in bunches, too, as teams look to lock in their top players long-term.
It's no secret that the NFL is a money-making machine: from merchandise, to commercials, streaming services, to tickets and more. Money is often a big hurdle between teams and players, with contract holdouts, hold-ins and trades giving each season plenty of drama on the sidelines.
The NFL salary cap has more than doubled in the last decade-plus and now sits at over $300 million per team heading into the 2026 season. Some teams are known to be more willing to spend money, while others like to be more cautious with the paycheck.
Some players choose to take less to be on the team they want or to rebuild a solid core around them, while others demand the highest value at their position. Just who is taking home the biggest bag?
We broke down the highest-paid players by position, based on average annual value, to gauge where the market stands. All values are via Spotrac .
Patrick Mahomes agreed this offseason to terms on a revised contract that adds two years to his existing deal and makes him the highest-paid quarterback in average annual value. The three-time Super Bowl MVP and two-time NFL MVP is the first player in NFL history to sign a contract worth more than $500 million. He passed Dak Prescott , who previously held the title at $60 million per year. Followed by Mahomes and Prescott are Josh Allen , Joe Burrow , Trevor Lawrence , Jordan Love and Matthew Stafford , who all hold $55 million AAV deals, according to Spotrac.
Bijan Robinson landed his record-setting payday after holding out at Falcons training camp for roughly one week. The deal could reach up to $75 million. Robinson's $22.25 AAV topped the previous record holder, Saquon Barkley , by roughly $2 million. Robinson led the NFL in scrimmage yards (2,298) last season.
The 32-year-old went undrafted in 2017 before signing with the Baltimore Ravens . He signed with the Giants this offseason after earning Pro Bowl and second-team All-Pro honors in 2025.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba was essential to the Seahawks ' Super Bowl championship run last season and was named the NFL's Offensive Player of the Year. He had 119 receptions and 1,793 receiving yards, a league high, along with 10 touchdowns in the regular season. His breakout year came at the perfect time for Sam Darnold's offense and he has high expectations as he enters Year 4.
George Kittle is arguably the best tight end in the league right now and it shows in his contract. The seven-time Pro Bowler and two-time first-team All-Pro has spent his entire career with the 49ers . Kittle started and ended his season with injuries last year, missing five games due to a hamstring tear suffered in Week 1 and going down with an Achilles injury in their wild-card game against the Eagles . He still has goals of a Week 1 return for the 2026 season.
Laremy Tunsil was the No. 13 overall pick in 2016, selected by the Miami Dolphins . He then went to the Houston Texans before joining the Commanders in 2025. His resume includes five Pro Bowl honors and he has started all 139 games he's played in.
The Bears already picked up a fifth-year option on Wright for 2027, and they secured his future even further when they came to terms during training camp on a four-year extension . The $93 million guaranteed on that new deal is the most ever for an offensive lineman, and the $29 million per year makes Wright the highest-paid right tackle in league history.
Tyler Smith , the 2022 No. 24 overall pick, has become pivotal on the Cowboys ' line and has three Pro Bowls during his time in the league. Matthew Bergeron , taken 38th in 2023, inked his deal shortly into 2026 training camp.
Tyler Linderbaum was drafted No. 25 overall in 2022 by the Ravens, where he remained until this offseason, when he joined the Raiders . The three-time Pro Bowler took 99% of offensive snaps last season, starting all 17 games.
Will Anderson Jr . became the highest-paid non-quarterback in NFL history with his massive three-year, $150 million deal. According to Next Gen Stats, he was seventh in run-stop rate (12.6%), third in run stuffs (13) and second in pressures (85) among defenders with at least 150 run defensive snaps in 2025. His performance put him second in NFL Defensive Player of the Year voting. He was named DPOY in 2023.
Jeffery Simmons briefly held the title of highest-paid interior defensive lineman this offseason before Jalen Carter took the throne with a huge extension on the eve of the first practice of training camp. Carter's extension doesn't kick in until after the 2027 season and includes $106 million guaranteed.
Fred Warner has spent his entire career with the Niners and the team has him under contract until 2030. He is a four-time first-team All-Pro and a four-time Pro Bowler, starting all 121 regular-season and 12 playoff games he's appeared in. The defensive leader was limited to six games last season due to an ankle fracture.
For the second time in his career, Ward tops the highest-paid defensive back list after signing a two-year, $62.2 million extension that ties him to Cleveland through 2029. Ward was already signed through 2027 on a five-year, $100.5 million extension in 2022. He's a five-time Pro Bowler with 18 career interceptions.
Derwin James has played for the Chargers since the team selected him No. 17 overall in 2018. He earned his fifth Pro Bowl and fourth second-team All-Pro honor last season. He had a career-best three interceptions last season, to go with 94 combined tackles, seven passes defended, two sacks and one forced fumble.
This marks the largest deal for a kicker in league history, earned in thanks to Pro Bowls in each of his three seasons in the NFL. Aubrey went undrafted in 2022 and joined the USFL, becoming a two-time champion in the league, before heading to the Cowboys in 2023. He has made 88.2% of field goals attempted and 96.9% of attempted extra points. He has six total field goals over 60 yards, an NFL record.
Jordan Stout led the league with a net average of 44.9 yards last season and earned a Pro Bowl spot due to his 2025 performance.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Browns owner reveals the one bet he would make on his team this year and it's one that could surprisingly hit
summary: Cleveland owner Jimmy Haslam is confident his team will surpass Vegas expectations, and the easiest schedule in the NFL suggests he might be right
full_text:
It's not often that you see an NFL owner come out and offer some unsolicited gambling advice about his team, but that's exactly what Jimmy Haslam did while meeting with reporters recently.
The Browns' owner closed out the first week of training camp on Friday by meeting with the media, and during his press conference, he made it clear that he's actually very aware of Cleveland's over/under number for the 2026 season.
"I would say this, and we never do this, but I think the odds are for us to win five and a half games," Haslam said. "I'll take the over."
The NFL has a very strict policy in place when it comes to gambling on football, but there's nothing in the rule book that would prevent someone from talking about what they would bet on, and that's exactly what Haslam did here. Now, Haslam did note that he would "never" actually bet, but he seems pretty confident that the over will hit this season.
The Browns' over/under is currently slightly juiced toward the over at DraftKings:
After an offseason in which the Browns traded Myles Garrett to the Rams, Haslam isn't expecting his team to be a Super Bowl contender this year, but he does think they'll improve on their 5-12 record from last year.
"We want to be a contending playoff team in 2027," Haslam said, via The Athletic . "That doesn't mean we can't make it in '26."
When it comes to predicting the Browns' over/under for the season, Haslam pretty much had to predict the over, because it would have looked absolutely awkward if he had taken the under (Not that the Browns have ever been worried about making things awkward). That being said, Haslam could have simply NOT mentioned the Browns' win total, but he put it out there, so now, we're going to take a look at whether his prediction is realistic.
Although the Browns' roster certainly has some big question marks with the biggest one being at quarterback, this team does have one of the best defenses in the NFL -- even without Garrett -- and that might be enough to carry Cleveland to at least six wins.
One thing working in the Browns' favor this year is the fact that they have the easiest strength of schedule in the NFL. Here's why that matters: The AFC team with the easiest schedule has finished with a winning record in eight straight seasons, including last year, when the AFC champion Patriots improved from 4-13 in 2024 to 14-3 in 2025.
Having a new head coach has been a jolt of energy for several bad teams in recent years. Over the past three seasons, the AFC team with the easiest strength of schedule has improved its record by an average of 7.7 wins, and all three of those teams had a new head coach going into the season.
In 2026, the Browns will have a new head coach in Todd Monken and he'll be looking to replicate the success of those three coaches.
Another thing to like about the schedule is that the Browns are matched up against the AFC South and NFC South this year. Last year, the 49ers were in the exact same spot as the Browns: They had the easiest strength of schedule in 2025 and they also got to play both South divisions. After going 6-11 in 2024, the 49ers used their scheduling advantage to go 12-5 in 2025.
Of course, no one is going to mistake the Browns for the 49ers, but getting to play both South divisions seems to help. The last two times an entire division was matched up against both South divisions, that division produced at least three teams that finished with winning records.
This should have the Browns feeling somewhat confident that they might be able to surprise some people this year.
If the Browns are going to be good this year, the defense is likely going to have to carry the load. The defense gave up the fourth-fewest yards in the NFL last season, and although they lost Garrett, Cleveland did add both Jared Verse and Quincy Williams, so the unit likely won't take a huge step back.
Offensively, the Browns have a QB battle going on between Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson that will likely go down to the wire. If the Browns can get just average QB play, they should be able to improve on their win total from last season. The Browns' offense only topped 20 points three times in 2026, and when you can't score, that puts a lot of pressure on the defense.
One advantage for the Browns' offense this year is the hiring of Monken. The former Ravens offensive coordinator knows the AFC North well, and that knowledge alone could lead to some small improvements on the field for the offense.
Speaking of the AFC North, the Browns have won at least two division games in eight straight seasons. Basically, no matter how bad they've been over the years, they've always been able to find a few wins against their division rivals. If they can once again win two division games in 2026, that means they'd only need to win four of their 11 non-divisional games to hit the over on 5.5 wins. There were five teams in the NFL that went 4-13 or worse last season, and the Browns will face four of them this season (Raiders, Jets, Titans, Giants). This certainly feels like a schedule where the Browns can eke out six wins, so Haslam might be on to something with his betting advice.
author: John Breech

title: George Pickens' 2026 season likely to be his Cowboys swan song after Zay Flowers, Drake London contracts
summary: Pickens' market continues to rise while Dallas stares down looming contract decision with him and All-Pro DT Quinnen Williams
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys and their fan base need to treasure Pro Bowl wide receiver George Pickens while they still can because the 2026 season will likely be his last in Dallas.
While that is an incredibly gloomy thought early on in training camp, the time on the NFL calendar when hope springs eternal for all of the league's 32 teams, it's a realistic conclusion given the continual uptick in the wide receiver contracts market and what Dallas will likely choose to prioritize.
The Baltimore Ravens inked two-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Zay Flowers to a reported four-year, $140 million extension on Tuesday prior to the start of his fourth NFL season. That deal is identical to Minnesota Vikings 2022 NFL Offensive Player of the Year wide receiver Justin Jefferson's in both years and total contract value, with Jefferson earning $2 million more than Flowers in guaranteed money, $110 million to $108 million. In June, the Atlanta Falcons re-signed wide receiver Drake London , Pickens' 2022 NFL Draft classmate, to a four-year, $141.054 million extension with $99.87 million guaranteed, making him the third-highest-paid receiver in the league.
Pickens, meanwhile, is locked in on the franchise tag, which will pay him $27.298 million fully guaranteed in 2026 after the Cowboys decided not to engage with him and agent David Mulugheta in long-term contract talks this offseason. That's puzzling with Pickens fresh off producing a career year with 1,429 yards receiving and 9 receiving touchdowns on 93 catches. Ranking third in the entire league in receiving yards earned the 25-year-old the first Pro Bowl and All-Pro selections (second team) of his career. Neither Flowers nor London has registered as gaudy a receiving yards total as Pickens did last season.
He leads the trio in career receiving yards (4,270) and career yards per reception average (16.0), while London has the edge in career receptions (309) and a narrow lead in career receiving touchdowns (22). Pickens' 21 career receiving touchdowns are one behind his 2022 NFL Draft classmate. Translation: Pickens can now demand more money than both Flowers and London on a long-term deal with a straight face. That's a significant problem for Dallas for a multitude of reasons, despite Jerry Jones feeling like Pickens having to prove it again on the franchise tag is a win-win situation for both parties.
"This can be a very win-win thing that we've done here: us, George and George being on the team," Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones said at Dallas' opening training camp press conference . "Make no mistake about it: George could be a Cowboy for the rest of his career, and that would be a long time. Make no mistake about it. This [the franchise tag] just fit for us, and thank goodness it fit for him, and we got it done."
The love between Pickens and Jones is mutual ... until the two sides have to sit down at the negotiating table again next offseason.
"Super excited. I'm always super happy when someone thinks highly of me, so shout out to Jerry," Pickens said on July 30, via The Athletic .
Receiving yards per reception
Waiting to extend Pickens, rather than doing so when trading for him as a somewhat distressed asset in May of 2025, has come back to bite them. The talent was always there, and in 2025, Pickens showed how prolific he can be with a quarterback of Dak Prescott's caliber, rather than the mediocre carousel of passers Pittsburgh paraded through its franchise from 2022 to 2024.
Now, the Cowboys have two major contractual decisions to make that will determine Pickens' future in Dallas: paying Pickens vs. paying All-Pro wide receiver CeeDee Lamb, and paying Pickens vs. paying All-Pro defensive tackle Quinnen Williams . Playing the waiting game led Dallas to re-sign their present-day No. 88 to a four-year, $136 million extension with $82 million guaranteed back in 2024. Delaying those negotiations in tandem with Pickens puts the Cowboys in a position where they have to choose between paying Lamb or Pickens, and Dallas will end up choosing Lamb. Dallas puts a premium on homegrown players they choose to extend, and Lamb has been everything the Cowboys have hoped for: he's developed into an All-Pro, five-time Pro Bowler who is also a team captain.
As for the Williams vs. Pickens debate, it seems as though the Jones family has already made their choice. They're choosing to prioritize the All-Pro anchor of their defense, whom they traded for, in an effort to make people forget about how they traded away All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers .
"Absolutely, we're very open to that," Cowboys COO Stephen Jones said at Dallas' opening training camp press conference when asked about extending Williams. "We want Quinnen here for the long haul. Obviously, we've got a lot of resources tied up in him. He knows what we think about him. We've had some discussions with the agent about how to go about the process.
"Certainly he's [Williams] one of the best in the business, and we know kind of what that market is. Obviously, it evolves and changes with each new deal, which is the case at any position. Certainly, he's at the top of the list in terms of the people that we want to keep around here long term, and there's other players on the roster that we may take a look at as well as we move forward."
Next offseason, the Cowboys will likely end up either tagging and trading Pickens or allowing him to walk in free agency in exchange for a third-round compensatory draft pick, thanks to their inability to get ahead of the fast-evolving wide receiver market. Either outcome is deflating because Dallas successfully identified a high-level talent who could reach new heights within their high-powered offensive ecosystem. Choosing to procrastinate on addressing his long-term contractual future will likely lead to him ending up like Parsons: another All-Pro-caliber talent Dallas developed, going on to crush it with another NFL team for the long haul.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Renner's 2027 NFL Draft scouting series: Ranking top 10 linebackers, with Clemson's Sammy Brown leading way
summary: Sammy Brown ticks every box you want to see for the position at a high level
full_text:
The 2027 linebacker draft class comes with some injury and role concerns, but make no mistake there's a lot of talent to be had at the position. Cutting this one down to only 10 prospects was not an easy task as there were nearly a half-dozen prospects that I could have feasibly slotted into the back of this top 10.
The strength of the class is obviously the rising juniors, but there are also a couple of fourth-year linebackers in this top 10 who would have been in the league already if it weren't for injuries suffered last season. The No. 1 prospect in the class I don't see changing, though, as he could play his way into a top half of Round 1 selection.
Positional rankings: IOL • S • LB • DT • TE • OT • RB • CB • EDGE • WR • QB
Note: ⭐️ represents each player's 247Sports star rating as a high school recruit
Brown has all the makings of a first-round linebacker and if it weren't for the loaded 2027 class he could end up in the top 10. Brown started by the end of his true freshman season in 2023 and became an All-ACC selection as a sophomore. He ticks every box you want to see for the position at a high level. He's fast, agile, strong, physical, and the surest tackler in the class. To have such a well-rounded game as a true sophomore on tape is a rarity.
Play of the Day No. 270: Sophomore linebacker Sammy Brown gets across the line of scrimmage before the ball leaves the quarterback's hands (Clemson vs. Georgia Tech, 2025). #POTD pic.twitter.com/LugVKGKSVK
His athletic background is the stuff of legend. Alongside linebacker in high school he also rushed for 2,289 yards at running back and averaged 44.5 yards per attempt as a punter. His freshman year he won the Georgia class 1A 400m state championship (50.5 seconds) and he has a 100m PR of 10.7. He was also a two-time state champion wrestler. That's the kind of athletic profile that's very easy to bet on.
To get by as a sub-220 pound linebacker you better be both a high-end athlete as well as overtly physical and Atkins fits both descriptions.
