title: Tee Higgins and Dexter Lawrence snubbed from NFL Top 100 Players ranking
summary: When I was in middle school and high school, my springs and summers were spent anticipating the weekly episodes of the NFL Top 100 Players going into the upcoming season. Ten players per week were revealed on NFL Network, and there were reaction shows right after each episode. The list was voted exclusively by the […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - JULY 29: Tee Higgins #5 of the Cincinnati Bengals performs during the Cincinnati Bengals Training Camp at Kettering Health Practice Fields on July 29, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images When I was in middle school and high school, my springs and summers were spent anticipating the weekly episodes of the NFL Top 100 Players going into the upcoming season. Ten players per week were revealed on NFL Network, and there were reaction shows right after each episode. The list was voted exclusively by the players, and they were usually spot on with the rankings every year. But this year, the list is drawing major criticism on Twitter. Lamar Jackson is ranked No. 69. Okay, yes, Jackson missed four games last year and wasn’t as dynamic as he was in 2023 or 2024, but the players are saying there are 68 players better than Jackson? Going into this season, they think there are nearly 70 players better than two-time NFL MVP Lamar Jackson? Look, availability is the best ability, and players do pay attention to production. A player’s whole career, though, should be taken into account when compiling this annual list. From a Bengals’ perspective, Joe Burrow checked in at No. 44 last week. So, there are 43 players better than Joe Burrow? Yeah, sure. But the ridiculousness doesn’t stop there. Tee Higgins and Dexter Lawrence didn’t even make the list. They were ranked just outside the top 100, as revealed early this week. Players who just missed the NFL Top 100… 110: Tyler Warren 109: Tee Higgins 108: Brian Branch 107: Devon Witherspoon 106: Jameson Williams 105: Dexter Lawrence 104: Chris Lindstrom 103: CJ Stroud 102: Lane Johnson 101: Mike Evans pic.twitter.com/bjfSYLDg0V — NFL (@NFL) August 3, 2026 Hold on… so the players who voted think there are 100 players better than BOTH Higgins and Lawrence? Humor me, a little bit. Tee Higgins absolutely justified the Bengals paying him with a terrific 2025 season. All he did, playing with three different starting quarterbacks, was score 11 receiving touchdowns on 59 receptions for 846 yards. Lawrence may have only had a half-sack last season. But as we have talked about at length this offseason, a change of scenery could be exactly what he needs to get back to his beast-like production from the middle of the defensive line. Let’s not forget he had nine sacks in 2024, and that was only in 12 games. Look, players and coaches know the NFL game better than anybody. That’s why the NFL Top 100 Players list used to matter significantly. It was a refreshing concept to have the players be the only ones voting. But this year, the list is coming into serious question and is being heavily criticized. For the players who voted, thinking there are 100 better players than Tee Higgins and Dexter Lawrence is lunacy. And 43 better players than Joe Burrow? Come on.

title: Bengals training camp Day 6 News and discussion
summary: The news from Monday’s training camp session was once again about the Cincinnati Bengals’ defense making plays. After an offseason of additions, this is music to fans’ ears. As the pads came on, the impact of free agent signing Jonathan Allen and the blockbuster trade for Dexter Lawrence II was felt all over the practice […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - JULY 29: Joe Burrow #9 of the Cincinnati Bengals performs during the Cincinnati Bengals Training Camp at Kettering Health Practice Fields on July 29, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The news from Monday’s training camp session was once again about the Cincinnati Bengals’ defense making plays. After an offseason of additions, this is music to fans’ ears. As the pads came on, the impact of free agent signing Jonathan Allen and the blockbuster trade for Dexter Lawrence II was felt all over the practice fields outside of Paycor Stadium. While the defense’s performance has been applauded, some are wondering if concern for the offense is warranted. Reports state that Zac Taylor’s offense has been operating from under center more than we’ve seen in any training camp, but the results seem mixed. While the run game had success Monday, the defense appeared to win more of the passing situations. We’re in early August, so it isn’t time to panic about the offense, but coming out of training camp with confidence and momentum could do wonders for a defense that ranked at or near the bottom of the NFL in 2025.Bengals News Dexter Lawrence making instant impact at Bengals camp: ‘Honestly, he’s been terrorizing practice’ “A maligned Bengals defense loaded up on offseason upgrades to the tune of a practice group that offensive players say is more intense and competitive than Cincinnati’s defense flashed last training camp.“ Could one player make that big of a difference on a defense? It appears that it could. Add that to the other offseason additions, and it is easy to see why the offense can see a difference in the 2026 defense as training camp ramps up. Joe Burrow, Bengals find camaraderie on unusual battlefield “Cincinnati’s first week of training camp has featured a few spirited practices, a noted practice scuffle and an intense edge from a team sick of missing the playoffs. But as it has looked to put the rest of the AFC North in check in 2026, the first days of the season have also featured a chessboard.“ Plenty of work takes place on the field during training camp, but connections are made in the locker room just as much, if not more. Players spending tons of time with one another and finding ways to connect beyond the game are crucial. This year, the thing that is bringing them together appears to be a chessboard. Training Camp Report | A Dax Hill Vignette As Bengals Put On The Pads “I feel like we can play a lot faster, be more confident and play faster knowing the ball has to come out. Simple as that,” Monday was reportedly a great day for Dax Hill. With all the talk about DJ Turner II’s contract, Hill is entering a contract year as well. Hill has battled injuries and played several different positions in his time in Cincinnati, but that experience and versatility were on full display for the first day in pads. Bengals experience false alarm in first padded practice of training camp, Joe Burrow and the offense struggle in specific area “The 25 year-old is eligible for a big-time payday before the regular season begins, which is when Cincinnati traditionally finalize its biggest internal contracts. He’s been completely locked in despite the potential distraction and it’s great to see him push through what appeared to be a cramp.” A scare at training camp to say the least. For DJ Turner II, it comes while contract negotiations are presumably going on behind the scenes. Thankfully, Hill was able to get back on the field quickly. Meanwhile, the Bengals’ offense struggled in an area it would really benefit them to succeed at.

title: Browns to add trio to Legends Club in 2026
summary: The Cleveland Browns Legends will grow by three members this fall when the franchise inducts Alex Mack, Brian Brennan, and Lou Rymkus into the club prior to the home opener on September 27. Established in 2001, the Legends program honors the men who have contributed to the success of an organization with eight professional championships […]
full_text: New York Jets cornerback Carl Howard is called for Pass Interference against Browns wide receiver Brian Brennan during the Browns 23-20 double overtime victory over the New York Jets in the 1986 AFC Divisional Playoff Game on January 3, 1987 at Cleveland Municipal Stadium in Cleveland, Ohio. The result was a 25-yard penalty that helped set up the game tying field goal with 0:07 seconds remaining in regulation time. (Photo by Dennis Collins/Getty Images) The Cleveland Browns Legends will grow by three members this fall when the franchise inducts Alex Mack, Brian Brennan, and Lou Rymkus into the club prior to the home opener on September 27. Established in 2001, the Legends program honors the men who have contributed to the success of an organization with eight professional championships and 18 members of the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Rymkus was a member of head coach Paul Brown’s inaugural team in the All-American Football Conference in 1946. During his six seasons with the Browns, Rymkus was part of a team that played in six league title games, winning five of them, including the 1950 NFL Championship in their first year in the league. You can see Rymkus, No. 44, in action in this highlight film from the 1950 Championship Game: He played in 76 games for the Browns, earning an All-Pro Second Team selection in 1948 as the Browns finished a perfect 14-0 season, and was the starting right tackle in 1950 as the Browns defeated the Los Angeles Rams, 30-28, in the league title game. Rymkus retired after the 1951 season and passed away in 1998 at the age of 78. A first-round selection by the Browns in 2009, Mack spent seven seasons in Cleveland and started in every game he played, including 85 consecutive games at the beginning of his career. He is one of just six players to make at least 100 starts for the Browns since 1999. Mack was the anchor of a dominant offensive line in Cleveland that included Pro Football Hall-of-Famer Joe Thomas and the recently retired Joel Bitonio – two other players who also played in 100-plus games for the Browns. A three-time Pro Bowl selection with the Browns, the most in franchise history for a center, Mack was also named to the Hall of Fame’s All-2010s team. Mack closed out his 13-year career with the Atlanta Falcons (2016 to 2020) and the San Francisco 49ers (2021), when he picked up his seventh Pro Bowl selection. Brennan was a fourth-round selection by the Browns in the 1984 NFL Draft and went on to be a fan favorite as the Browns made three trips to the AFC Championship Game during his eight years in Cleveland. He played eight years with the Browns and is currently fifth on the franchise’s all-time list for receptions (315), ninth in receiving yards (4,148), and tied for 15th in receiving touchdowns (19). Brennan’s best season was in 1986, when he led the team in receptions (55), receiving yards (838), and receiving touchdowns (6) as the Browns advanced to the AFC Championship Game after a 12-4 season. Brennan split time between the Cincinnati Bengals and then-San Diego Chargers in 1992 before retiring.

title: Cleveland Browns Training Camp Recap: Day 6 – Live in Berea
summary: Day 6 of Cleveland Browns training camp took place Tuesday, August 4. I was in attendance, so here is a mixture of my personal report of the experience, and the usual aggregated media notes. Cleveland Browns Training Camp Report – Day 6 (8/4/26) 1. Live from Berea: I made my annual trip to Berea, Ohio […]
full_text: Day 6 of Cleveland Browns training camp took place Tuesday, August 4. I was in attendance, so here is a mixture of my personal report of the experience, and the usual aggregated media notes. Cleveland Browns Training Camp Report – Day 6 (8/4/26) 1. Live from Berea: I made my annual trip to Berea, Ohio on Tuesday, the third practice date open to fans, to watch Cleveland Browns training camp in person. My primary reason for going to camp each year is to enjoy the fan atmosphere at camp, as opposed to paying attention to practice itself (because for the most part, I can still summarize the big plays from all the other members of the media). My video recap of training camp (about a half hour long) can be found here . 2. Construction of District 46 Taking Shape: In the image comparison below, if you roll over the slider, the image with grass was from last year (2025), and the image with construction is from today (2026). Signs on the fence say that it will be completed by Summer 2027, so this time next year, I’d expect to be able to give a walking tour of the finished area. We’ve seen renderings of the area before, but here was one of the banners on the fence. The middle of the picture would be looking down Pearl Street. The finished product is supposed to have a community field for youth, high school, and adults, a hotel, a sports medicine facility by University Hospitals, apartments, 30,000 square footage of retail, and a parking garage. Considering the mockup shows several surface lots, which already seem completed in large part, I’m not sure if a garage is still in the works. I could not go down Pearl Street, because security was enforcing no pedestrians and were only waving members of the media through. That is presumably for construction purposes — I’m sure next year, anyone will be able to walk down the area. Unfortunately, they also got rid of the tiny neighborhood park where I would park my bicycle all this years when going to camp. 3. Making My Way Inside: After checking out that initial construction, I made the regular journey down Third Street and then Beech Street, seeing houses sell parking spaces for $20 and a few houses having vendor stands in their yards. Gates opened at 12:30 pm, with practice set to start at 1:30 pm. I arrived closer to 1:00 pm, so I knew I wasn’t going to be one of the first 500 fans to receive the giveaway (a Browns hat). This year, the Browns added a long set of bleachers opposite the field that has the tall grandstand bleachers, which means regardless of which field the team is practicing on, there should be ample seating space for everyone in attendance. The theme of the day was Superhero Day. Brownie the Elf had a Superman cape, and the dog mascot (which I don’t remember seeing before) looked like Iron Man. I also saw the Puppy Pound, and they had a mock field of what a portion of the new stadium will look like in Brookpark. Below is a general shot of practice from the Grandstand Bleachers. You can see the construction taking place in the background. In the gallery below, a zoomed in shot shows the University Hospitals building being constructed. In front of that, but within the Browns fields, are the new bleachers along that side with plenty of seating. 4. Heavy on the Runs Early: When it’s training camp time, fans look forward to the passing plays and how the quarterbacks are throwing. In the early part of team drills, though, it seemed like 80% of the calls were run plays. That didn’t stop the defense from being fired up with a handful of stops in the backfield: The #Browns defense comes up with an early run stop, and were fired up about it. pic.twitter.com/aDK6Zacrg2 — Dawgs By Nature (@DawgsByNature) August 4, 2026 It looked like a defense had a handle on things, and Zac Jackson agreed with that: The defense is dominating the early part of practice. The offense is mixing in some different line combinations but nobody’s keeping the defensive line out of the backfield. — Zac Jackson (@AkronJackson) August 4, 2026 5. Rest Day for Concepcion: Before practice, head coach Todd Monken said that WR KC Concepcion was fine and just a little sore after he went down at the end of practice yesterday. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Training camp is all about evaluation for teams, especially the Cleveland Browns, who are trying to decide who their starting quarterback will be . Whether it is underrated players , impressive NFL draft picks , or the bottom of the roster, Browns GM Andrew Berry and HC Todd Monken have a lot of people to keep their eyes on. Interestingly, Monken noted that he isn’t fully evaluating the quarterbacks right now due to the install process the team is going through . Other players, on the other hand, are having decisions made after evaluation. On Monday, Cleveland waived UDFA RB TJ Harden to make room for DT Travis Bell . On Tuesday, the Browns waived OT Jack Conley to make room for signing former Seattle Seahawks CB Tyler Hall . An undrafted free agent in 2020, Hall has played for four teams, including one game last season for the Super Bowl champions. With the Las Vegas Raiders, Hall had his most playing time in 2022 and 2023 when he combined to play 18 games with six starts. All but six of his defensive snaps came during those two seasons, while he has also contributed 253 snaps on special teams. Conley was an undrafted free agent in 2025 and spent time on three practice squads, including the Browns, last season, but did not see any regular-season action.

title: Browns roster 2026: Dillon Gabriel, Quincy Williams, Emmanuel McNeil-Warren are underrated
summary: Okay, so. We don’t need to torture avid Cleveland Browns fans with the quarterback jokes, because they’ve all been told. We don’t need to bag on Deshaun Watson or Jimmy Haslam, as much as those two individuals have presented legit reasons for mockery and scorn. And we don’t really need to go over all the […]
full_text: Okay, so. We don’t need to torture avid Cleveland Browns fans with the quarterback jokes , because they’ve all been told. We don’t need to bag on Deshaun Watson or Jimmy Haslam, as much as those two individuals have presented legit reasons for mockery and scorn. And we don’t really need to go over all the changes that happened with the coaching staff per se — everyone visiting this fine site likely already knows that Kevin Stefanski was replaced by Todd Monken as head coach and offensive shot-caller, while Jim Schwartz was replaced by Mike Rutenberg as the man in charge of the defense. Instead, let’s dive into reasons for optimism that have very little to do with the quarterback thing because we’ll go there in a minute. The 2026 Browns can benefit from EVP/general manager Andrew Berry’s recent personnel moves, including a 2025 draft that appears to be long-term great. The defense under Schwartz was generally anywhere from pretty good to really good, and outside of Myles Garrett, most of the key pieces are returning. It’s not as if Jared Verse, who came to Cleveland in the Garrett trade, is chopped liver, either — he’s just not a lead-pipe first-ballot Hall of Famer lock like No. 95. At least not yet. The 2026 draft brought two estimable weapons in receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston, and the offensive line underwent a neat transformation this offseason with first-round tackle Spencer Fano and free agents Zion Johnson, Elgton Jenkins, and Tytus Howard. 2025 Hidden Gem Teven Jenkins announced his presence with authority last season, so the front five should be very solid over time. Rookie running back Quinshon Judkins was an absolute boss when healthy. Basically, the 2026 Browns appear to be one of those teams that are just a quarterback away from contention. Which is a bit like saying that you’re one Eddie Van Halen away from being Van Halen, but one does the best one can with what one has. Wherever the Browns are headed this season, they’ll need the best possible from everyone on the roster — not just the big names. To that end, I’ve identified three Hidden Gems — one underrated veteran, one underrated free agent, and one underrated draft pick. And I’m sure the underrated veteran won’t inspire some agita in the comments. All I ask is that you hear me out on this one. Underrated veteran: QB Dillon Gabriel The Browns should not expect top-tier quarterback play in the 2026 season. We’re pretty sure about that. Once you’ve lowered the bar accordingly in that regard, what’s the next most crucial thing for the game’s most important position? For the Browns, situational consistency could be it. And that’s why Dillon Gabriel could be the team’s best option this season . You can always share your Browns-related thoughts, as JohnW81 did, in DBN’s Feed by clicking here! It started in 2024, when Gabriel was Bo Nix’s replacement at Oregon. Overall in that season, Gabriel completed 326 of 451 passes for 3,854 yards, 30 touchdowns, six interceptions, and a passer rating of 114.6. Good numbers, but it’s how Gabriel got to those numbers that impressed me. When under pressure: 56 of 104 for 892 yards, eight touchdowns, one interception, and a passer rating of 104.3. When blitzed: 103 of 142 for 1,286 yards, 15 touchdowns, one interception, and a passer rating of 132.5. On passes of 20+ air yards: 27 of 49 for 960 yards, eight touchdowns, one interception, and a passer rating of 131.9. Throwing from the pocket: 275 of 361 for 3,137 yards, 22 touchdowns, three interceptions, and a passer rating of 118.6. Throwing outside the pocket: 51 of 86 for 720 yards, eight touchdowns, three interceptions, and a passer rating of 102.9. Gabriel had to wait for his shots with the Browns in 2025, but when he got them, he did deliver. Overall, he completed 110 of 185 passes for 937 yards, seven touchdowns, two interceptions, and a passer rating of 80.8. Again, it was how Gabriel got to those numbers that stood out in a quarterback room that couldn’t get out of its own way most of the time. When under pressure: 32 of 63 for 320 yards, four touchdowns, one interception, and a passer rating of 80.1. When blitzed: 37 of 63 for 313 yards, two touchdowns, one interception, and a passer rating of 75.7. On passes of 20+ air yards: 2 of 8 for 44 yards, one touchdown, one interception, and a passer rating of 50.0 (okay, this needs some improvement). Throwing from the pocket: 97 of 157 for 767 yards, six touchdowns, one interception, and a passer rating of 84.0. Throwing outside the pocket: 13 of 28 for 170 yards, one touchdown, one interception, and a passer rating of 63.1. Does this bring to mind Tua Tagovailoa as a point guard-style quarterback who’s pretty good at distributing the ball all over the place, as long as you don’t ask him to scald defenses with deep balls, and rely too much on functional mobility? Before you laugh at any Tua comps, think about how much Tagovailoa at his best would have presented a marked improvement over what Shedeur Sanders or Joe Flacco did with the Browns last season, and certainly what Deshaun Watson would have forced us to watch had he been healthy. It’s not that Dillon Gabriel is the guy to break the Browns’ ridiculous quarterback curse. For the 2026 season, that’s not the point. The point is that if you ask Gabriel to limit his deeper shots to the intermediate level (on throws of 10-19 yards last season, he completed 19 of 44 for 305 yards, four touchdowns, no interceptions, and a passer rating of 97.3), and let him cook under center ( where he did see a relatively nice uptick in EPA/Play )… well, maybe the Browns could make enough of that to avoid stranding their defense again, and actually win some ballgames in successive order. explain to my why and how dillon gabriel isn't the browns' best quarterback yes, i know the bar is buried underground pic.twitter.com/1iu6Rvn41g — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) August 1, 2026 Underrated free agent: LB Quincy Williams New coaches love to bring players with whom they’re familiar to their new stops, and new Browns defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg happily brought linebacker Quincy Williams to Cleveland once he had signed on as Jim Schwartz’s replacement. Williams, the brother of former New York Jets and current Dallas Cowboys interior defensive lineman Quinnen Williams, was selected in the third round of the 2019 draft by the Jacksonville Jaguars out of Murray State, and Rutenberg was the Jags’ assistant linebackers coach at the time. When Rutenberg became the Jets’ linebackers coach in 2021, he brought Williams onto the roster after Williams failed to make final cuts with Jacksonville in August of that year. This reunion should not come as a surprise. “That’s my dog. He’s like my brother,” Williams said of Rutenberg once Williams had signed his two-year, $13 million contract with $9.5 million guaranteed. “First thing before we talk about football, the biggest thing is Rudy cares about the heart. What I do off the field affects what I do on the field. So, he wanted to tackle both things as far as what I do on the field, so I can show up as myself — show up as this personality always smiling as me, show up every single day at work like that. So, he cares about that a lot. And then on the field, as long as we take care off the field, on the field should be easy. He taught me every single thing I know as far as the linebacker positions in the league. He was with me the two teams I’ve been on, so we have a good relationship.” Williams has never been what you would call a star in coverage, but when it comes to facing forward, blowing up run fits, and going after the quarterback, he’s got it all on point. Last season for a Jets defense that was generally quite abysmal, Williams racked up four sacks, 12 pressures, eight tackles for loss, 61 solo tackles, and 42 stops. For a Browns defense that will be looking to place pressure players around Jared Verse as it once tried to do for Myles Garrett, Williams’ blitz…

summary: Normally, when training camp starts in the NFL, we see the end of ranking season. Throughout the offseason, we covered all sorts of Cleveland Browns-related rankings. (Photo by Julio Aguilar/Getty Images) | Getty Images Normally, when training camp starts in the NFL, we see the end of ranking season. Throughout the offseason, we covered all sorts of Cleveland Browns-related rankings. Whether it was multiple power rankings , 2026 NFL draft grades/rankings , where stars like Carson Schwesinger , Denzel Ward , Harold Fannin Jr. , and Quinshon Judkins were ranked among their positions, or where the Browns young core was placed among the rest of the league , ranking season was vast but seemed mostly over. With training camp in full swing, one more set of rankings, tiers really, is now available. As we covered, Mike Sando’s QB tiers do not speak highly of QBs Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson . There is more hope connected to Sanders from the 50 coaches and executives, but he is also ranked at the bottom of the list of 35 quarterbacks. Given Cleveland’s history, it is interesting to note that two former Browns quarterbacks also made the list , but not former playoff QB Joe Flacco . Sando’s tiers have Baker Mayfield tied with Sam Darnold for 14th overall in the second tier. As Mayfield looks to enter free agency , his career has been an interesting up-and-down roller coaster with another season to prove he is worthy of a top-tier contract. Fitting squarely between Watson and Sanders in the rankings is former Cleveland QB Jacoby Brissett . The Arizona Cardinals starter heading into the 2026 season, Brissett negotiated a raise on his contract this offseason but is still ranked near the bottom of the veteran starters in the NFL. Joining Watson, Sanders, and Brissett in the bottom five are two recent early first-round picks: Michael Penix Jr. (32) and JJ McCarthy (34). Are you surprised at any of the rankings listed above? Did you expect Mayfield and/or Brissett to be higher on the list? Does Penix and McCarthy being ranked so low give you even more concern about drafting a quarterback high in the future? summary: Is the above comment about Cleveland Browns QB Shedeur Sanders a strong one to title this piece? Of course it is. Is it accurate? At least it is what one defensive coordinator believes. The Browns QB competition is off and running. All we know, according to HC Todd Monken, is that a lot of things […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - APRIL 21: Deshaun Watson #4, Shedeur Sanders #2 and Dillon Gabriel #8 of the Cleveland Browns run a drill during a voluntary veteran minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on April 21, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Is the above comment about Cleveland Browns QB Shedeur Sanders a strong one to title this piece? Of course it is. Is it accurate? At least it is what one defensive coordinator believes. The Browns QB competition is off and running. All we know, according to HC Todd Monken, is that a lot of things still have to be installed in Week 2’s schedule and QB Dillon Gabriel has earned more reps . Day 5 was a lot like the previous days at Cleveland’s training camp , with a few exciting plays and a lot of concern about the quarterback play . From the outside looking in, the Browns quarterback room does not have a lot of believers. In Mike Sando’s annual QB tiers article , with 50 executives and coaches ranking 35 veteran quarterbacks, Deshaun Watson was ranked 31st, with Sanders a few slots behind at 35th, last overall. Both were in the lowest tier of the rankings. The comment that jumped out about Watson was about as negative as the one on Sanders that we titled this piece with: “I don’t think he can come back,” an offensive coach said. “You do not all of a sudden get drive and desire and processing skills. He showed he had none of that with what he put on film. He’s a 5 (lowest tier ranking) at this point.” Important to note that one voter believes so much in Monken that he put Watson in Tier 2, at least that is the assumption Sando noted. The Sanders write-up is a bit longer for NY Times subscribers, but is led by the above quote from a defensive coordinator. It wasn’t all negative, however, as there are notes of hope: “If Shedeur has really invested in himself to be a professional quarterback, studying the playbook and knowing his assignments and being able to get the offense in and out of the huddle at an efficient clip, which he could not do last year, then there might be some upside,” the voter said. With one head coach actually adding praise, not just hope: “I thought he was all right, better than expected,” this coach said. “They did a good job with him of making the game simple. And I thought Shedeur played with a chip on his shoulder.” In the end, the rankings are about what the quarterbacks have done. Now, under Monken with a new offensive system, line, and set of weapons, Watson and Sanders have a chance to change the narrative about their talents. If not, 17 weeks of good sleep are coming for different defensive coordinators. What do you think about the quotes related to Watson and Sanders? Do you think they are fair or go over the top? title: Cowboys news: Kenny Clark, Quinnen Williams making an impression
summary: Tyler Smith on facing ‘top tier’ DTs in practice, position clarity and more – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Tyler Smith has enjoyed the early training camp battles with Quinnen Williams. “I feel like things are going well,” [Tyler] Smith said. “Obviously, putting on the pads is just getting back into the physicality that the football season […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - JULY 30: Quinnen Williams #92 of the Dallas Cowboys in a defensive stance during training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields on July 30, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images Tyler Smith on facing ‘top tier’ DTs in practice, position clarity and more – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Tyler Smith has enjoyed the early training camp battles with Quinnen Williams. “I feel like things are going well,” [Tyler] Smith said. “Obviously, putting on the pads is just getting back into the physicality that the football season entails, but I feel like we’re off to a great start. Obviously, there are things to clean up, every day is not perfect, but I think we’re building towards what we’re trying to be.” That doesn’t mean it’s been easy. Facing him on the other side of the line now are Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark, two veterans who have won Pro Bowls in their career and weren’t lining up across from Smith at camp last year. They did see each other in practice during the season, but battling in Oxnard is different. “I feel like where we were at last year, I didn’t feel like we had as many live reps,” Smith said of facing Williams and Clark. “But definitely getting the training camp experience has definitely been better. I feel like it’s a whole different brand of physicality. We get way more good on good reps than we do during the season, because there’s not as much load management there. I feel like it’s really great work.” Smith’s battles with Williams have been the ones that have drawn a lot of attention from on-lookers, as the pair are both among the best players at their position. From Smith’s perspective, the two are only getting better by playing one another. “I think it’s great for me and great for him as a player,” Smith said. “I think just being able to go against somebody every day that’s going to push you to be your best and like, there is going to be times when you win. There’s going to be times when you lose. But ultimately what are you learning form that rep? What are you learning from those experiences? And that’s something even in year five, and he’s [year eight], that’s something that we’re both learning and both going through.” ‘Bash Brothers’ Quinnen Williams, Kenny Clark are setting the tone at Cowboys training camp – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News The Dallas Cowboys might have the best defensive tackle duo in the NFL. The first practice of training camp is not supposed to be physical. League rules even try to limit the physicality when the pads come on, let alone when they aren’t worn early. It’s hard to limit the inherent physicality of defensive tackles like Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark, however. Just ask starting center Cooper Beebe. “The first couple of days, when you go against those dudes and, boom, you get a long arm to the chest with no pads, it definitely left some bruises for sure,” Beebe said. Bruises will heal, but the benefits of working with two defensive tackles like Williams and Clark — the Bash Brothers for this Cowboys defensive line — should sustain. At least the Cowboys hope so. The Cowboys have trumpeted the importance of Williams and Clark — two additions that weren’t here at training camp last year — to the team’s defense. The two have provided added benefits for the team’s offense, as well. Especially on the interior. “They’re heavy in the middle,” Cowboys left guard Tyler Smith said, “and you know when you go against them you have to come with your business.” That’s been evident in the first five days of practice. That’s especially true when you compare it to years past. Last year, the Cowboys had a defensive tackle group of former first-round pick Mazi Smith, veteran Solomon Thomas, Perrion Winfrey — a spring league standout who ultimately made the team — seventh-round pick Jay Toia and Osa Odighizuwa. Only Toia remains on the roster. This year, the starting offensive line has mostly faced Williams, Clark, free agent acquisition Otito Ogbonnia and veteran Jonathan Bullard. Two Cowboys starters limited in Tuesday’s practice; Ezeiruaku ejected for punch – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram The hype around Jaishawn Barham continues to build in DeMarvion Overshown’s absence. In Tuesday’s training camp practice for the Dallas Cowboys, linebacker DeMarvion Overshown and offensive tackle Tyler Guyton were limited while dealing with soreness. Overshown had a lower body/leg issue while Guyton nursed elbow discomfort. Neither injury is considered concerning, but the team will manage the workload of each player as camp ramps up in the coming days. Also in Tuesday’s practice, outside linebacker Donovan Ezeiruaku was ejected for throwing a punch at offensive tackle Terence Steele. Per head coach Brian Schottenheimer’s policy, Ezeiruaku was thrown out of practice, as he was escorted out by a member of the front office. In Overshown’s absence during the team period on Tuesday, Dee Winters and Jaishawn Barham were featured as the starting linebackers with the first-team unit, while Nate Thomas filled in for Guyton’s absence. It came just a few minutes after Schottenheimer had mentioned that Guyton would maintain his spot as the starting left tackle after Thomas’ slow start to training camp in what has been pinned as a position battle between the two players heading into Oxnard. Each player was slated to get a four-day rotation as the starter, but Guyton remains in place after the first four days. “We talked to Nate and said that he needs to show us a little more consistent play to push for that. I know we had told you guys about the rotation,” Schottenheimer said. “Tyler will stay at left tackle. I’m excited to see how Nate handles that challenge, but Tyler is playing really, really well.” Barham stepping in for Overshown is yet another feather in the rookie third-round pick’s cap early in training camp, as he has stacked together multiple strong practice performances. “His ability to apply the things we’re coaching,” Schottenheimer said about what has stood out about Barham. “We’ve put him in some different spots, which is really cool. You see and know the physicality, but to know and apply it has been great.” Packers’ Micah Parsons: Playing vs. Cowboys in Week 6 ‘realistic’ – Rob Demovsky, ESPN.com When the schedule came out, it seemed inevitable Micah Parsons’ first game back would be against the Cowboys. For a guy who said he’s not into timelines but rather coming back as strong as possible, Micah Parsons sounded optimistic about one thing: He likes his chances of playing in the Green Bay Packers ‘ Week 6 game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lambeau Field. “I think it’s very realistic,” Parsons said Tuesday. He acknowledged, however, that there’s still work to be done in his rehab from last year’s torn ACL/meniscus injury sustained in Week 15. “I wouldn’t say it’s not possible, but, at the same time, in these next 10 weeks — 10, 12 weeks from now on — we’ve got to do our part to make it possible,” Parsons said in his first session with reporters since training camp opened last week. “It’s not off the board, but we’ve got to put the work in.” Parsons opened training camp on the physically unable to perform list and likely will remain with that designation when the regular season opens. That means he would miss at least the first four games of the season. However, a change in the PUP rule now allows players to begin practicing after just two regular-season weeks. In the past, players could not do so for the first four weeks of the season. Given that the Packers rarely allow players coming off ACL injuries to practice earlier than nine months after surgery, Parsons isn’t likely to practice until late September. The Packers play the Chicago Bears in Week 5 (Oct. 4), followed by the Cowboys (Oct. 11). The Packers were 9-3-1 when Parsons went down against the Denver Broncos , and they didn’t win another game the rest of the way. Parsons had 12.5 sacks and,…

title: Dallas Cowboys 2026 Opponent Preview: Houston Texans
summary: The 2026 NFL season will feature the eighth ever edition of The Governor’s Cup, which is the meeting between the Dallas Cowboys and Houston Texans. With the last two all-Texas pro football meetings coming in Arlington in 2022 and 2024, it is time for the Cowboys to visit the Texans in Houston for the first […]
full_text: The 2026 NFL season will feature the eighth ever edition of The Governor’s Cup, which is the meeting between the Dallas Cowboys and Houston Texans. With the last two all-Texas pro football meetings coming in Arlington in 2022 and 2024, it is time for the Cowboys to visit the Texans in Houston for the first time since 2018. With our preview series shifting towards some of the perceived toughest games on the Cowboys schedule, the Texans will be the first non-divisional opponent the Cowboys play in the continental United States this season. Prior to this week four battle, the Cowboys will play at the Giants, versus the Commanders, and in Brazil against the Ravens, before week four at the Texans in one of five scheduled early kickoff window games. The Texans are 18-8 at home under head coach DeMeco Ryans since 2023, going 7-2 last year while holding six of their nine home opponents to 20 points or less. It was this defense that led the Texans to a third straight appearance in the Divisional playoffs, but yet again this is where they exited after the offense was shut down by the eventual AFC champion Patriots. The Texans have further committed to bolstering the defense this offseason, one that is expected to be among the league’s best yet again, but absolutely could not come away from the offseason without some type of splash on offense too. They did so by trading for Lions running back David Montgomery, pairing him with Woody Marks out of the backfield and Nico Collins, Jayden Higgins, and Tank Dell at wide receiver. The Cowboys own offense has sky high expectations coming into this season, and one of the things they should be out to answer early is how they play against premier defensive minds. Starting the season against John Harbaugh, Dan Quinn, Jesse Minter, and then this Texans defense will give some early answers here. Interestingly enough, the three coaches listed above along with Ryans for Houston are not just defensive coordinators for their teams, they are head coaches with a rare focus on defense in today’s game. How Brian Schottenheimer as the Cowboys’ offensive-minded head coach deals will with this early season pressure and attacks the Texans defense is a question still with some waiting to be done before answering, but until then we can take a closer look at the totality of what the Texans have done this offseason. Texans Key Free Agent Signings/Departures * SIGNED IN FREE AGENCY SAF Reed Blankenship DE Logan Hall DE Jadeveon Clowney LB Jake Hummel DE Dominique Robinson OL Braden Smith OL Evan Brown TE Foster Moreau OL Wyatt Teller DT Sheldon Rankins (Re-signed) OL Trent Brown (Re-signed) OL Ed Ingram (Re-signed) SAF M.J. Stewart (Re-signed) * DEPARTED IN FREE AGENCY DT Tim Settle WR Christian Kirk P Tommy Townsend WR Braxton Berrios LB Damone Clark The Texans will bring back their top four pass catchers from a year ago in Schultz, Nico Collins, Jayden Higgins, and Xavier Hutchinson, making offensive line the next priority to have a sustainable offense around C.J. Stroud that can go deeper in the playoffs. Wyatt Teller and Braden Smith project as new starters at guard and tackle, but come with quality experience and the type of mean streak this Houston team values almost across the board at all positions to give them a physical and tough identity. The Texans are interestingly built to embrace the heavy formation trend expected to take the NFL by storm this season, with Schultz and FA addition Foster Moreau at tight end, a retooled offensive line, and receivers like Collins and Higgins that can win out of the slot or from condensed formations. Losing Kirk and Berrios in free agency does thin the depth chart at wide receiver for players that fit this mold for Houston, but the net positives this organization achieved on offense while bringing in strong reinforcements on defense should have them very excited about their positioning in the AFC South. The most notable defensive addition here is Reed Blankenship coming over from the Eagles, giving the Texans a tough safety group of Blankenship, Jalen Pitre, and Calen Bullock. The Texans did move on from former Cowboys linebacker Damone Clark in free agency, who was most recently with the Lions in 2025. They recently added last year’s sack leader for the Cowboys though, a reunion with veteran Jadeveon Clowney, bringing his career back to Houston after being their first overall pick in 2014. The Cowboys returning experience along the offensive line should know plenty about how to deal with Clowney, but if he still has as much juice left in the tank as he showed in Dallas on an otherwise terrible defense, the matchup will not be easy. The Texans also lost Tim Settle in free agency, but now the Cowboys will potentially still play against him twice this season too, as he signed with the Washington Commanders. Texans 2026 Draft Class Round 1, Pick 26: G Keylan Rutledge Round 2, Pick 4 (36 Overall): DT Kayden McDonald Round 2, Pick 27 (59 Overall): TE Marlin Klein Round 4, Pick 6 (106 Overall): G Febechi Nwaiwu Round 4, Pick 23 (123 Overall): LB Wade Woodaz Round 5, Pick 1 (141 Overall): SAF Kamari Ramsey Round 6, Pick 23 (204 Overall): WR Lewis Bond Round 7, Pick 27 (243 Overall): LB Aiden Fisher The Texans commitment to being a force in the trenches was just getting started in free agency. Starting their draft with one of the best run blockers, Keylan Rutledge out of Georgia Tech, in the first round, and Ohio State’s Kayden McDonald as a people-mover at defensive tackle, further embraced the identity they’re looking for. The rest of this draft class also shows off smart drafting by the Texans, as they went for prospects that will slide onto depth charts where established talent is already in place and expectations can be tempered. We’ve already talked about both Schultz and Moreau at tight end, which leaves room for rookie Marlin Klein as the team’s second of two second-round picks to develop. The same goes for Nwaiwu at guard, Woodaz at linebacker, and Ramsey at safety. The Texans fanbase, obviously one of the newer ones in the NFL at large, has fully embraced the last three seasons under Ryans where the team’s identity has been on hard-nosed defense. In year two of coach Schotty’s focus on trench play, physicality, and culture, Dallas will go toe-to-toe with a Texans team valuing many of the same things. Texans 2026 Coaching Changes * New to staff this season: Tight Ends James Ferentz The Texans will have the same defensive, offensive, and special teams coordinator under Ryans in 2026, with ST coordinator Frank Ross being the longest-tenured of the bunch as a staff member since 2021. Even two of the positions we’ve highlighted as pivotal for Houston this year, safety and running back, have returning coaches with experience in Danny Barrett as assistant HC and RB coach and Stephen Adegoke who’s been coaching safeties since 2023. So far for our preview series, the Texans have far and away the most coaching continuity, with only tight ends coach James Ferentz making the list of new hires. The Texans let the division slip away for the first time since 2023 last year despite winning two more games than their previous South-winning seasons under Ryans, by way of the upstart Jaguars with first year HC Liam Coen going 13-4. They will put their defense to the test at the start of the season against Josh Allen, Joe Burrow, the Colts in week three, then Dak Prescott and the Cowboys followed by their remaining division opponents the Titans and Jags back to back in weeks five and six. It will be revealing early for the Texans, and frames the Cowboys game as one with heightened importance even beyond the state bragging rights. Previous 2026 Opponent Previews: Philadelphia Eagles New York Giants Seattle Seahawks Arizona Cardinals Baltimore Ravens Washington Commanders Green Bay Packers

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 40
summary: It is Day 40 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - JANUARY 16: Dak Prescott #4 of the Dallas Cowboys rushes for a touchdown against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the second quarter in the NFC Wild Card playoff game at Raymond James Stadium on January 16, 2023 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Day 40 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Oh yes, this is Day 40 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit one of the most complete playoff performances of the modern Cowboys era. Dallas went into Tampa Bay, dominated Tom Brady’s Buccaneers and put this one to bed in extraordinary fashion. Monday, January 16, 2023 — 8:15 p.m. ET Raymond James Stadium, Tampa, Florida Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 31, Tampa Bay Buccaneers 14 There was plenty of reason for Cowboys fans to feel nervous beforehand. Tampa Bay had beaten Dallas 19-3 in the season opener, a night that also ended with Dak Prescott suffering a fractured thumb. Brady had never lost to the Cowboys in seven previous meetings, and Dallas entered the playoffs after an ugly 26-6 defeat against Washington. Instead of carrying those concerns into Tampa, the Cowboys produced their sharpest game of the season. The opening minutes were slow, with both offenses struggling to generate a first down. Dallas finally broke through on its third possession. Tony Pollard carried four times for 25 yards during an 80-yard drive, and Dak Prescott found Dalton Schultz for a 22-yard touchdown. Brett Maher missed the extra point, but the Cowboys had taken the first lead, 6-0. Tampa Bay appeared ready to answer when Brady drove the Buccaneers to the Dallas five-yard line. On second-and-goal, however, he attempted to throw the ball away in the back of the end zone and instead found Jayron Kearse. The interception was Brady’s first in the red zone since 2019 and prevented Tampa Bay from changing the momentum. Prescott then directed one of the defining drives of the night. Dallas traveled 80 yards in 15 plays while taking more than eight minutes off the clock. Facing fourth-and-goal from the one, Prescott kept the ball on a bootleg and walked around the left side for a touchdown. Maher missed again, but the lead had grown to 12-0. The Cowboys struck once more before halftime. Prescott completed seven of nine passes on an 80-yard drive, escaped pressure and found Schultz for an 11-yard touchdown with 27 seconds remaining. Maher missed his third consecutive extra point, yet Dallas still went into the locker room ahead 18-0. Nothing changed after halftime. Starting at their own 14, the Cowboys drove 86 yards in eight plays. Schultz made a juggling 26-yard reception, CeeDee Lamb added another 26-yard catch and Pollard broke an 18-yard run before Prescott found Michael Gallup for a two-yard touchdown. Maher’s fourth missed extra point left the score at 24-0, but the outcome was already becoming difficult to doubt, and so was Maher as the team’s kicker. Brady finally put Tampa Bay on the board late in the third quarter with a 30-yard touchdown pass to Julio Jones, although the two-point attempt failed. Dallas responded immediately. Facing fourth-and-four at the Tampa Bay 18, Mike McCarthy kept the offense on the field and Prescott found Lamb completely uncovered for a touchdown. Maher finally converted the extra point, although some people were calling for the two-point attempt to keep him off the field. The Buccaneers added a late Cameron Brate touchdown and successful two-point conversion, but the closing points did little more than reduce the final margin. Dallas had already controlled the game at the line of scrimmage, protected Prescott and prevented Brady from creating the type of comeback that defined his career. This game belongs on the countdown because it ended several long-running Cowboys frustrations at once. Dallas earned its first victory over Brady, snapped an eight-game road playoff losing streak and secured its first postseason win away from home since beating San Francisco in the 1992 NFC Championship Game. #Cowboys vs #Buccaneers 2022 Wildcard Round Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 31, Tampa Bay Buccaneers 14 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/6m5r3K9Vkt — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 4, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Brady announced on February 1, 2023, that he was retiring for good. That confirmed the loss to Dallas as the last game of his illustrious career. title: Cobie Durant is playing like the Cowboys’ best cornerback
summary: Who is the best cornerback on the Dallas Cowboys roster? This is a difficult question to answer, and unfortunately for the worst kind of reasons. DaRon Bland begins the season with the most pedigree of the group having been named an All-Pro before, and Shavon Revel carries an air of excitement as he is only […]
full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Oxnard, CA, USA; Dallas Cowboys cornerback Cobie Durant (2) at training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Who is the best cornerback on the Dallas Cowboys roster? This is a difficult question to answer, and unfortunately for the worst kind of reasons. DaRon Bland begins the season with the most pedigree of the group having been named an All-Pro before, and Shavon Revel carries an air of excitement as he is only a year removed from being one of the more exciting draft prospects by the team. Still though, neither of them necessarily feel like sturdy options to pick as answers to this question. Enter Cobie Durant. An afterthought of a free agency signing and someone who has become more known than anything for his jersey number in that he hasn’t given it up to rookie phenom Caleb Downs, Durant is only a handful of practices into his Cowboys career and yet it looks like he is the best player in his respective room. Cobie Durant is standing out in all the right ways Calling anyone the best or worst anything right now after a handful of practices is making quite the mountain out of barely a mole hill, but facts are facts to this point. And at this point Durant is flashing more than anybody else and had a particularly strong showing during the group’s first padded practice on Monday. The mothership’s Patrik Walker caught a great video of his interception that really shows how he managed to focus all the way through the play and pick off Dak Prescott. Dak Prescott under duress attempts to squeeze it in to CeeDee Lamb. Cobie Durant says not on his watch — INT. #Cowboys pic.twitter.com/DObKkWUxc9 — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) August 3, 2026 Standing out in this cornerback room is not exactly hard (with all due respect). It was one of the positions of greatest need when the offseason began, and while the Cowboys did not address it as much as others, defensive coordinator Christian Parker has a defensive backs background. Perhaps he is an amplifier that makes everyone in the respective area better because of his knowledge and experience. Whatever the case, Durant is making so many plays that the idea of him forfeiting his jersey number to the draft pick with the most pomp and circumstance in a decade isn’t even a talking point anymore. He is earning his keep. Cobie Durant tight coverage and a PBU against CeeDee Lamb. pic.twitter.com/u3NTgg9AWe — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) August 3, 2026 This is exactly the type of thing that needs to happen for the Cowboys to reach the aspirations that we are starting to have for them. We know the players on the team who can raise the ceiling of the group, but the floor is what needs elevating. If enough Cobie Durants of the world are hit on by the team then the floor rises and so do all of the ships that rest upon it.

title: Cowboys safety group making a name for itself beyond Caleb Downs
summary: Keeping with the theme of 2026 Dallas Cowboys training camp having a different look and feel to it from the start, we are back to discuss players that are starting to string together early consistency – now including the team’s first padded practice that happened on Monday. Yesterday, we mentioned the importance of using multiple […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 14: Julius Wood #33 of the Dallas Cowboys defends during a joint practice against the Los Angeles Rams at River Ridge Playing Fields on August 14, 2024 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images Keeping with the theme of 2026 Dallas Cowboys training camp having a different look and feel to it from the start, we are back to discuss players that are starting to string together early consistency – now including the team’s first padded practice that happened on Monday. Yesterday, we mentioned the importance of using multiple reps and days of practice trending in the right direction for a player to truly feel good about their projection. With only unpadded practices through this point, the consistency tag was handed to two skill position players and QB Dak Prescott maestro-ing it all. Christian Parker’s defense seem to have taken that personally, as it took just one padded practice for them to start flipping the narrative strongly in their favor. You’ve likely already seen by now how the Cowboys cornerbacks stole the show at Monday’s more physical practice . Cobie Durant had an interception, Shavon Revel strung together more flash plays in coverage, and DaRon Bland got in on the action as well. The cornerback versus wide receiver battles have taken up alot of the attention from Cowboys camp as a whole, and allowed other important things to go under the radar. One such thing that we are here to talk about now, which does tie into cornerback and secondary play at large, is the play the Cowboys are getting at safety. The Cowboys depth chart at safety shows a side to Parker’s coaching excellence that hasn’t been discussed as much as his eye for player acquisition specific to the scheme, and how the front office has supported that, or the way he’s utilizing the current rookie class. The arrow-pointing-up reports about safeties Malik Hooker, Markquese Bell, even Julius Wood and Alijah Clark, and, of course, even through the most recent practice, 11th overall pick Caleb Downs . Throw in the fact that P.J. Locke and Jalen Thompson are expected to see plenty of snaps once the regular season begins, and this is a very interesting, versatile safety group budding for the Cowboys. The update on Wood came from Nick Eatman of the team’s official website , and Clark flashed in a similar way as well: Bringin’ the Wood – On the first day of pads, you wouldn’t expect anything other than someone named “Julius Wood” to have a physical practice. Just an hour before, his head coach Brian Schottenheimer mentioned Wood as being active and making the safety position rather deep. And then in practice, he had several big pops, jarring the ball loose on a pass during the team drills and he also wasn’t afraid to come up in run support. Also, Caleb Downs had a few run stops as well. But Wood is a guy trying to get noticed – and he did that Monday. – (Nick Eatman) Cowboys S Alijah Clark with a nice run stuff pic.twitter.com/7GoFX1aTe9 — Sebastian Sanchez (@Sanchez_Reports) August 3, 2026 Downs was also mentioned for his run support, meaning the Cowboys are starting to have a stacked list of safeties comfortable coming down to defend in the box. Paired with how well the cornerbacks are playing in coverage, and linebackers are being used in disguise as well, and the Cowboys defense is on a whole new level of scheming in an attempt to confuse offenses this season. Safeties are the ultimate chess piece of a defense that can unlock so much of this, and the Cowboys are learning that pretty quickly in Oxnard. One key way to forecast how good a team may or may not be in the NFL for any given season is to look at where they can make the most difference in their play versus the opponent, and how much those things often weigh on the outcome of games. For example, the Cowboys have likely the best duo of wide receivers in the league, with Ryan Flournoy rising as a third option. If this trio continues doing what they’re capable of, and the Cowboys cornerbacks keep their momentum from the start of padded practices going, Dallas will have the potential to build a significant differential in big pass plays generated on offense versus allowed on defense. Dak Prescott has of an offense that returns all of its starters from 2025, as well as the play-calling head coach and offensive coordinator. With Prescott in full command, and the defense not pulling any punches when it comes to throwing the kitchen sink at opponents and embracing all of their depth, this could create the most important difference. We already know Prescott hasn’t needed much help when it comes to outplaying the other quarterbacks in the NFC East, but if the Cowboys defense is ready to regularly stress all of the opposing QBs on their schedule and make Dak the far-and-away better passer in more matchups, the sky will be the limit for this team. Caleb Downs with a great fill in the run game here #Cowboys pic.twitter.com/dk4t96F8nv — Tommy Yarrish (@tommy_yarrish) August 3, 2026 Even if Downs settles into a true nickel role for the majority of his snaps, and the amount of moving around he does settles down at some point in his rookie campaign, the Cowboys are showing they have enough other exciting depth at safety to still be versatile on the back end and give offenses fits. In the competitive nature of this camp so far, look for the Cowboys offense to come out with man-coverage beaters that get after the cornerback group that won the day Monday, but put a spotlight on Dallas’ safeties to disrupt this even more and continue making a name for themselves as a unit.

title: Cowboys defense dominates the day in first padded practice
summary: The Dallas Cowboys have one of the top offenses in the NFL. Tyler Guyton seems to be trending upward, and they’ve also seen some positive things from Javonte Williams, Jaydon Blue, […]
full_text: The Dallas Cowboys have one of the top offenses in the NFL. Quarterback Dak Prescott has been wheeling and dealing to his top two targets CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, plus Ryan Flournoy continues to ascend. Tyler Guyton seems to be trending upward, and they’ve also seen some positive things from Javonte Williams, Jaydon Blue, and Phile Mafah in running game. That was in shorts and helmets. On Monday, the Cowboys put the pads on for the first time, and things got spicy. One thing was clear during practice, and it was that the defensive unit came out on a mission, because they were making plays left and right during team drills. Let’s start with first-round safety Caleb Downs. What else is there to say? He’s quickly showing why he was such a sought-after draft pick back in April. Downs looked like he was shoot out of a cannon as he did a great job with run fits and making plays against the pass. Look for Downs to keep being lined up in the box, in the deep middle of the field, and close the edge. He’s going to be the chess piece of this defense under Christian Parker, and he’s only going to get better. Caleb Downs … WHOA. #Cowboys #trainingcamp pic.twitter.com/XWBdfdJ43F — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) August 3, 2026 DaRon Bland and Caleb Downs with tight coverage here for the PBU. pic.twitter.com/QvcfgaRiQ1 — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) August 3, 2026 DeMarvion Overshown had to be salivating to get the pads on after another injury-plagued year in 2025. Much like Downs, Overshown was flying around and roaming on the second level on Monday, and he even had the biggest hit of the day on running back Hunter Luepke on a toss play. He even showed his prowess against the pass some, which isn’t surprising as a former safety. The skill set is undeniable when it comes to Overshown, and as long he remains healthy, this will be more of the same. DeMarvion Overshown 👀 pic.twitter.com/drO3CamM7v — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) August 3, 2026 Rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham had already been turning heads with his play in shorts and helmets during the first several practices. That continued on Monday as he and Overshown held down first-team reps at the linebacker spot. He looked very fluid and comfortable as he filled gaps against the run, and even beat All-Pro Tyler Smith on a rep that would have been a sack in a real game. He is undoubtedly making a huge statement early in camp that he will be on the field quite a bit in 2026. In fact, it could be more than people think. Jaishawn Barham vs Tyler Smith https://t.co/1VPRHBtrwX — Mauricio Rodríguez (@MauNFL) August 3, 2026 Not to be forgotten, the Cowboys’ cornerbacks were the stars of the day . Shavon Revel had some very nice battles against Lamb, and even did a great job jamming him at the line of scrimmage once. Cobie Durant keeps making plays, and he snagged an interception on Prescott in the end zone. DaRon Bland, who is looking to prove he’s still worth the investment the Cowboys have in him, had a solid day as well, which included some very sticky coverage against George Pickens which led to a pass breakup. Also, rookie Devin Moore got a nice pass breakup versus Lamb, and had some words for him after the play. Cobie Durant INT pic.twitter.com/uUbF9wN64M — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) August 3, 2026 Ceedee Lamb Got Jammed Up By Revel Jr #sheeeesh pic.twitter.com/W5D27EekES — JESSE (With No “i”) (@Mr4thAndLong) August 3, 2026 It’ll be interesting to see what transpires on Tuesday in the second padded practice.

title: Here is what happened to last year’s final Cowboys roster cuts
summary: As training camp kicks off for real this week with padded practices, many a player on the Cowboys’ 90-man offseason roster is beginning to wonder what his chances are of making the roster. Realistically, for most of the UDFAs and street free agents brought in during the offseason, just making the practice squad must be […]
full_text: As training camp kicks off for real this week with padded practices, many a player on the Cowboys’ 90-man offseason roster is beginning to wonder what his chances are of making the roster. Realistically, for most of the UDFAs and street free agents brought in during the offseason, just making the practice squad must be considered a success. But even those up to 16 practice squad spots are highly contested. Out of the standard 16 players, at least 10 must be rookies or second-year players, while up to six can be veterans with unlimited accrued experience. And with teams reducing rosters in one fell swoop from 90 to 53 players, there’ll be a lot of players scrambling for jobs. But what happens to the players who don’t get a spot on the practice squad after final cuts? Do they automatically become the proverbial grocery packers at WalMart or Target? Well, not if they made it through camp with the Dallas Cowboys, at least if last year is anything to go by. On August 25 & 26 last year, the Cowboys released 37 players to get to the final 53. Where are those 37 players now? I’m glad you asked. Here’s an overview of all 37 players, showing what happened to each player in 2025 and where he is today: body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table { border: 1px solid #000 !important; border-collapse: collapse !important; } body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th { padding: 0px 6px !important; } 2025 final Cowboys roster cuts Name POS Status 2025 Status 2026 Still on Cowboys Roster Justin Barron* LB Cowboys Cowboys Alijah Clark* S Cowboys Cowboys Malik Davis* RB Cowboys Cowboys Princeton Fant* TE Cowboys PS Cowboys Traeshon Holden* WR Cowboys PS Cowboys DeMarvion Overshown (Reserve/PUP) LB Cowboys Cowboys Jonathan Mingo (Reserve/Injured) WR Cowboys Cowboys Shavon Revel (Reserve/NFI) CB Cowboys Cowboys Josh Butler (Reserve/PUP) CB Cowboys Cowboys Tyrus Wheat DE Lions Cowboys Still In NFL Jalen Cropper* WR Cowboys PS Saints Rivaldo Fairweather* TE Cowboys PS Cardinals Earnest Brown* DE Cowboys PS Titans Geron Christian* OT Denver Denver Robert Rochell* CB Panthers Panthers Kemon Hall* CB Titans Buccaneers Buddy Johnson* LB Colts Raiders Saahdiq Charles* OG Panthers PS Panthers Josh Kelly WR Texans PS Texans Nick Broeker OT Bills PS Bills Tommy Akingbesote DT Bills PS Bills Hakeem Adeniji OT Cowboys Ravens Payton Turner (Reserve/Injured) DE Cowboys IR Lions UFL/CFL Israel Mukuamu S Panthers UFL Deuce Vaughn RB Broncos PS UFL Denzel Daxon DE Cardinals PS CFL Tyler Neville TE — UFL Michael Ojemudia CB — UFL Currently out of football Will Grier* QB Cowboys PS Retired C.J. Goodwin ST Cowboys Retired John Stephens TE Cowboys IR Injury settlement Jalen Brooks* WR Cardinals — Troy Pride CB Colts PS — Darius Harris LB Patriots PS — Mike Smith S — — La’el Collins OT — — Christian Matthew CB — — Couple of topline thoughts: 62% of the final cuts (23 of 37) are still on NFL rosters 76% (28/37) are still playing organized football in the NFL, UFL, or CFL Only 19% may still be looking for a team (which excludes the two retirees) Whatever else you think of the Cowboys’ roster-building, these numbers suggest their scouting department is finding players who remain viable NFL prospects even when Dallas doesn’t have room for them. Of course, I didn’t go through the numbers of the remaining 31 NFL teams to see how the Cowboys’ numbers stack up, but I’m confident that having 23 out of 37 “surplus” players still in the NFL today is a pretty good rate. The players marked with an (*) were the initial 15 players the Cowboys signed to their 2025 practice squad, and the data here suggests that making the Cowboys’ practice squad is a pretty good indicator that a player will remain in the NFL. Five of the initial 15 are still with the Cowboys today, and eight were eventually signed by another NFL team either in 2025 or 2026. Will Grier retired, so he shouldn’t count against the total, which leaves WR Jalen Brooks as the only initial practice squad signing without a team this year. That is a “success rate” of 93% for the Cowboys practice squad. Looks like having the Cowboys on your résumé doesn’t hurt. So if you’re a down-roster guy on the Cowboys’ training camp roster, focus on making the practice squad. Last year’s numbers suggest that getting to 53 isn’t the only way to stay in the NFL. Make the practice squad, and you’ve given yourself a pretty good chance to keep the dream alive. And that’s really all anybody can ask for.

title: Sai’vion Jones looking to fill some big shoes
summary: There is talk coming out of training camp about Sai’vion Jones being ready to take a big step forward in Vance Joseph’s defense this season. Veteran defensive lineman Zach Allen had high praise for Jones the other day, mentioning he has taken a big leap entering his second season. With the loss of Johnathan Franklin-Myers […]
full_text: There is talk coming out of training camp about Sai’vion Jones being ready to take a big step forward in Vance Joseph’s defense this season. Veteran defensive lineman Zach Allen had high praise for Jones the other day, mentioning he has taken a big leap entering his second season. With the loss of Johnathan Franklin-Myers to the Tennessee Titans in free agency, a large void in the defensive front to the tune of roughly 500 snaps across from Allen. It is worth noting that the Denver Broncos defense under Vance Joseph typically uses a fairly heavy rotation of five players along their standard three-man line. During his rookie season, Jones didn’t see the field much. That isn’t unusual for mid-round defensive lineman. It’s a big jump from college to the pros. He saw playing time in Week 4, 14, and 18 with just 33 total defensive snaps. Which means for those of us eye-test guys, there isn’t a lot to go on from his rookie season. At this point, it’s all a projection. I’m excited to see what Jones will be able to accomplish this season. He’s darn near a clone in size to Zach Allen, with both of them being 6’5” and 285 pounds. The third-round pick from the 2025 NFL Draft has had a year to study this defense, get his feet wet, and learn from one of the best-coached defensive fronts in the game today. The sky is the limit for this young Bronco.
