title: 2026 Denver Broncos Training Camp: Day 4 News and Notes
summary: Day 4 of Denver Broncos training camp is in the books! Today was the most physical and chippy practice of camp so far, and we saw our first little camp skirmish. The defense dominated again, and All-Pro Zach Allen and the Denver Broncos front 7 and defense came away as the winners. Cornerback Riley Moss […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - JULY 30: Talanoa Hufanga (9) of the Denver Broncos stands with teammates during practice at Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Thursday, July 30, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Day 4 of Denver Broncos training camp is in the books! Today was the most physical and chippy practice of camp so far, and we saw our first little camp skirmish. The defense dominated again, and All-Pro Zach Allen and the Denver Broncos front 7 and defense came away as the winners. Cornerback Riley Moss and Jonah Elliss continued to be standout players during camp and are your early contenders for the camp winners right now. Turning up the intensity 📈 pic.twitter.com/bpI2OC7FG6 — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) August 4, 2026 In today’s camp report, we have more on the defense dominating the day again, Jaylen Waddle being a big fan of Marvin Mims, Sean Payton excited to see who wins the LB3 job, a positive update on Nik Bonitto who left practice with an injury, more injury updates, news and notes, tweets from camp, quotes and more! Defense, Zach Allen, Riley Moss, and Jonah Elliss stand out again The pads were on, and the Denver Broncos defense dominated the day again. It was the most physical and chippy practice thus far, and the defense more or less repeated their performance from Monday during today’s practice. The Denver Broncos front 7 and pass rush dominated the defense and was led by All-Pro defensive lineman Zach Allen, who channeled his inner Von Miller and kinda wrecked practice for the offense. Cornerback Riley Moss continued his strong training camp and deflected multiple passes while edge rusher Jonah Elliss had a sack and has been providing consistent pressure throughout camp. #Broncos safety Talanoa Hufanga walks by media after camp today with a message: “Just make sure y’all write in your reports, defense won the day. Defense won the day.” It did — Luca Evans (@bylucaevans) August 4, 2026 The Broncos offense had its way with the defense early in camp, but once the pads came on, the defense has stood tall in back-to-back practices. We know this unit is good and should be among the best in the NFL, so it is promising to see these two units go back and forth so far during training camp. Speaking of Allen, head coach Sean Payton had some high praise for the Broncos team leader and All-Pro on the defensive line. He praised his stamina and ability to play at a high level while carrying a high snap count, his intelligence and quickness off the ball. “I think the first thing you’d say is, and some players have this, he has tremendous stamina, so play 38 looks like eight, play 60 still looks like eight. So that’s a big asset at a position where it’s hard. Then I would say his intelligence and his quickness off the ball. He’ll win usually in the first second and a half of a rush, or he’ll win early. So that’s what makes him difficult.” Allen also spoke to the media today and was asked how this defensive line unit can improve despite being mostly the same unit from the previous years. He started off by praising DC Vance Joseph for setting such a high standard for them and then said he hopes they can get to a point where “there are less mistakes, but still have that fast and violent playstyle”. “There are always things to improve on. That’s the really cool thing about this group is we’re just constantly trying to find new ways to get better. It all starts with ‘VJ’ (Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph). He sets such a high standard. Yes, we were good last year, but there were still a lot of things that we could have been better at and cleaned up. We want to be as consistent as we can be and play at the highest level that we can. It starts with right now taking it day-by-day. Playing with a good play style, and playing fast, and playing violent and correcting mistakes in the meeting room. Hopefully we get to the point where there are less mistakes but still have that fast, violent playstyle.” The Broncos defense and specifically their front 7 will be key to this team’s success this season. As we know, they have led the NFL in sacks in back-to-back seasons and will need to repeat that success this season if they want to make it to the Super Bowl. That all starts upfront with Zach Allen, but they’ll need players like rookie Tyler Onyedim, Sai’vion Jones, Eyioma Uwazurike, and others to step up, and so far, it sounds like those players are doing well. On top of that, you have Jonah Elliss and Riley Moss being standout players, which makes this defense even better and deeper, which is bad news for the NFL. Jaylen Waddle is a big fan of Marvin Mims Broncos explosive wide receiver Jaylen Waddle has been making plays all camp, even against top cornerback Pat Surtain II, and is looking as advertised. However, today after practice when he met with the media, he told the reporters that he is a “big fan” of another explosive wide receiver on the team. "I'm a big fan of Marvin Mims, I'm not going to lie!" 🙌 Jaylen Waddle is SUPER impressed by his fellow WR 💪 pic.twitter.com/C08LbpVr0o — DNVR Broncos (@DNVR_Broncos) August 4, 2026 Waddle told reporters that he is a big fan of Marvin Mims and said that, “He is very explosive, and I love watching him work”. He added that he loves picking his brain and that you have to respect that speed. “Man, Marvin, I am a big fan of Marvin Mims; I am not going to lie. He is very explosive, and I love watching him work. I love going out and being in meetings and picking his. Marvin is a big play waiting to happen. You have to respect that speed, man, and it’s great just seeing him” We have seen Mims make big plays as a wide receiver and returner throughout his career, and you have to respect that speed. He is an electric deep threat, dangerous in space, and is an All-Pro return man. Pairing his playmaking ability with Jaylen Waddle, who is one of the more explosive playmakers in the NFL, and the Denver Broncos have the potential to be a productive big-play offense this upcoming season. Mims has had a strong start to camp and is pushing for more snaps and targets in this offense. He is competing with Pat Bryant, who is also having a strong camp, and Troy Franklin for that WR3 job, or at least snaps and targets in this offense. He will also continue being a dangerous return man who can take it for a touchdown whenever he touches the ball. He is in the final year of his contract, which has made some speculate about him being a trade candidate, but unless you’re getting a high pick in return, his value to this team with Super Bowl hopes is much higher than whatever draft picks you will get in return. Payton is excited to see how LB3 shakes out The Denver Broncos LB3 competition is one of the more interesting camp battles that fans were excited to see play out. Well, according to Head Coach Sean Payton, we can add him to the list of people excited to see who emerges as the Broncos LB3 coming out of training camp. A sneaky-important position for #Broncos in 2026: ILB3. Need reliability there and Denver currently has a young, inexperienced group. Sean Payton said he’s “excited” to see who emerges there, from ST perspective too. Clear no depth ILBs have separated yet. pic.twitter.com/vWXirGCimt — Luca Evans (@bylucaevans) August 4, 2026 Payton was asked if he is concerned about the amount of inexperience the team has at their backup positions, and he said he is excited to see who those other two players are to make the team behind veterans Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad. “No, I’m kind of excited to see who kind of… Both from [Special Teams Coordinator/Assistant Head Coach Darren] Rizzi’s perspective and then from a defensive perspective, who are those other two players?” The Broncos do have a lot of inexperience at the backup linebacker position. Jordan Turner, who is currently on the NFI, was a UDFA last season, as was Karene Reid, who cracked the 53-man roster last season. Then you have…

title: Denver Broncos news and tidbits from Monday’s training camp practice
summary: Yesterday after their first padded training camp session, the Denver Broncos had several prolonged interviews. Head Coach Sean Payton, safety Talanoa Hufanga, and tight end Adam Trautman offered updates and insight to a wide array of questions from reporters at their new training camp facility. Sean Payton offers several important updates One of the first […]
full_text: ENGLEWOOD, CO - JULY 31: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos talks to a player during training camp at Broncos Park Powered by CommonSpirit on July 31, 2026 in Englewood, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Getty Images) | Getty Images Yesterday after their first padded training camp session, the Denver Broncos had several prolonged interviews. Head Coach Sean Payton, safety Talanoa Hufanga, and tight end Adam Trautman offered updates and insight to a wide array of questions from reporters at their new training camp facility. Sean Payton offers several important updates One of the first updates mentioned was regarding Luke Wattenberg. The veteran center left practice early on with a right arm injury, but Payton didn’t appear to be too concerned about it. At face value, that alleviates some of the worry about missing our starting center long-term. Additionally, he cleared up the air and confusion around second-year cornerback Jahdae Barron’s role with the team. He mentioned that Barron was not playing safety, as someone had floated in an article and on social media the other day. “He’s playing nickel, he’s playing corner and then when we get into dime, he replaces a linebacker. So he’s doing really good. There’s been no position change.” Payton also gushed about the development of cornerback Riley Moss and defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike. With respect to Moss, he cited several areas that have really impressed him and what makes him a great player. “I think learning to play with his feet, really working on reducing some of those fouls. He competes his tail off. I love that about him. He has those traits where it’s a short mindset, short memory. He’s moving around really well right now,” said Payton. “Again, it’s gaining confidence in the defense we’re calling, understanding the leverage, the third-down leverages, and then what we’re trying to take away. He’s handling that progression well.” Speaking on Uwazurike, he noted that he has been pleased with his progression and development. He is one of a handful of defensive linemen battling for an increased role on defense with the departure of John-Franklin Myers. “There’s some really good tape. I’m excited about what’s up for him because he has all those traits you’re looking for, and it’s important to him,” Payton added. If Uwazurike hopes to replace a significant number of Franklin-Myers’ snaps, he will need to improve his pass rush ability. That has been hit-or-miss thus far in his NFL career, but he unteachable traits and a dominant physical profile that overwhelms opposing offensive lineman on run downs. Payton also praised wideout Pat Bryant. With a logjam at wide receiver, it will be interesting to see how each player is utilized. Though Payton mentioned there will be no issue with finding a way to get the second-year wide receiver involved in weekly game plans. “He has some of the better hands in traffic with his feet on the ground, he’s really good at run after the catch. I said this to you guys a year ago, he’s real smart. He’s someone that can move from ‘X’ to the slot. It’ll be easy creating his role.” Talanoa Hufanga speaks on practice intensity, the defense, and leadership Safety Talanoa Hufanga was second to take the podium in front of reporters. He lauded the high energy and intensity of the first practice session. Moreover, the versatile backend defender was over the moon and spoke loves that the defense is almost completely intact relative to last season. “Pretty crazy actually. With the first group, I think the cool part is we’re able to diagnose the defense and offense really easily. Everybody’s on the same string. We kind of know what we guys like to do, where we want to be, me to ‘B. Jones’ and Alex’s communication. It’s, ‘What can we tell the corners’?’ Everybody’s kind of on a string, and I think that’s what really helps when you have the same group of guys, for sure,” Hufanga stated. He also talked about being a leader and team captain last season. For him, it was a ‘true honor’ to be voted by his teammates as one in his first season with the franchise. In fact, he stated it was ‘shocking’ all things considered. Hufanga isn’t sure if he will be a captain this season, but will have no problem being a vocal leader on the defensive side of the ball. “I think I naturally, regardless of if I’m a captain or not, I think now that’s kind of what they expect out of me is what they’re going to get now. The standard has definitely changed for me in trying to go out there and be the best version of myself for my teammates,” he added. Adam Trautman dishes out thoughts on OC Davis Webb and QB Bo Nix The last player to take the podium was tight end Adam Trautman who was one of the leaders of the Broncos’ tight end room last season. He had the top snap share player of the group and saw most of his time at inline tight end. Unfortunately, the unit was one of the least productive in the NFL and the Broncos need them to perform better this season. Perhaps a reason for optimism could be a switch at play caller. Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb will be handling those duties but will still get input from Payton from time to time. Trautman spoke highly of Webb and offered some tidbits and insight to the type of coach he is. “He brings a lot of energy. Obviously, he relates to the players as well. We’re excited to have him. He is a little ball of energy out there honestly, and it’s pretty fun. It’s cool to get into meetings and just watch him talk about concepts, scheme, everything as a whole,” remarked Trautman. He also echoed the sentiment Hufanga did relative to the team’s continuity. The veteran tight end is a huge fan of the roster the front office has assembled. He praised the front office for locking up their key players before the hit the market and taking care of their own players. Trautman also noted that outside expectations [media and fans] on building super teams just isn’t realistic. “There’s a perception from the outside of like you go into free agency and it’s like ‘Oh, you get this person, this person, this person.’ A super team is like, that’s not realistic. So that’s not what happens. Also, they’ve done deals for all of our guys early. All of our elite players, they’ve done them early. We have a good base, good culture. There are several guys that have contributed to that. Why would you want to get rid of them?” Last but not least, Trautman had glowing praise for third-year quarterback Bo Nix. He spoke with high confidence that he is in store for a big season. With Nix poised to make the next step, Denver’s offense should reach new heights in 2026. “He’s just in full total control. I said this all last year, but you’re never going to feel like you’re out of the game when he’s in the huddle.”

title: Which Broncos wide receiver will earn the third spot in the rotation?
summary: As training camp rolls along, the position group battle at wide receiver continues to heat up. The Denver Broncos will showcase Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle as their dynamic duo for the 2026 season. However, who will fight their way to the third option in the Broncos’ aerial attack is yet to be determined. Denver […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - DECEMBER 28: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos celebrates with Marvin Mims Jr. #19 after a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on December 28, 2024 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images As training camp rolls along, the position group battle at wide receiver continues to heat up. The Denver Broncos will showcase Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle as their dynamic duo for the 2026 season. However, who will fight their way to the third option in the Broncos’ aerial attack is yet to be determined. Denver had quarterback Bo Nix throw more than any other quarterback in 2025. The acquisition of Waddle will undoubtedly amplify their aerial production. Alas, there are only so many targets to go around and this receiver group is a strong five deep. Behind Sutton and Waddle, Marvin Mims Jr., Troy Franklin, and Pat Bryant all have unique talents and skillsets. From early camp reports , Mims and Bryant appear to be making the most plays of the trio. Though there is still a lot of time left before the regular season to decipher who will rise to the top. Marvin Mims Jr. A second-round selection in 2023, Mims has made a lot of big plays in the Mile High City. Touting two All-Pro and Pro-Bowl nods for his return skills, fans know his impact on special teams. Yet many have always wondered when—if ever—will Mims take flight as a receiver. After an impressive 2024 season, I was convinced Mims would be featured more in ’25. I couldn’t have been more wrong. In fact, he ranked behind Sutton, Franklin, and Bryant in snap count. Mims had a high catch rate, but not nearly as many explosive plays down the field compared to his second-year efforts. Mims has been a highlight reel during camp thus far. His penchant for hauling in deep passes has been on display. For several years now, Head Coach Sean Payton has often been asked about Mims’ involvement in the offense. And virtually every time he acknowledges they need to get him the ball more. Will this finally be the year that happens? Troy Franklin In his second season, Franklin was big part of Denver’s passing plans. In ‘25, he was targeted 104 times and came down with 65 receptions for 709 yards and 6 touchdowns. All those marks ranked second on the Broncos behind only Sutton who led every category. Nearly half of those catches resulted in first downs. His odds of being that involved this season? Personally, I think zero. That’s just being brutally honest. The former Oregon Duck lined up at wideout 670 times last year. One can’t help but acknowledge Waddle’s presence on the team will cut his snaps drastically. In 11 personnel packages, the team may prefer Bryant in many scenarios, especially due to his run blocking ability. When it comes to ball tracking down the field, I feel Mims’ ability in that respect is quite a bit better. Is there any particular area Franklin stands out at more than the others? Pat Bryant Picked in the third round of the 2025 NFL Draft, Bryant earned a lot of reps as a rookie. Appearing in fifteen games with seven starts, the former Illini standout carved himself a nice role in Denver’s rotation. He logged 475 offensive snaps—the third most at the position. Overall, Bryant reeled in 31 passes on 49 targets for 378 yards and 1 touchdown. An impressive 22 of those receptions resulted in a first down. Unfortunately, he suffered two concussions and a hamstring injury that limited his participation and impact down the final stretch of games. Nevertheless, Bryant’s toughness, attitude, and inside-out flexibility have all been praised by Payton since being drafted. Yesterday, he noted crafting a role for the second-year wideout will be easy. Just how large of a roll may that be, perhaps top three in the wide receiver pecking order? What do you think, Broncos Country? I’m not so sure there is a clear consensus on this one. Which player seems poised to earn the third spot in the Broncos’ receiving rotation? Let me hear all your thoughts in the comments section.
author: Christopher Hart

title: Depth and development have played key role in Broncos quick turnaround
summary: The Denver Broncos have swung big trades, reeled in top notch free agents, and drafted several quality contributors throughout the Sean Payton era. Boasting quality starters across the board, the Broncos have transformed from annual underperformers to touting the ability and talent to compete with any team in the National Football League. Securing back-to-back playoff […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - DECEMBER 25: Jahdae Barron #23 of the Denver Broncos runs out of the tunnel prior to an NFL football game against the Kansas City Chiefs at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos have swung big trades, reeled in top notch free agents, and drafted several quality contributors throughout the Sean Payton era. Boasting quality starters across the board, the Broncos have transformed from annual underperformers to touting the ability and talent to compete with any team in the National Football League. Securing back-to-back playoff berths and their first division title in a decade, the Broncos’ outlook looks the brightest it has in ages. Overlooked, but equally as important, Payton and his staff have assembled a roster loaded with depth in many areas. That has been critical for Denver’s three-year evolution and franchise turnaround. One position group in particular is the offensive line. Their success is a big reason why the Broncos can contend for a Super Bowl title. Early on, it appears that depth may be tested. In their first pads practice of camp, starting center Luke Wattenberg exited yesterday’s first pads practice session with an apparent arm injury and did not return. After practice, Payton expressed confidence Wattenberg wouldn’t miss much time. However, the extent of the injury and his timetable of return is unknown If he misses time, fourth year pro Alex Forsyth would take over. Forsyth was seventh-round draft selection out of Oregon and part of Payton’s first draft class with the team. A practice squad player for his rookie year, Forsyth has appeared in every game the past two seasons with six starts. Payton took a moment to praise the backup pivot’s intelligence and noted he was wise beyond his years. “Yes, he’s super savvy and smart. He’s one of the smarter guys in that room. You don’t feel a young player. You feel like, if you interviewed him, you’d feel like you’re talking to a seven-year vet,” stated Payton. “He’s a little bit of an old soul that way and much appreciated though. He’s really talented.” Speaking of talent, the Broncos defense has a lot of it. Especially in their secondary. Yesterday, reports acknowledged they were a key reason why the defense won the day against the offense. Sitting atop the depth of Broncos’ defensive backfield is second-year cornerback Jahdae Barron. With the high-profile trio of Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja’Quan McMillian scheduled to start once again, Barron is on the hunt for an increased role in 2026. Selected with their first-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, the former Jim Thorpe Award winner appeared in every game and notched five starts as a rookie. He posted 35 tackles, 7 pass breaks ups, 1 forced fumble, and 1 interception. Overall, he saw 334 snaps, roughly 30-percent of the defense’s total in ‘25. Some fans have been critical of Barron’s lack of immediate impact, but the former Longhorns standout fared well and made a positive impact in his snap share. During his post-practice presser, Payton dismissed rumors stating Barron had moved to safety and clarified his role with the defense. “He’s playing nickel, he’s playing corner and then when we get into dime, he replaces a linebacker. He’s doing really good. There’s been no position change.” Another spot where the competition is hot is wide receiver. The Broncos aerial attack is ready for liftoff. The have a batch of talented wideouts vying for the next big role after Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle. Second-year wide receiver Pat Bryant is among them and has been turning heads at camp. A third-round pick alongside Barron in the ‘25 NFL Draft, Bryant’s physicality, run blocking, and ability to snag tough catches were a big part of his rookie campaign successes. He hauled in 31 receptions on 49 targets for 378 yards and 1 touchdown—22 of those catches resulting in first downs. Yesterday, Payton gave Bryant a glowing review for his efforts to date. It’s too early to tell who will earn the third spot battle at wideout, but the former Illini standout is making a tough run for it. “I think his weight is at a good spot. He has some of the better hands in traffic with his feet on the ground. He’s really good at run after the catch. I said this to you guys a year ago, he’s real smart. Someone that can move from ‘X’ to the slot. It’ll be easy creating his role.”
author: Christopher Hart

title: Horse Tracks: ‘Right pieces, right team,’ says Surtain
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! It was inevitable someone would ask the “Super Bowl or bust?” question. Pat Surtain II didn’t take the bait. After all, it’s August. But he didn’t shy away from it, either. Because it’s August with some high expectations. “Our expectations are pretty high, but we are just going to take it […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - SEPTEMBER 7: Pat Surtain II (2), Ja'Quan McMillian (29) and Talanoa Hufanga (9) of the Denver Broncos prepare for Cam Ward (1) and the Tennessee Titans during the fourth quarter of the Broncos' 20-12 win at Empower Field at Mile High on Sunday, September 7, 2025. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) Good morning, Broncos Country! It was inevitable someone would ask the “Super Bowl or bust?” question. Pat Surtain II didn’t take the bait. After all, it’s August. But he didn’t shy away from it, either. Because it’s August with some high expectations. “Our expectations are pretty high, but we are just going to take it week-by-week,” he said, as well-coached in PR as in coverage. “Obviously, that’s the main goal, but it starts right here in training camp and it starts early on in the season. Our main focus is to start out fast and start out hot early. That way we can prepare ourselves to get to that stage.” And the All-Pro corner believes the set-up is perfect for that. “We have all of the right pieces and the right team … the right guys with the right mentality to start things off the right way. This team is great all across the board.” Pat Surtain II “We have all of the right pieces and the right team,” Surtain said. “We have the right guys with the right mentality to start things off the right way. This team is great all across the board.” And a big part of that is the guy calling the defense. Having Vance Joseph back another year is not an insignificant piece of the Super Bowl puzzle. “It does a lot,” Surtain said. “Having ‘VJ’ on our side, a guy that’s been in this league for a long time and knows the ins and outs of this game. When you talk to him, everything about him speaks volumes, but he’s an even better person. Having a guy like that on the defensive side of the ball just translates to success.” Losing players like John Franklin Myers and PJ Locke means there is a void to fill, but Surtain is confident the coaches and veterans can bring the young guys along to do just that. “That’s part of the business, as they say,” Surtain noted about losing Myers and Locke. “Obviously when great players leave, you have to count on other guys to step up.” Between Sai’vion Jones and Eyioma Uwazurike working to replace Myers’ spot, or JL Skinner and Devon Key filling in for Locke, Surtain is not worried about that happening. There are always young guys stepping up. 🔒’d in at #BroncosCamp @R_moss5 x @PatSurtainll pic.twitter.com/KIop5m5aji — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) August 3, 2026 Ja’Quan McMillian, for example, is primed to be an impact player, says Surtain. “His mindset is off the charts. The way that he carries himself on and off the field and his work ethic… There are only a few that quite work like him,” he said. “Being undrafted and coming in, nobody knew about him. Now, he’s a hot commodity. It goes to show the work that he’s put in and how much he values and hones in on his craft. I’m excited for ‘J-Mac.’ He’s a big-time player.” And it was Riley Moss who stole the show yesterday when pads came on. It was cornerback Riley Moss, however, who stole the show with the play of the day. During the final 11-on-11 team period, Courtland Sutton appeared to catch the ball for a big gain, but Moss wrestled the ball away at the last second for the INT. “It’s fantastic,” Sean Payton said of the play. “… The ability to be able to catch it as a defensive back, it’s tough if you don’t have decent enough hands because they’ll just throw at you. So, it was a good play.” In fact, takeaways will be one major emphasis of improvement over last year’s success — something the defense struggled to get last season. “That’s true,” Surtain acknowledged. “We can do that when the ball is in the air, capitalize on more opportunities of taking the ball away. Obviously, those game-changing plays are very vital in NFL games. Taking the ball away and just doing that would definitely help us a lot, too.” But right now, in training camp, it’s mostly about trusting the process, and the wins will come, Surtain says. “I feel like every year, everyone has new goals. …I mentioned before starting out fast early on and not allowing anything to go by. I feel like that is our next step and just staying committed to the process,” Surtain added. “Trusting what ‘VJ’ has for us, and trusting us and our defense as a unit. We have the right pieces at the right places. It just feels right right now.” Even for the six-year veteran, training camp brings a new buzz for the upcoming season, and the buzz this year is good. “I mean, honestly man, it doesn’t even feel like Year 6. It feels like when I was a rookie just starting to come in, starting to come [out of] my shell, but yes, time is flying” he added. “Just seeing how far this team has come has been quite surreal honestly, to say the least. So yes, I’m excited to enter Year 6 and to get it going again.” But first training camp. “It’s going to be a fun camp,” Surtain added.

title: Detroit Lions add new RB, waive WR Lawrence Keys
summary: The Detroit Lions continue to do some roster shuffling amidst some injuries at training camp. Their latest moves, per the transaction wire, were signing running back Raheem Blackshear and waiving Lawrence Keys with an injury designation. Blackshear went undrafted in 2022, but has spent some time with the Bills, Panthers (2022-24), Titans, Steelers, and Jets […]
full_text: Jul 24, 2024; Charlotte, NC, USA; Carolina Panthers running back Raheem Blackshear (3) runs with the ball at Carolina Panthers Practice Fields. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The Detroit Lions continue to do some roster shuffling amidst some injuries at training camp. Their latest moves, per the transaction wire, were signing running back Raheem Blackshear and waiving Lawrence Keys with an injury designation. Blackshear went undrafted in 2022, but has spent some time with the Bills, Panthers (2022-24), Titans, Steelers, and Jets since then. From 2022-24, he played 41 games for the Panthers, starting two. Over that time he carried the ball 52 times for 203 yards and three touchdowns, while adding another 16 catches for 138 yards. The majority of his playing time, however, came on special teams, where he accounted for 405 snaps over those three seasons. Since then, he’s only made the Titans, Steelers and Jets practice squads. He also spent a month earlier this year on the UFL’s Columbus Aviators, but did not appear in any games for the team. At 5-foot-9, 190 pounds, Blackshear is not the biggest of options at tailback, but he’s got decent quickness and a willingness to both play special teams and compete as a pass protector. The addition comes a day after Lions reserve running back Sione Vaki suffered a poked eye and broken nose at training camp. How long he’ll be out isn’t clear, but Dan Campbell seemed optimistic it wouldn’t be a long time. “He’s going to be out for a little bit here,” Campbell said Tuesday. “We’re hopeful vision should be okay in time. We’re not going to have him here today. Just going to let him kind of recover a little bit. So, we think he’ll be okay. He’s just going to need a minute here.” Detroit has also been without No. 1 running back Jahmyr Gibbs, as he continues to hold in for a new contract. As for Keys, he suffered a hamstring injury on Monday. If he clears waivers, he could revert to the Lions’ injured reserve list.

title: Detroit Lions 2026 training camp observations, Day 6: Starting DL making an impact
summary: The Detroit Lions were back on the practice field on Tuesday, strapping on the pads for Day 6 of 2026 training camp. The team practiced a bit longer than on Monday, roughly two hours, working through individual drills, kickoffs and punt coverage/blocking drills, four sets of 11-on-11s, and a full team situational drill to close […]
full_text: Detroit Lions defensive tackle Alim McNeill (54) speaks to media after practice during OTAs at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Friday, May 29, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions were back on the practice field on Tuesday, strapping on the pads for Day 6 of 2026 training camp. The team practiced a bit longer than on Monday, roughly two hours, working through individual drills, kickoffs and punt coverage/blocking drills, four sets of 11-on-11s, and a full team situational drill to close out the day. Injury updates Jeremy Reisman wrote a full report on Tuesday’s injury updates , with the cliff notes being that RB Sione Vaki will miss some time after getting poked in the eye and breaking his nose, TE Anthony Firkser broke his fibula and was placed on injured reserve (the team re-signed Zach Horton as a replacement), and WR Lawrence Keys will be out for a bit with a hamstring injury. At practice, Malcolm Rodriguez exited a few minutes early with what the team is calling an ankle injury, but it’s worth noting he did return to the field after practice to spend time with his family. Starting DL making an impact The offensive line looked great on Monday , but it was the defensive line that was flying around on Tuesday, most notably their starters. With individual drills and the first set of 11’s focusing on rushing, the defensive line was able to show its physicality early in practice and carry that momentum throughout the day. Aidan Hutchinson continues to find ways to get pressure, the power elements to Tyleik Williams’ game look improved, but the play of Alim McNeill and Tyler Lacy have been positive developments. McNeill got two tackles-for-loss (TFL) in the first team period, added another a period later, and forced a pressure on Jared Goff to force a throwaway in the final session. He looks like he has put his injury behind him and is back to being an impact player in the trenches. “Alim is a great player,” left guard Christian Mahogany told Pride of Detroit after practice. “I’ve faced him at all stages; before he got paid, after he got hurt, and now that he’s fully back, he’s himself again. Alim’s a hell of a player, an All-Pro level player, and it’s good to go against him every day, and then talk to him after to see what he sees on the field, and it’s a good experience for someone like me.” Lacy is one of the biggest surprises in camp so far. The Lions appear to want to still deploy a lot of base defensive sets (three linebackers), and in those formations, Lacy has started at the “Big End” role, lining up at the 4i or 5-technique. Then with the reserves, Lacy will kick inside at the 3-technique, showing his positional range. “He’s big, he’s strong, he’s stout, he’s physical. And, so for that big end, especially big end in base, he’s like the perfect big end in base,” coach Dan Campbell said on Day 3 of training camp. “I mean, that’s the way you want him to look, the way you want him to play. And, so the next step for him will be some of this stuff where, okay, now we transition to nickel, slide to the three technique.” In practice on Tuesday, he secured a TFL on the first play of 11s, then followed that up by pancaking a blocker and opening an alley for Jack Campbell to make a run stop. In the next series, he forced a pressure that may have been credited as a sack, then made a key run stop in the third set of team drills. He’s taken some big steps to improve from the player we saw last season. Christian Mahogany earning more LG starter reps Since returning from injury, Mahogany has been slowly acclimating back into practice and has seen a steady increase in snaps with the starter at left guard. On Tuesday, Mahogany still rotated with Juice Scruggs, but the pendulum has shifted toward Mahogany, as he earned starting reps in individual drills, two of the four 11s, and the situational drill to close practice. While he’s still working his way back and battling to retain his starting left guard job, you can see he’s made an effort to add even more power elements to his game, while also maintaining his athleticism so that he can fully operate in offensive coordinator Drew Petzing’s scheme. “I just feel a lot stronger and a lot more confident in myself at the position,” Mahogany told Pride of Detroit after practice. “Just trying to make sure we all gel well—Hank (Fraley) said it to us yesterday, ‘the five (that start) the first game may not be the five at Week 18, or come playoff time. Getting that continuity with everyone is huge for confidence. Seeing how Cade (Mays) and Penei (Sewell) like everything done, and I’m working my way back so I can meet that standard as well.” Mahogany certainly looks comfortable in Petzing’s scheme, as he can put his power on display, and his ability to pull, locate, and block targets in space is something that separates him from his competition. “Coach Petzing is a mastermind when it comes to the (offensive scheme),” Mahogany continued. “He’s involved in the run game a lot, and I feel like I really fit his scheme.[…] Pulling is a big thing here—it was a big thing in school too; we pulled a lot at Boston College. […] I’ve been pulling my whole life, and I’ve always been told ‘pulling guards win championships,’ so that’s what we have to do (here).” Stepping up at RB With Jahmyr Gibbs holding out and Sione Vaki injured, the Lions have leaned on their remaining four running backs to carry the load. Let’s take a quick look at how they’re performing. Isiah Pacheco has shown more burst to his game now that the pads have come on, has delivered some yards after the catch in the flat, as well as presenting himself as a reliable check-down option for Goff. Next up has been Jacob Saylors, who has gotten some run with the first-team (backing up Pacheco) as well as starting with the second team. On Tuesday, he once again produced two 10+ yard runs, and routinely is able to pinball off one-handed tackle attempts. “He knows the system, and he’s a smart guy,” Campbell said at his morning presser. “He’s conscientious. And, so that’s always going to help when you come into camp. [..] He looks much more comfortable. And he’s got ability. I mean, you see it. Jabari Small has stepped into an RB3 role, and he continues to show impressive agility in multiple phases. He also drew unprompted praise from Campbell on Tuesday morning. “Small is doing some things, and he’s doing some things on special teams too,” Campbell explained. “Low to the ground, center of gravity, he’s stout, he’s strong. He’s got lateral quicks. Pretty good, man. You guys are going to get a pretty good look here.” Small has taken advantage of his opportunity, and while it looks like he’ll have a hard time cracking the top four, there could still be a path for him to stick around in Allen Park. Quick hitters Dominic Lovett executed a pretty double move, catching a 50-yard bomb from Teddy Bridgewater that resulted in an 80-yard TD. Jackson Meeks made two big 16-yard catches during situationals to help the second team set up the game-winner to end practice. Ahmed Hassanein had a pressure that led to a “sack”, another TFL on a running back. Levi Onwuzurike is making plays with the third team, but much less when he is with the second team, which has raised some questions on his status. Mekhi Wingo, working with the first team, pressured Goff and forced a throwaway. Trevor Nowaske delivered a beautiful tackle for loss on Saylors, where the hit was so physical that Nowaske’s helmet flew off. Nowaske followed that series up with a sack, blowing right by Devin Cochran (who otherwise had a decent day). Keith Abney secured another clean pass breakup and continues to look physical on special teams. Chuck Clark and Amaris Brown each added pass breakups to their practice highlight reels. Jake Bates went 8 for 8 on the day, connecting from 39, 41, 44, 46, 46, 51, 51, and 59 yards.

title: 6 standouts from Day 6 of Detroit Lions training camp
summary: The Detroit Lions closed out Week 1 of training camp with their second padded practice and a relatively long one. While Erik Schlitt has full observations from Tuesday’s practice coming soon, I’m here to share my six biggest standouts from the session. Alim McNeill McNeill has an incredible start to practice on Tuesday, knifing his […]
full_text: Detroit Lions defensive tackle Alim McNeill (54) walks off the field after practice during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions closed out Week 1 of training camp with their second padded practice and a relatively long one. While Erik Schlitt has full observations from Tuesday’s practice coming soon, I’m here to share my six biggest standouts from the session. Alim McNeill McNeill has an incredible start to practice on Tuesday, knifing his way into the backfield on back-to-back runs. The first, he swam around Cade Mays in a hurry to meet with Rock Ya-Sin for a tackle for loss. On the very next play, he beat Blake Miller’s down block attempt to get his hands on the back again. One person who has been up close and personal opposite McNeill is starting right guard Tate Ratledge. After practice, Ratledge was asked for his standouts on the defense, and McNeill was the first and only name out of his mouth. “Man, Alim,” Ratledge said. “I told somebody the other day how excited I am to get a full camp against him when he’s 100 percent, because he’s really good. Obviously what I saw from him last year at practice, he’s a completely different player now. He’s explosive, strong. So he’s getting me better every day.” Nick Whiteside While that wasn’t quite as big of a day for Whiteside as he’s had all camp, he still makes Tuesday’s list because of a promotion he got. During 1-on-1s, Whiteside was paired up with some of Detroit’s best receivers. He battled, but eventually, lost his rep against Amon-Ra St. Brown, who created some late separation and high pointed a ball over Whiteside’s back. But he came back and decisively won his rep against Isaac TeSlaa to close out the drill. And while he mostly repped with the second team for the rest of practice, he did get some time with the first-team defense during the final situational drill. He helped end the offense’s attempt at a late-drive score, covering Jameson Williams on fourth-and-10 play. Williams did get both hands on it and should’ve come down with the pass, but Whiteside was in decent coverage. Jabari Small Prior to practice, Campbell was asked about the opportunities for guys like Jacob Saylors with Jahmyr Gibbs still sitting in and Sione Vaki out with a broken nose. While Campbell mused on about Saylors for a bit, he was just as eager to talk about Small. “Small is doing some things and he’s doing some things on special teams too, man,” Campbell said. “Low to the ground, center of gravity, he’s stout, he’s strong. He’s got lateral quicks.” Those compliments carried over into practice, where Small got some work with the first team offense alongside Isiah Pacheco and Saylors. During the 11-on-11 rushing drills, Small was the first to bust out a big run with a decisive cut and acceleration to hit hole. I also came away impressed with his shiftiness on a few jump cuts during practice. He, too, ended practice in a significant role, pairing alongside Tom Kennedy as the kick returner during the final situational drill. Small has got a long road to make the 53-man roster, but while the room is shorthanded, he’s doing everything within his control to make the most out of his opportunities. Damone Clark Clark has pretty regularly been with the second-team defense all camp and that didn’t change on Tuesday. However, I came away from Day 6 of practice very impressed with his ability to play downhill and run-fit. His athleticism flashed while tracking down Jacob Saylors on one run. Then he followed it up with the recognition to fill a gap forcing a lineman to drag him out of the hole with an obvious hold. Then during a situational drill, he closed in on a curl route from Greg Dortch quick enough to tackle the veteran receiver a yard short to force a fourth-and-1. On top of that, Clark continues to rep high in most special teams snaps. On Tuesday, he was part of the first-team punt coverage unit. Clark is in an interesting position, because now that linebacker room is filled with a few other veteran depth players (Devin White, Troy Reeder) who he’ll have to fend off to keep his roster spot. Sam LaPorta It’s been an admittedly quiet start to camp for the Pro Bowl tight end. Some of that is likely due to him being on a perceived pitch count, but he’s also not quite looked like his explosive self in 1-on-1 drills. However, Tuesday was a big step in the right direction for LaPorta. In individuals, he easily beat Chuck Clarks to the flats for a short pickup. Then he had his first explosive day of camp, finding the soft spot in the zone on a corner route for 30-yard gain during 11-on-11s. He got open against shortly after on a crossing route against Clark, but Jared Goff just overthrew him. Finally, he capped off a 55-yard drive from the first-team offense with a mesh concept that found him open in the flats for a 5-yard touchdown that gave D.J. Reed no chance to make a play on the ball. I don’t think there’s any real reason to be worried about LaPorta, but it’s still good to see him start to pick things up toward the end of Week 1 of training camp.

title: Detroit Lions training camp injury news: Sione Vaki update, TE injuries mounting
summary: Another day of Detroit Lions practice brings another few additions to the injury list. Unfortunately, there weren’t any players returning from injury on Tuesday, but the news wasn’t all that bad for most players. Let’s get into the latest Detroit Lions training camp injury news from Day 6 of practice. Not practicing: Vaki was originally […]
full_text: Detroit Lions running back Sione Vaki (33) practices during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, July 30, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Another day of Detroit Lions practice brings another few additions to the injury list. Unfortunately, there weren’t any players returning from injury on Tuesday, but the news wasn’t all that bad for most players. Let’s get into the latest Detroit Lions training camp injury news from Day 6 of practice. Not practicing: RB Jahmyr Gibbs ( not-injury related ) RB Sione Vaki (eye, broken nose) TE Anthony Firkser (broken leg) TE Miles Kitselman (leg) WR Lawrence Keys (hamstring) OT Giovanni Manu (NFI) EDGE Derrick Moore (groin) EDGE Payton Turner (back) LB Jimmy Rolder (leg) S Kerby Joseph (PUP, knee) S Brian Branch (PUP, Achilles) Vaki was originally reported to have gotten his eye poked during Monday’s practice, but the reality is a little worse. Campbell noted Tuesday that Vaki also broke his nose in a freak accident. “Vaki yesterday got poked in the eye, broken nose. So, he’s going to be out for a little bit here. We’re hopeful vision should be okay in time,” Campbell said. “We’re not going to have him here today. Just going to let him kind of recover a little bit. So, we think he’ll be okay. He’s just going to need a minute here. It’s just one of those freak things. Somehow a hand gets through the face mask. It was unbelievable.” Generally, the outlook sounds good for him. Unfortunately, the news was much worse for tight end Anthony Firkser, who broke his fibula, according to Campbell. The Lions have already placed him on injured reserve, so unless the Lions release him with an injury settlement, his season is over just two days after joining the Lions. In response to the injuries to Firkser and Kitselman, the Lions have signed Nick Muse and re-signed Zach Horton. Per Campbell, Keys suffered a hamstring injury on Monday. Campbell called it “a little bit of a hammy,” which seems to suggest it’s relatively minor in nature. Out, but working with trainers G Ben Bartch (undisclosed) TE Tyler Conklin (PUP, calf) Bartch continues to sit out during both individual and team drills, while getting some work with trainers. It’s unclear what is currently keeping him out of practice, but he’ll need to return to the field soon if he wants to legitimately enter the left guard competition. Conklin continues to work with trainers for nearly the entirety of practice. He appears to be nearing a return just in time, as Detroit’s tight end room is shorthanded. Left practice early LB Malcolm Rodriguez (ankle) Rodriguez left the field toward the end of practice and the Lions officially listed him with an ankle injury. After practice was over, he returned to the field to be with family with his left ankle mildly taped and was walking on the ankle comfortably.

title: Lions say Bijan Robinson extension ‘can’t hurt’ Jahmyr Gibbs contract talks
summary: On Tuesday morning, news broke that Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson had agreed to a three-year extension worth an average of $22.25 million per year, including $51 million guaranteed. That deal resets the running back market and turns eyes to Detroit Lions Jahmyr Gibbs, who is currently holding in from training camp while he […]
full_text: Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) on field after practice during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Monday, August 3, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co On Tuesday morning, news broke that Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson had agreed to a three-year extension worth an average of $22.25 million per year, including $51 million guaranteed. That deal resets the running back market and turns eyes to Detroit Lions Jahmyr Gibbs, who is currently holding in from training camp while he awaits a new deal. Minutes after the Robinson news broke, Lions coach Dan Campbell took the lectern for his daily training camp press conference and was asked if the Robinson development could help speed up the process for Gibbs. “I think it certainly’s not going to hurt,” Campbell said. “It’s not going to hurt, but we’ll see. I’m anxious to get Gibbs back out there. Every day that goes by, that’s another day that you feel like you miss with him and getting him out there with the guys and him doing his part. But, there again, it’ll get done when it gets done.” Gibbs spoke extremely briefly with reporters on Monday after practice and simply told them “time will tell” when a deal is done. Gibbs and Robinson were drafted in the same draft class, with Robinson being selected eighth overall while Gibbs was taken 12th. Here’s a side-by-side comparison of stats for both players through three seasons: Bijan Robinson: 805 rushes 3,910 rushing yards 4.9 YPC 25 rush TDs 198 catches 1,738 receiving yards 9 receiving TDs Jahmyr Gibbs: 675 rushes 3,580 rushing yards 5.3 YPC 39 rush TDs 181 catches 1,449 receiving yards 10 receiving TDs At this point, there haven’t been any hard reports on how close a Gibbs deal is to getting done, but some NFL insiders have speculated that it could get done within the next couple of weeks.

title: Tracking the Detroit Lions’ defensive roster bubble: Arise, Ahmed Hassanein
summary: Every week, we are tracking the Detroit Lions players on the roster bubble and offering our predictions for who is in and who is out. The Lions defensive roster bubble continues to grow with questions about injuries and a ton of moving parts in the secondary. Some situations are becoming a little clearer, while others […]
full_text: Detroit Lions edge Ahmed Hassanein(99) during OTAs at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Friday, May 29, 2026. | Junfu Han / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Every week, we are tracking the Detroit Lions players on the roster bubble and offering our predictions for who is in and who is out. The Lions defensive roster bubble continues to grow with questions about injuries and a ton of moving parts in the secondary. Some situations are becoming a little clearer, while others only seem to be getting more confusing. Here are the Pride of Detroit staff’s current predictions about the players on the defensive roster bubble. We’ll break down each position below the chart to explain the shifts in the depth chart. View Link Defensive end : Assumed in: Aidan Hutchinson, DJ Wonnum, Derrick Moore Ahmed Hassanein: 10 “IN” votes (up 7) Payton Turner: 1 vote (down 5) Anthony Lucas: 0 votes Arise, Ahmed Hassanein believers. The love for Hassanein’s attitude and potential has come together this camp for a very, very strong early performance for the second-year edge defender. He’s making plays on special teams, and has worked his way up to consistent second-team defensive reps. This can’t be a bad look, either: Saw Brad Holmes and Ahmed Hassanein talking after practice today and asked Hassanein about it. “I’m gonna do whatever it takes to prove you right,” Hassanein said he told Holmes. “You prove me right by doing what you’re doing. You’re a football player,” Holmes said to him. https://t.co/1Nx0KxI5ov pic.twitter.com/vd5v6Vgb3L — Colton Pouncy (@colton_pouncy) August 4, 2026 And with Payton Turner struggling to shake his reputation as injury-prone, this decision is starting to look easier and easier. Defensive tackle: Assumed in: Alim McNeill, Tyleik Williams, Levi Onwuzurike OFF BUBBLE WATCH: Jay Tufele (cut) Tyler Lacy: 11 “IN” votes (no change) Skyle Gill-Howard: 8 votes (down 1) Mekhi Wingo: 6 votes (up 3) Chris Smith: 4 votes (up 3) Tyre West: 0 votes (no change) Aidan Keanaaina: 0 votes (no change) Most of the movement here is in regard to the nose tackle position. Essentially, all of Jay Tufele’s votes prior to the start of training camp shifted to Chris Smith and Mekhi Wingo. Smith looks like the next guy up at nose tackle, but hasn’t stuck out early in camp. Wingo, however, continues to rep with the first and second-team defenses when Alim McNeill needs a break. The fact that he is repping ahead of a guy like Levi Onwuzurike is notable, but we’re not yet ready to put Onwuzurike on the roster bubble. Linebacker: Assumed in: Jack Campbell, Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez NEW TO ROSTER BUBBLE: Jimmy Rolder (injury) NEW TO ROSTER BUBBLE: Joe Bachie NEW TO ROSTER BUBBLE: Devin White (signed) Trevor Nowaske: 10 “IN” votes ( up 1) Damone Clark: 10 votes (up 1) Devin White: 6 votes Troy Reeder: 4 votes (up 4) Jimmy Rolder: 3 votes Erick Hunter: 1 vote (no change) The Jimmy Rolder injury has caused some massive shifts here. Campbell said the injury wasn’t significant, but he’ll be out for “a while.” Seems like the most likely scenario is he goes on injured reserve when the cutdowns start, meaning he’ll be OUT and miss at least the first four games. Still, three staffers are holding out hope he avoids IR. Rolder’s votes from last week have been spread across the room, with newly signed Devin White getting the biggest jump. About half of the staff thinks he’s in, but Troy Reeder and Damone Clark have a little more belief, as well. Cornerback: Assumed in: DJ Reed, Rock Ya-Sin, Ennis Rakestraw, Roger McCreary, Keith Abney Khalil Dorsey: 8 “IN” votes (down 2) Nick Whiteside: 6 votes (up 5) I’m dangerously close to putting Roger McCreary on the roster bubble due to the rise in Nick Whiteside. Whiteside’s play has been undeniable, but it’s really challenging to find a way to put him on the roster. Reed, Ya-Sin, Rakestraw, and Abney all feel pretty safe. Khalil Dorsey may be the best special teamer on the roster, which makes it hard to put Whiteside above him. Meanwhile, McCreary is on a one-year, minimum salary contract with just $800,000 guaranteed. I’ve still got him as an assumed in, but with the growing support around Whiteside, I think next week we may need to pull him down to the bubble. As Dan Campbell said on Monday, the cornerback room is about to get interesting. Safety Assumed in: Christian Izien NEW TO BUBBLE WATCH: Kerby Joseph NEW TO BUBBLE WATCH: Brian Branch Avonte Maddox: 11 “IN” votes (no change) Thomas Harper: 11 votes (no change) Chuck Clark: 11 votes (no change) Kerby Joseph: 4 votes Brian Branch: 4 votes Dan Jackson: 1 vote (up 1) Loren Strickland: 0 votes (no change) We are no longer assuming that Kerby Joseph is “IN” nor that Brian Branch is “OUT.” Dan Campbell dropped the bombshell last week that Branch could return to the practice field as early as the end of training camp, which would lead to him avoiding the PUP to start the season. But Campbell also said that they are not expecting Joseph to be ready by Week 1, which was just as big of a surprise. Detroit is going to face a very difficult decision with both players on whether they should start the season on PUP, and as you can see, the POD staff is split on what they’re going to do. Oddly, that hasn’t changed much about the rest of the room, as staffers have used the extra votes elsewhere on the roster. That said, Clark and Maddox are getting very close to moving off the roster bubble. Given that they’ve taken nearly every first-team rep in camp, it seems unlikely Detroit will change course. But we’ll see as camp continues.

title: Who will be in the Detroit Lions’ starting secondary in Week 1?
summary: Going into Detroit Lions training camp, one of the biggest questions was: how will the secondary shake itself out? There were—and still are—a ton of questions among the defensive backs that have left people both curious and concerned. The sudden fall of Terrion Arnold left the outside cornerback position thin and questionable. The unclear injury […]
full_text: Detroit Lions cornerback D.J. Reed (4), center, practices next to cornerback Rock Ya-Sin (23) and cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (2) during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, July 30, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Going into Detroit Lions training camp, one of the biggest questions was: how will the secondary shake itself out? There were—and still are—a ton of questions among the defensive backs that have left people both curious and concerned. The sudden fall of Terrion Arnold left the outside cornerback position thin and questionable. The unclear injury timelines for Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph made predicting the Week 1 starters challenging. Detroit also added a handful of new pieces—Roger McCreary, Keith Abney, Christian Izien, and Chuck Clark—who could all challenge for a significant role on this defense. But we now have about a week’s worth of information from training camp. Be it the play on the field or comments from coaches and players, we’ve got a somewhat better picture of what Detroit’s secondary may look like when they kick off the season against the New Orleans Saints. So today’s Question of the Day is: Who will be part of the Lions’ starting secondary in Week 1? My answer: Let’s start at the safety position. At this point, I think it’s fair to say that Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph are unlikely to be ready at the start of the season. Don’t get me wrong, there are seriously promising signs that Branch will return earlier than initially expected , and Joseph is going through some pretty intense workouts with trainers. However, coach Dan Campbell said they aren’t expecting Joseph to be out there in Week 1 , and he said Branch is on a very similar timeline. So while I think those players could be ready by Week 2-4, I remain doubtful for the season opener. In training camp, the Lions haven’t wavered in their replacements for the two. It’s been Chuck Clark and Avonte Maddox almost exclusively. It’s clear Detroit likes having experienced, trustworthy veterans on the backend, and defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard explained why: “As far as bringing in veteran guys, who understand what we’re looking for as far as disguising. That’s where we’re trying to get to now as a defense. I told them it’s time to go to the next level guys. The quarterbacks in thisleague are too good now. So, it’s all about lying to them. You have got to be liars on defense. You have got a lot of that guy with the green dot on offense. Pre-snap, he has to see something and then post-snap, that picture has to change or else you’re sitting duck. And, these guys have done these things. They understand the why behind it.” So, injuries pending, I think Clark and Maddox are the Lions’ starting safeties in Week 1. As for the cornerback situation, it’s a little more muddled. While I do think D.J. Reed and Rock Ya-Sin have separated themselves early in training camp, things get a lot more complicated when you start talking about the nickel spot. Ennis Rakestraw has seen plenty of first-team reps at outside corner and nickel, but I don’t think he’s exactly stood out yet. Roger McCreary has also gotten a ton of reps as the first-team nickel. But the wild card here is Christian Izien. He missed the first three practices, but then Campbell revealed the original plan was for him to start as the No. 1 nickel. He’s just now getting started in camp, and he’s already starting to command some first-team nickel reps. If he wins that job, do McCreary and/or Rakestraw move more predominantly to the outside corner position and contend for a starting job there? Of course, I can’t completely count out Nick Whiteside, either. He’s made more plays than anyone in training camp, albeit with the second and third-team defenses. He got extremely high praise from Dan Campbell on Monday, and Detroit has a history of being a meritocracy. Doesn’t matter when you were drafted. Doesn’t matter how much you’re getting paid. If you produce, you’ll play. And if Whiteside can continue this crazy start to camp—and do so against starting-level competition—he could win this job. Ultimately, though, I think the starting secondary looks like this in Week 1: CB1: D.J. Reed CB2: Rock Ya-Sin NB: Christian Izien S: Chuck Clark S: Avonte Maddox Now, it’s time for you to make your predictions. summary: The Green Bay Packers announced on Tuesday that they have officially waived tight ends Luke Lachey and RJ Maryland with injury designations. These moves were expected, as Lachey ended up finishing Monday’s practice on a scooter and in a boot, and Maryland injured his hamstring prior to the practice. Neither was seen at Tuesday’s practice, […]
full_text: ASHWAUBENON, WISCONSIN - JULY 31: RJ Maryland #48 of the Green Bay Packers looks on during the Green Bay Packers training camp at Ray Nitschke Field on July 31, 2026 in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers announced on Tuesday that they have officially waived tight ends Luke Lachey and RJ Maryland with injury designations . These moves were expected, as Lachey ended up finishing Monday’s practice on a scooter and in a boot, and Maryland injured his hamstring prior to the practice. Neither was seen at Tuesday’s practice, following the signings of McCallan Castles and Drew Biber . For the most part, the Packers have avoided major injuries, outside of the tight end position, in training camp. Unfortunately, Tucker Kraft (ACL) and Luke Musgrave (neck) are banged up and out of team drills (Musgrave is still on the PUP list and has yet to practice). On top of that, the team initially signed a UDFA tight end alongside Maryland, Eni Falayi, but Falayi failed his physical upon reporting to camp. For perspective, Maryland signed with Green Bay for $15,000 guaranteed, and Falayi was offered a contract that would have paid him $125,000 had he cleared his physical . Lachey also failed his physical when the Packers initially tried to claim him off waivers earlier this offseason (he had an unrelated hamstring issue), but was only re-signed once he was healthy. So if you’re counting at home, that’s six injuries or failed physicals for five Green Bay tight ends. Less than great. Over the last week, the Packers have signed three players at tight end: Castles, Biber and international exemption Thomas Yassmin. They worked out six players at the position last week, including the three that they’ve signed. The current tight end room healthy enough to practice in team drills for Green Bay right now is: Josh Whyle (2025 practice squad call-up) Drake Dabney (2025 practice squadder, signed in Week 10) Messiah Swinson (2025 practice squadder, signed in the postseason) McCallan Castles (signed during camp) Drew Biber (signed during camp) Thomas Yassmin (signed during camp) If the starters play in the preseason, you might get some names you don’t know playing premium tight end snaps for the first-team offense. Immediately, Castles, who was let go by Green Bay pre-draft, jumped in with the second-team offense on Tuesday. The Packers need all the help they can get at the position.

title: Jordan Love named top-10 quarterback by NFL coaches, executives
summary: For almost a decade, The Athletic has been running a series where they ask 50 NFL coaches and executives how they feel about quarterbacks, forcing them to rank signal-callers into tiers so the publication can average out the numbers into rankings. In this year’s edition of Mike Sando’s rankings, Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love […]
full_text: ASHWAUBENON, WISCONSIN - JULY 31: Jordan Love #10 of the Green Bay Packers looks on during the Green Bay Packers training camp at Ray Nitschke Field on July 31, 2026 in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images For almost a decade, The Athletic has been running a series where they ask 50 NFL coaches and executives how they feel about quarterbacks, forcing them to rank signal-callers into tiers so the publication can average out the numbers into rankings. In this year’s edition of Mike Sando’s rankings , Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love finally cracked the league’s top-10 passers for the first time. Below are Sando’s quarterback rankings of the NFL’s first two tiers of quarterbacks, which, again, are the opinions of NFL coaches and executives. Tier 1 1: Patrick Mahomes t-2: Josh Allen t-2: Matthew Stafford 4: Joe Burrow Tier 2 5: Lamar Jackson 6: Justin Herbert 7: Dak Prescott t-8: Drake Maye t-8: Jared Goff 10: Jordan Love t-11: Brock Purdy t-11: Caleb Williams 13: Jayden Daniels t-14: Baker Mayfield t-14: Sam Darnold 16: Trevor Lawrence 17: Jalen Hurts Love received two Tier 1 votes, 37 Tier 2 votes and 11 Tier 3 votes. Every season that he’s been a starter, more and more NFL voters buy into the idea of him being a Tier 2 quarterback. Overall, he moved up three spots from last year’s rankings, passing Jayden Daniels, C.J. Stroud, Jalen Hurts and Baker Mayfield, but was passed by Drake Maye, too. Below are some quotes that coaches and executives had for Sando about Love’s game: “He’s good — I was surprised,” an opposing defensive coordinator said. “Really solid, mobile, threw with better accuracy than I thought. I’d give him a 2.” … “Smart, can do things at the line, has the arm talent, the mobility when he needs it, but knows how to sit in and deliver,” another defensive coordinator said. “Not a consistent killer yet, but if he plays good ball, you can win a Super Bowl with him.” … “There are years where I could have pushed Love up to the bottom of Tier 1, top of Tier 2,” another defensive coach said. “He needs more consistency, week-in and week-out. He has some WTF plays and throws, like, ‘Why are you doing this?’” … “He is still coming into his own as a player,” another defensive coordinator said. “Early on, he was trying to be Aaron Rodgers. You could tell from his mannerisms: too cool for school. I think he is starting to settle into who he really is. He has the size, the length, all the tools.” … “If you can create pressure on him and make him move around, it ain’t the same,” an exec placing Love in Tier 3 said. “It took Aaron Rodgers three years to learn how to manipulate the pocket. Brett just did it. The question is, can Love learn it?” … “I used to think Josh Allen was a 2 because he just does too much where I go, ‘OK, it’s not by the book, it doesn’t always look the way it is supposed to, but God, is it productive,’” an offensive coach said. “Jordan Love is the Tier 2 version of that. He is at times careless and overly aggressive. It looks like it shouldn’t be working, and he’s getting away with things. “But he’s always getting away with them, so at some point, I just have to tip my cap and be impressed.” Personally, I’m still taking Love over Jared Goff, who is 1st in the NFL in EPA/dropback from a clean pocket but 28th in the NFL when pressured (out of 32 qualifiers) over the last three seasons. Love is sixth in both categories, for what it’s worth. To me, Goff absolutely needs a good offensive line to make things work, or it can get real ugly. At least I get the arguments for the likes of Maye or Justin Herbert off physical ability, but ranking Goff over Love seems incorrect to me at this point. — What do you guys think? Is Love ranked too high or too low? Did the NFL get it right? Let us know in the comments section.

title: Packers Training Camp: Jordan Morgan looks like a starting left tackle
summary: The Green Bay Packers have not yet announced whether the team will or won’t stream its Family Night practice on Packers.com, as they did last year. Before last summer, you were only able to watch the Packers’ Lambeau Field scrimmage on the Packers TV Network stations in Wisconsin, Minnesota, Iowa and Alaska. If you are […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - JANUARY 10: Jordan Morgan #77 of the Green Bay Packers runs across the field during an NFC Wild Card Playoff game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on January 10, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers have not yet announced whether the team will or won’t stream its Family Night practice on Packers.com, as they did last year. Before last summer, you were only able to watch the Packers’ Lambeau Field scrimmage on the Packers TV Network stations in Wisconsin, Minnesota, Iowa and Alaska. If you are out of market and want to get a look at the Packers in a team setting, this would be your one opportunity before the preseason, as Green Bay has cracked down on video of team drills progressively. Hopefully, you all can get a look at a Packers practice with your own eyes before a backup-heavy preseason starts. Anyways, here’s what you missed from practice on Tuesday, if you weren’t there in-person. Injuries The reserve list remains the same, as running back Chris Brooks (hamstring, NFI), tight end Luke Musgrave (neck, PUP), defensive lineman Javon Hargrave (knee, PUP), defensive lineman Jordon Riley (Achilles, PUP), edge rusher Micah Parsons (knee, PUP) and long snapper Matt Orzech (calf, PUP) remain out of practice. Beyond those players, cornerback Carrington Valentine (hamstring) and safety Jonathan Baldwin (undisclosed injury) also missed practice on Tuesday with injuries. The Packers signed tight ends McCallan Castles and Drew Biber to help them during this period where their tight ends have been banged up, and neither RJ Maryland nor Luke Lachey were seen at practice today, so Maryland and Lachey are presumed to have been waived injured in order to make room for the additions of Castles and Biber. Green Bay’s roster was full going into today, so corresponding roster moves needed to be made. Offense Jordan Morgan just showed why his athleticism is suited for left tackle. Beat Lukas Van Ness on first three 1v1 reps. 1) Stood up Van Ness on bull 2) Ushered Van Ness outside on speed 3) Mirrored Van Ness on inside out move Good start for Jordan Love’s new blindside blocker. — Ryan Wood (@ByRyanWood) August 4, 2026 For those of you who are worried about Jordan Morgan’s transition to left tackle, the news has been quiet on the Morgan front this summer (usually a good sign for offensive linemen), but he did stand out today. Tuesday’s practice was one-on-one heavy compared to other practices, probably a result of the Packers finally being in full pads for a second practice. In one-on-one drill, Morgan looked the part of a starting left tackle. Morgan, Burton, rhyan, Monk and Belton is the OL today. — Bill Huber (@BillHuberNFL) August 4, 2026 McDuffie and Cox all over a run by Strong. Forced inside by the corners and safeties flying to the ball. Second series of offense is back to the normal OL of Morgan – Monk – Rhyan – Belton – Kinnard Love to Jacobs on a bootleg throwback screen for a really nice gain. — Andy Herman (@AndyHermanNFL) August 4, 2026 Aaron Banks and Zach Bako-Bewele (formerly Tom) continue to rehab their knee injuries, so they only go through individual drills right now and sit out competitive and team periods. Because of that, the Packers have needed replacements at left guard and right tackle in camp. Generally, the answer has been for Jacob Monk to play left guard and Darian Kinnard to play right tackle, but the team rolled with rookie Jager Burton, who injured his hamstring on the first day of camp, and Anthony Belton, who usually plays right guard, at those positions to open up the team period on Tuesday. Monk slid in as Belton’s replacement at right guard. In the team’s second series, though, it was back to Belton at right guard, Monk at left guard and Kinnard at right tackle. Either way, it seems pretty clear that the Packers’ top eight offensive linemen are Morgan, Banks, Sean Rhyan, Belton, Bako-Bewele, Kinnard, Monk and Burton. Green Bay will likely roster 10 offensive linemen (maybe even 11) on their initial 53-man roster, so the final two spots are really what’s up for grabs right now. Barryn Sorrell reads the screen perfectly and intercepts Jordan Love for a PICK 6. Very, very good day for 99 — weston hodkiewicz (@WesHod) August 4, 2026 Quarterback Jordan Love threw his first interception of training camp yesterday after staying clean for several practices, but today he added to the interception tally as he threw a pick-six to edge rusher Barryn Sorrell on a throwback screen intended for running back Josh Jacobs. Hey, this is what camp is for, right? Defense Good start by Cisse in the one-on-ones. Three targets, zero catches. — Bill Huber (@BillHuberNFL) August 4, 2026 While the pecking order at cornerback has pretty consistently stayed Keisean Nixon, Carrington Valentine, Brandon Cisse and then Benjamin St-Juste, Cisse is making some plays. As Sports Illustrated’s Bill Huber noted, Cisse didn’t allow a catch in his first three one-on-one looks, a drill that favors the offensive side of the ball. Don’t look now but Anthony Campbell with a strong debut in one on ones against two blue chips in Belton and Burton. Period belonged to Warren Brinson who was a force on his three reps vs Belton, Barrett and then Rhyan. Jordan Morgan and LVN were featured matchup. Morgan looked… — weston hodkiewicz (@WesHod) August 4, 2026 If there has been any “riser” in training camp so far, it’s probably defensive lineman Anthony Campbell, who has been a pass breakup monster at the line of scrimmage. He looked good in one-on-ones today. There’s a chance he could push Nazir Stackhouse for a roster spot, as the Packers will likely keep six interior defensive linemen on their roster now that they’ve transitioned to a 3-4 defense. Two quick pash rush wins for McClellan in the opening team period. — Paul Bretl (@Paul_Bretl) August 4, 2026 Second-year Warren Brinson and rookie third-round pick Chris McClellan also made some plays today. Hopefully that’s a good sign for the defensive side of the ball and not a bad sign about the Packers’ interior offensive line situation. Special Teams 1st punt unit: Whelan, Adomitis, Bullard, Niemann, Hopper, McDuffie, Sorrell, Strong Jr., Mosby. Gunners working separately. — Carter (@cmsemb) August 4, 2026 We’ve already had looks at the team’s preferred gunners and shield players on punt team, but it is worth noting that the preferred “offensive line” on the punt unit is linebacker Ty’Ron Hopper, linebacker Isaiah McDuffie, edge defender Barryn Sorrell and edge defender Aaron Mosby. Usually, Nick Niemann helps out on the line of scrimmage, not as part of the shield (usually a spot reserved for safeties and running backs). It’s going to be tough to keep Mosby rostered on the 53, considering how many bodies are ahead of him on the defensive depth chart. Don’t be surprised if Mosby makes the practice squad and is brought up at some point in-season, which has pretty much been the norm for his run in Green Bay. Lukas Van Ness has been a starting “lineman” on the punt unit throughout his NFL career, but it looks like now that he’s graduated into a starting role on defense, he’s no longer a preferred player there. That begs this question: Is it really a smart idea for Sorrell to be the starter opposite of LVN, which has been the case throughout camp, when he’s starting defensive drives after sprinting 40 yards downfield on the punt team? I’m not sure, but this is the trouble you run into when your tight ends off the bench aren’t blocking tight ends, the other body type that can contribute at these positions.
