 Falcons running back Bijan Robinson returned to practice after a five-day hold-in Tuesday. Robinson got a three-year extension worth up to $75 million and is now the highest-paid running back in the NFL.

 Head coach Kevin Stefanski referred to Robinson's hold-in as "very amicable." Robinson had been at every practice on the hip of running backs coach Michael Pitre prior to actually coming back.

 "He wants to be out there practicing," Falcons running back Brian Robinson Jr . said. "You know he wants to be competing. So, I used to just tell him, 'Yo, take your time, handle your business. Whenever your time comes, it's going to come. I know you want to be out there with us, but we going to hold it down until you come back.'"

 Bijan Robinson didn't do much Tuesday. He worked a bit with the running backs in individual drills and did a play-action drill after practice with quarterback Michael Penix Jr . Pitre said they will work to ramp Bijan up over the next few days based on recommendations by the training and medical staff.

 
 Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa (tight back) said he continues to make progress and expected to be practicing fully Wednesday. Tagovailoa has eased into 11-on-11 sessions the last two days, but has only thrown seven passes. He was 3-of-4 in 11s on Tuesday. 
 Quarterback Cooper Rush , who signed with the Falcons last Wednesday, got reps with the first-team offense in a two-minute drill near the end of practice. Penix has still not yet been cleared for 11s, but got reps again in 7-on-7 work Tuesday. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa participated in 11-on-11 team sessions Monday for the first time this training camp. Tagovailoa has been dealing with a tight back and was still limited. He did two series, going 3-for-3 passing in 11s with individual drills, as well.

 Michael Penix Jr . (right knee) had his best 7-on-7 session Monday, going 6-of-8 with two drops, working mostly with younger players and reserves. His best throw of camp came on the final play of practice. Penix found  Antwane Wells Jr . for a long touchdown pass down the left side.

 Penix has still not been cleared for 11s. The majority of those reps still went to Jack Strand , followed by veteran Cooper Rush . Strand was 7-of-11 passing in those sessions, while Rush was 3-of-7.

 More observations: 

 
 Defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich returned to practice Monday. Ulbrich's wife Cristina died last week after a battle with cancer. "He's a father figure, older brother for me," Falcons linebacker Divine Deablo said. "So, I was glad to have him back out here. I hugged him as soon as I seen him. Everybody just wants to play for 'Brich' at the end of the day." 
 This was the first camp practice with pads. 
 Offensive tackle Wanya Morris and defensive tackle  Da'Shawn Hand  both left practice with apparent injuries. 
 Michael Jerrell , Brandon Walton and rookie seventh-round pick Ethan Onianwa  rotated at right tackle. Free agent signee Jawaan Taylor is not yet cleared to practice after elbow surgery last season. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Cooper Rush has only been with the Falcons for a little more than 72 hours, but he is starting to get himself acclimated fairly well.

 The veteran quarterback got reps with the first-team offense for the first time Saturday morning in 11-on-11 team sessions. Overall, Rush was 6-of-10 with a red zone touchdown to tight end  Kyle Pitts Sr .

 The Falcons signed Rush on Wednesday , just before their first practice of training camp. Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa is dealing with a tight back and has yet to do anything but individual work and a walk-through. Michael Penix Jr . is not yet cleared for 11s after right ACL surgery last November.

 Undrafted rookie Jack Strand has gotten the majority of 11-on-11 reps with the first team and still did Saturday. But Rush is clearly starting to ramp up.

 More observations:  

 
 Tagovailoa only did individual work, while Penix did individuals and then a 7-on-7 goal-line session. Penix was 4-of-8 passing, including a touchdown pass to rookie running back Cash Jones . 
 Christian Harris has gotten the vast majority of reps with the first-team defense at inside linebacker, alongside Divine Deablo . But rookie sixth-rounder Harold Perkins Jr . broke in with first-team reps. Stefanski said a rotation at that spot -- and many others -- will continue during camp. 
 

 

 

 Friday, July 31 
 Undrafted rookie quarterback Jack Strand is drawing raves from his teammates and coaches for how well he has performed after getting thrown into the proverbial fire.

 Strand has taken the majority of reps in 11-on-11 team sessions with Tua Tagovailoa (tight back) and Michael Penix Jr . (right knee) not fully cleared. On Friday, Strand was 7-of-8 passing in 11s and completed his first six passes.

 "Being a rookie, being able to come into a system like this where it's not easy to be able to regurgitate what he's getting told in the headset to the offense," Tagovailoa said. "I think he's done a really good job this offseason studying, understanding the playbook a bit. And you don't see that a lot in rookies, especially rookie quarterbacks."

 The 6-foot-4, 240-pound Strand, who played at Division II Minnesota State-Moorhead, has an impressive arm, as well.

 "Dude can sling the ball," Tagovailoa said.

 More observations: 

 
 The Falcons are battling through some tragic circumstances currently. Defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich's wife died earlier this week after battling cancer. The team made the information public Thursday night. Head coach Kevin Stefanski spoke to the media before practice Friday morning and said he would not discuss football until later. "Like any family, we will support Jeff and the kids and we'll put our arms around him and the kids literally, as an organization," Stefanski said. 
 Penix had a rough go in a 7-on-7 red zone drill. He was just 1-of-7 passing with one near interception by cornerback AJ Terrell. 
 
 

 Thursday, July 30 
 Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa was back at practice Thursday. Sort of.

 Tagovailoa (tight back) made a few throws during individual drills, but that was it. He did not participate in any team sessions, though he did remain on the field in full uniform.

 Michael Penix Jr ., not yet cleared for 11-on-11s, was also at practice, but he did not make any throws in practice, because it was a scheduled rest day, per a team source. There will be a few of those during training camp.

 The Falcons did not do any 7-on-7 drills on Thursday. Penix had been leading those.

 In 11s, undrafted rookie free agent Jack Strand got the majority of reps. He was backed up by veteran Cooper Rush , whom the Falcons signed Wednesday to add depth to their banged-up quarterback room.

title: Falcons extend Robinson, offensive core, put spotlight on QB
summary: Bijan Robinson, Drake London, Kyle Pitts and Matthew Bergeron have extensions, but they don't have a QB1 -- yet.
full_text:
New Atlanta Falcons general manager Ian Cunningham said at his opening news conference in February that he wants the organizational principle to be "draft, develop, retain."

 This offseason has put the emphasis on the latter -- retain -- perhaps more than any other offseason in franchise history.

 The Falcons signed All-Pro running back Bijan Robinson to a three-year contract extension Tuesday worth up to $75 million that makes him the highest-paid running back in NFL history. It was the latest big-money deal in a whirlwind two months in Atlanta.

 On June 8, the Falcons penned wide receiver Drake London to a four-year, $141 million extension. Three weeks later, tight end  Kyle Pitts Sr . was extended for three years and $54 million. And then, last Saturday, the Falcons upped the ante, extending left guard Matthew Bergeron for four years and $96 million.

 

 That's about $366 million put on the books over the past eight weeks. And a major signal that Cunningham, new coach Kevin Stefanski and new president of football Matt Ryan will build the future of the team around this young offensive core.

 Robinson is 24 years old. Pitts is still only 25, the same age as London. Bergeron is 26. That group will now likely remain together for at least the next three seasons, all with market-impacting deals.

 There are few surface questions about why the Falcons re-signed all four. Robinson is arguably the best running back in the NFL. He led the league in scrimmage yards (2,298) last season. Pitts was the second-most-productive tight end in the NFL last season after Trey McBride . London has consistently been a top-10-level receiver despite a revolving door at quarterback. Bergeron has been a starter since his first game.

 However, there is one extremely valid inquiry: Does it make sense to commit all that money to three skill players and an interior lineman when the future is very much uncertain at quarterback?

 Michael Penix Jr ., the No. 8 overall pick in 2024, is still working his way back after right ACL surgery last November. He has not yet been cleared for 11-on-11 team sessions in practice. The Falcons signed Tua Tagovailoa to a bargain deal -- one year, $1.3 million -- in the offseason to compete with Penix for the starting job. Tagovailoa himself has been dealing with a tight back and has been limited thus far in practice.

 

 The Falcons are hoping that one of the two emerges as the clear starter this month, though neither has gotten anywhere close to enough reps in practice to bear that out.

 "I don't care who your quarterback is," Stefanski said. "[Quarterbacks] want great players around them. It only makes their job easier."

 If Atlanta gets good quarterback play this season, it has the offensive players and a good enough defense to win the NFC South. That is an annual hope for a team that has not made the playoffs nor had a winning record in nine seasons. Since Ryan was traded in 2022, the Falcons have had five starting quarterbacks: Marcus Mariota , Desmond Ridder , Taylor Heinicke , Kirk Cousins and Penix. If Tagovailoa wins the starting job, the Falcons will have their sixth different Week 1 starter in as many seasons.

 Looking beyond this season, the Falcons will have Penix under contract for the 2027 season and then his fifth-year option season in 2028 if the team picks it up. At some point, a decision must be made on if the organization believes Penix can still be a franchise quarterback, but there is still a time to figure that out.

 If Tagovailoa wins the starting job and shows out, then the Falcons will have to make a big decision much sooner, because Tagovailoa is not under contract past 2026 and an impressive season will up his asking price considerably. Perhaps more than the Falcons would be willing to commit to given his past inconsistency.

 In any case, what the Falcons have done with extending this very good offensive core is give whoever ends up being the quarterback -- this year and in the future -- the best possible chance at success.

title: Tracking 2026 NFL hold-ins: Gibbs, Vea and Tuipulotu
summary: Here is the latest on Falcons' Bijan Robinson, Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs, Bucs' Vita Vea and Chargers' Tuli Tuipulotu.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL preseason kicks off with the Pro Football Hall of Game on Thursday , with three weeks of action to follow, but there are a handful of prominent players who are still not practicing because of their contract situations.

 The start of NFL training camps brought these negotiations to a head. Players can hold out and stay away from camp until their financial situations are addressed, or they can hold in, where they report to camp to avoid fines but skip practice while waiting for a new contract. We're tracking the important hold-ins across the league, with updates from our NFL Nation writers on each situation.

 The list of stars not practicing includes Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs ,  Tampa Bay Buccaneers defensive tackle Vita Vea  and  Los Angeles Chargers outside linebacker  Tuli Tuipulotu . 

 Which player will be next in resolving his contract dispute? Are any of these four willing to miss games once the season begins? Let's examine each situation.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Gibbs | Robinson | Vea | Tuipulotu 

 
 

 

 Jahmyr Gibbs , RB, Detroit Lions 
 

 Status: Holding in, seeking a new contract 

 Aug. 4 update:  Lions coach Dan Campbell said  Bijan Robinson 's record-setting deal with the Atlanta Falcons  is " certainly not gonna hurt " the team's contract negotiations with their own star running back, Gibbs. The Falcons and Robinson agreed to a three-year extension Tuesday that includes $51 million guaranteed, setting the stage for a new deal for Gibbs, who continues to hold in and miss practices at training camp. "[Robinson's deal is] not gonna hurt, but we'll see," Campbell said. "Look, I'm anxious to get Gibbs back out there."

 Aug. 3 update: Gibbs  missed his fifth consecutive practice Monday as his apparent hold-in continues while he looks to reach agreement on a new deal during training camp. However, the three-time Pro Bowler was spotted roaming the sidelines in a gray Lions cutoff hoodie for the second straight day at the Meijer Performance Center, often chatting with teammates Amon-Ra St. Brown , Jameson Williams and Jared Goff on the sideline in between drills. While leaving the field to enter the locker room alongside team security, Gibbs was briefly approached by reporters and stated that "only time will tell" when he returns in his first official comments on his absence from practice.

 

 Aug. 2 update: Gibbs was spotted on the sidelines Sunday, sporting a hoodie as he watched his teammates practice for the first time since training camp began. Gibbs has now missed his fourth consecutive practice as he seeks a contract extension. Lions WR Jameson Williams described Gibbs as "the best of the best" following practice as they were spotted communicating in between on-field drills. Williams feels Gibbs should be the NFL's highest-paid running back. "I wouldn't even say look at the stats, look at the film," Williams said. "Nobody close. He's the best."

 July 31 update: The Lions star missed his third day of practice as the hold-in continues. Coach Dan Campbell mentioned earlier this week that Gibbs was dealing with a "little bit of a back" issue during conditioning tests but clarified that it's nothing to worry about ahead of Friday's session. "No, I don't think it's severe," Campbell said. Gibbs, who is showing up at the team facility, has continued to communicate with teammates, such as wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown . "Obviously, we're missing one of our best players on offense, which sucks, but he's still in the building," St. Brown said. "He's still at all the meetings and everything. So, I think that the players understand what's going on. Everyone kind of gets it. It's part of this business, but we're still out there practicing, doing our thing."

 July 30 update:  The running back missed his second straight day of practice Thursday as the apparent hold-in continues until he reaches a new contract extension. Campbell addressed the situation ahead of Thursday's practice, saying that he is "not even sweating it" as both sides are working to secure a long-term deal. Gibbs did complete a conditioning test Wednesday in which Campbell said he "had a little bit of a back" issue, so it's unclear if Gibbs will start practicing right away once he inks a new deal.

 -- Eric Woodyard, Lions reporter 

 

 
 

 Bijan Robinson , RB, Atlanta Falcons 
 Status: Signed a new deal 

 Aug. 4 update:  The two-time Pro Bowler and the Falcons reached agreement on a three-year extension worth up to $75 million that now will make him the highest-paid running back in NFL history, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

 Aug. 1 update:  Robinson was again at practice, though not practicing, for the fourth straight day. Robinson left the field at one point during the media video shooting period and then came back when the cameras were off. Otherwise, he was with his teammates on the sidelines like he has been since camp started on Wednesday.

 July 31 update : Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski addressed Robinson's hold-in for the first time Friday morning. He said he was confident the contract situation will be resolved amiably.

 On how he is approaching the conflict, Stefanski said: "Just coach the football team."

 "Understand that there's a business side to everything we do and there's the football side and sometimes you're living in both worlds, if you will," Stefanski said. "But just going to continue to coach the football team."

 Robinson was once again in a jersey with no helmet or cleats for a third straight day. He was on the sideline encouraging teammates after plays. At the end of practice, he did pushups with his teammates who lost a drill.

 July 30 update: Robinson was a hold-in for a second straight practice Thursday. Like Wednesday, the team's first practice of training camp, Robinson was present on the field, chatting with teammates and seemingly in good spirits. He wore a Falcons jersey but had no helmet or cleats. Robinson and the Falcons have not commented on the situation, though coach Kevin Stefanski is likely to address it Friday morning.

 -- Marc Raimondi, Falcons reporter 

 

 
 

 Vita Vea , DT, Tampa Bay Buccaneers 
 

 Status: Holding in, requesting a trade 

 Aug. 2 update: The star defensive tackle remains sidelined with a back injury, as well as his contract hold-in. Coach Todd Bowles said there is "nothing new" to report on his injury, and he is unsure if Vea will make the trip to the  New York Jets  for a pair of joint practices starting Aug. 11.

 July 30 update: While Vea was on the sidelines during Wednesday's first training camp practice and was standing alongside teammates during positional drills, he was not on the practice field Thursday. Bowles said Vea tweaked his back in the team's conditioning test Tuesday and he was getting treatment. Vea did, however, participate in an interview on the "Up & Adams Show," but he did not discuss his contract. Vea is set to earn $17 million this season, but none of it is guaranteed, along with a per-game roster bonus that is capped at $1 million total. The Chargers, Tuipulotu, and his representation remain mum about Tuipulotu's absence from practice, though it appears to be contract-related. title: 2026 Baltimore Ravens training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Ravens training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Baltimore Ravens ' camp is taking place at Under Armour Performance Center in Baltimore, and Ravens reporter Jamison Hensley has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Ravens camp. We will update this file often. Can new coach Jesse Minter get  Lamar Jackson  and the Ravens to the Super Bowl? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Ravens camp 
 
 Zay Flowers, Ravens agree to four-year, $140M extension 
 Derrick Henry, entering 11th year, not thinking about retirement 
 Ravens waive rookie Diego Pavia to make room for Ethan Pocic 
 Ravens' Madubuike (neck) practices for 1st time in 10 months 
 
 
 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane has become the star of Ravens training camp.

 Early in team drills, Lane made an unbelievable one-handed grab along the sideline, which will go down as one of the best receptions in Ravens' camp history. After running a route to the right sideline, Lane had to reach back to catch Lamar Jackson 's 20-yard pass with his extended right hand while falling backward to the ground.

 "That was a great play by Ja'Kobi," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. "He's continued to flash and make those type of plays. As [for] anybody, you're always searching for consistency down after down. Again, the more he shows Lamar that he's making those types of plays, the more trust they build, and that's really what training camp and what practice is all about."

 

 Later, in one-on-one drills, Lane showed his playmaking ability again, using a double move to get behind cornerback T.J. Tampa and catching a long touchdown pass from Jackson.

 This has been an outstanding start to camp for Lane, a third-round pick from USC who has become the team's No. 3 wide receiver behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman . On Thursday, Lane first electrified the crowd by elevating over two defenders for a leaping, 30-yard catch over the middle.

 Other observations:  

 
 There was a brief scare when No. 1 cornerback Nate Wiggins leapt high to pick off Jackson and then landed hard on his back after safety Jaylinn Hawkins accidentally collided with him. Wiggins didn't move for a few minutes as trainers looked at him on the field. But Wiggins got back to his feet and continued to practice, saying he got the wind knocked out of him. 
 In one of the more unusual plays of camp, Jackson was intercepted by 310-pound defensive lineman David Olajiga , who had dropped back into coverage. But right tackle Roger Rosengarten made a heads-up play by knocking the ball away from Olajiga and forcing a fumble. 
 Reserve cornerback Amani Oruwariye picked off No. 3 quarterback Skylar Thompson with aggressive play. Oruwariye closed on tight end Ty Pezza and ripped the ball away. 
 
 
 Monday, Aug. 3 
 On Monday, Ravens defensive end Calais Campbell practiced for the first time since his personal tragedy this offseason.

 Last month, Campbell's brother was charged with murder after police found their 71-year-old mother dead at home in Atlanta during a welfare check. Campbell's family told police that his brother struggled with mental illness.

 'We're excited to work him in, start to ramp him into getting ready," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. "That'll be at a pace that's good for him."

 Campbell was not made available to reporters after practice. Last month, the Campbell family issued a statement asking for privacy while they deal with "overwhelming grief."

 Campbell's participation on Monday was limited to individual drills. The Ravens excused him from practicing for the first week of training camp.

 Campbell, 39, is entering his 19th NFL season after signing a one-year, $5.5 million contract with Baltimore in April.

 "He's a force multiplier of just how he operates and the wisdom that he brings," Minter said. "On top of, he's still a really high caliber player for his position."

 Other observations:  

 
 In the first padded practice of camp, first-round pick Olaivavega Ioane was looking to make a block downfield and he accidentally collided with running back Derrick Henry , which caused both of them to go to the ground. "Welcome to the league, huh," said Ioane, the Ravens' starting right guard. "Now I know to stay out of his way." 
 Offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford said it's going to take all of training camp for the Ravens to make a decision at starting center. Danny Pinter , Ethan Pocic and Jovaughn Gwyn are competing for that spot. "We want to make sure that we're diligent in giving everybody the opportunity that's here," Ledford said, "and just make sure we get the right guy that we want in there with that first group." 
 Pro Bowl defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike is sporting a new neck roll at practice. Madubuike, who is looking to come back from neck surgery, has suited up but has not participated in individual or team drills. Asked about the neck roll, Minter said, "Whatever makes the players feel their best and play with the most confidence -- it definitely looks like a little bit of a throwback." 
 In one-on-one drills against cornerbacks, rookie third-round pick Ja'Kobi Lane flashed again, beating Chidobe Awuzie and catching a deep pass on a fly route. Lane is off to a fast start to the second week of training camp after a strong first week. He is competing for Baltimore's No. 3 wide receiver spot. 
 Lamar Jackson and the Ravens offense had their most out of sync practice of camp. Jackson finished 6-of-14 passing (42.8%) after failing to complete his first five passes. He was trying to push the ball downfield more, so there wasn't as many high-percentage throws. 
 
 
 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Ravens kicker Tyler Loop took another step toward moving past last season's horrific finish by coming through under pressure on Saturday.

 Before 20,185 fans at the University of Maryland's SECU Stadium, Loop drilled a 43-yard kick to end practice, setting off a celebration among the players and earning a hug from quarterback Lamar Jackson . The players would have had to do 50 pushups if Loop had missed.

 "There's people here and there is something on the line," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. "It's hard to create those types of environment."

 It was about seven months ago when Loop missed a 44-yard field goal attempt in a 26-24 loss at the Pittsburgh Steelers that ended Baltimore's season. The Ravens have shown their confidence in Loop by not bringing in another kicker to compete against him.

 "He was a rookie. Things happen," Jackson said. "I know he has a lot of motivation in himself. We have all the trust and belief in him, as well."

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Lamar Jackson was 8-of-10 in limited work and threw his second interception of camp. Jackson was picked off by backup cornerback Keyon Martin , who has had a strong start to camp. "He's got a knack for the ball," Jackson said. "He's a guy who's hungry. He wants to be a difference-maker for the defense." 
 After three days of practice, Minter gave three veteran players the day off: running back Derrick Henry , offensive tackle Ronnie Stanley and outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson . 
 Minter said the Ravens' first padded practice will be Monday.

title: Proposing five big trades during 2026 NFL training camps
summary: NFL rosters are mostly locked in for 2026, but we crafted five potential win-win deals that teams should consider making before Week 1.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL season might be a little more than a month away, but rosters aren't locked in quite yet. Training camp brings hope, optimism and trade talks, which is what we're focusing on here. And there are still a few roster holes to be patched -- and some trade candidates who could be dealt to fill them. So, let's play matchmaker.

 I'm proposing five deals which would make sense for both sides considering each team's depth chart, contention horizon and salary cap, along with each player's ability and contract. Is this finally the moment when the Giants move on from edge rusher Kayvon Thibodeaux ? Could Kayshon Boutte find a new home after the Patriots' wide receiver acquisitions? And is there a star defender who would fit well with the 49ers?

 Let's dive in. Here are five trades that should happen before Week 1.

 

 
 Jump to a proposed trade involving: 
 Bates | Thibodeaux 
 Coleman | Little | Boutte 

 
 

 

 49ers get a defensive boost with Bates 
 49ers receive: S Jessie Bates III , 2028 sixth-round pick 
 Falcons receive: 2027 third-round pick

 The Falcons' 2023 signing of Bates was an example of free agency gone right. The Falcons paid sticker price -- four years and $64 million -- to sign Bates, who was very effective in Cincinnati and continued that quality play in Atlanta. That was particularly true in 2023, when Bates delivered six interceptions and three forced fumbles while earning second-team All-Pro honors.

 He was good again in 2024, but he wasn't quite on the same level last season. Still, the 29-year-old Bates remains one of the best safeties in the league. (He ranked fifth in this year's survey of coaches and executives conducted by ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.)

 

 If the Falcons were expected to contend, it would make sense to keep Bates and see the original contract through. But they aren't, and with a ton of 2027 cap space even after the  Bijan Robinson   extension , the Falcons will likely be spenders next offseason. They would risk losing Bates without getting a compensatory pick in return if he walks in free agency. So it's better for Atlanta to deal him now. And while that would mean finding a replacement for Bates, the Falcons wouldn't be lacking in safety talent thanks to emerging second-year player Xavier Watts .

 It just so happens that former Falcons head coach Raheem Morris, who coached Bates the past two seasons, is now the 49ers' defensive coordinator . And he could use an upgrade at safety alongside Ji'Ayir Brown and Malik Mustapha . The timing works, as the 49ers are contenders who could use defensive help after ranking 25th in EPA allowed per dropback last season.

 

 San Francisco would be giving up real draft capital for a rental player, but that's an indicator of Bates' skill and the fact that his contract would cost the 49ers only $13 million in 2026 -- a below-market price to sign a player of his caliber.

 
 

 Patriots satisfy the edge-rush need with Thibodeaux 
 Patriots receive: Edge  Kayvon Thibodeaux , 2027 fifth-round pick 
 Giants receive: 2027 third-round pick

 I included a Thibodeaux trade in this same story last year . One year and another first-round edge rusher later, he's now an even more obvious candidate to be dealt.

 Thibodeaux is playing on his $14.75 million fifth-year option and is set to be a free agent at the end of this season. While there was an argument for having him as a third edge rusher behind Brian Burns and Abdul Carter  in the past, New York now also has first-round pick Arvell Reese , who plays linebacker and edge. To keep Thibodeaux around at this price to potentially be the team's No. 4 edge rusher isn't ideal.

 So the Giants need to find a trade partner who:

 
 Has a need at edge 
 Has the cap room to take on Thibodeaux's 2026 contract 
 Is an immediate contender given his pending free agent status 
 
 The Patriots fit the bill and then some, because Thibodeaux offers long-term upside if New England decides to re-sign him. The Patriots' current edge rushers are Harold Landry III and Dre'Mont Jones . At this stage of their careers (Landry is 30, Jones 29), they're better fits as No. 2 and No. 3 edge rushers, respectively, on a contending team. Thibodeaux hasn't been good enough yet to be New England's unquestioned top edge rusher, but he possesses the promise to develop into that.

 Thibodeaux's 9.9% pass rush win rate at edge last season -- below average for the position -- was similar to what Landry (10.8%) and Jones (8.6%) posted. Thibodeaux had only 2.5 sacks last season in 10 games but has shown more in the past. In 2024, he recorded a 16.8% pass rush win rate at edge (16th best), and he recorded 11.5 sacks as a rookie in 2022. Thibodeaux is also solid in the run game, and his 27.9% run stop win rate at edge last season was above average for the position.

 Giants fans will likely feel like the team should get more in this deal. But it's all about the contract, as Thibodeaux has only one year left on his deal and is getting paid pretty close to what he would probably make on the open market.

 

 

 
 

 Colts give Coleman a fresh start 
 Colts receive: WR Keon Coleman , 2028 sixth-round pick 
 Bills receive: 2027 fourth-round pick

 Coleman was already a potential trade candidate before Bills owner Terry Pegula blamed the team's former coaching staff -- as opposed to the current front office -- for pushing to draft the wide receiver with the No. 33 pick in 2024. Coleman has struggled in two NFL seasons, but it was a fairly shocking insult toward a player still on the roster.

 Buffalo doesn't have to trade him, but between his on-field struggles and the negative vibes stemming from ownership's comments, it certainly could. And the Colts would be a logical candidate to bet on Coleman at a reduced cost.

 Coleman has recorded 1.65 yards per route run over 583 career routes, along with a 48-51-49 triple-slash of open, catch and YAC scores from ESPN's player-tracking based  receiver scores . Those numbers aren't great and aren't what the Bills hoped for when they drafted him, but they're not terrible either. He could still definitely be a contributing player to a winning team with some growth.

 Indianapolis needs receiver help. After being re-signed to a $28.5 million-per-year deal , Alec Pierce underwent  ankle surgery and is not yet back on the practice field. The Colts have the promising Josh Downs in the slot, but the depth chart on the outside behind Pierce is rough, with Nick Westbrook-Ikhine and Ashton Dulin the likely next options. The Colts could use another receiver regardless of Pierce's status, so taking a chance on Coleman's upside makes sense.

 

 The Jahan Dotson trade in 2024 , in which the Eagles sent a third-round pick and two seventh-rounders to the Commanders for Dotson and a fifth-rounder, is a useful comp. Like Coleman, Dotson was entering his third year after an uneven first two seasons. But Dotson was a higher draft pick (No. 16 vs. No. 33) and was better regarded than Coleman is now, which is why I think the latter would cost less to acquire.

 
 

 Cardinals get offensive line help with Little 
 Cardinals receive: OT Walker Little , 2027 seventh-round pick 
 Jaguars receive: 2027 sixth-round pick

 Little was Wally Pipped last year by Cole Van Lanen , who ascended into the starting lineup at left tackle after Little missed two games with a  concussion . The Jaguars kept Van Lanen at left tackle even after Little returned, then extended him in the offseason. That makes Little an expensive third tackle, due an almost fully guaranteed $11.5 million this season.

 

 Little had his best season in terms of pass block win rate in 2025 but was still only in the 27th percentile among tackles. While tackle depth is important, my guess is that the cap-strapped Jaguars would cut Little if his money weren't guaranteed. But it is. Dealing Little would be a cost-saving maneuver, so the compensation on any deal ought to be barely above -- maybe even…

title: 2026 Buffalo Bills training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Bills training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Buffalo Bills' camp is taking place at St. John Fisher University in Pittsford, New York, and Bills reporter Alaina Getzenberg has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Bills camp. We will update this file often. How will the transition to Jim Leonhard's defense go? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Bills camp 
 
 Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson carted off with leg injury 
 Josh Allen on Bills' alternate uniforms: 'Stop hating on the jerseys' 
 Bills unveil new 'Nickel City' alternate uniforms 
 2026 Buffalo Bills training camp preview 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 The Bills wore full pads during 11-on-11 drills for the first time in training camp. And with the pads came the fighting.

 Players had to be separated several times, with the back-and-forth talk starting between the offensive and defensive lines even before the team periods. One big altercation came when rookie inside linebacker Kaleb Elarms-Orr didn't realize the play was over and made contact with tight end Dalton Kincaid . The offense did not appreciate the late hit, and coach Joe Brady even had some words after the things calmed.

 One player who was consistently in the middle of the fighting and got involved in that one is offensive lineman Alec Anderson .

 "Well, I didn't enjoy hitting our guy after the whistle, but I enjoyed punching him in the face a couple times and choking him out," Anderson said. "So, that's always enjoyable."

 Veteran edge rusher  Bradley Chubb said that he loved the physicality the team brought.

 "You'd rather say chill than sic 'em," Chubb said. "So, when you got a team full of sic 'ems, that's a good thing. But at the end of the day, we got to make sure we channel our energy in the right place."

 More observations: 

 
 Quarterback Josh Allen and wide receiver DJ Moore connected for arguably the most eye-popping play of camp thus far. Allen found Moore deep downfield with three defenders -- cornerbacks Christian Benford and Maxwell Hairston and safety Cole Bishop -- trailing Moore. After it initially appeared Moore wouldn't catch up to the pass from Allen, the ball landed in the right spot for Moore to stretch out his arms midstride to bring it in. Fellow wide receiver Khalil Shakir said, "[Moore and Allen's] connection has been unreal" and that the play was so beautiful, it feels "fake." 
 
 

 
 Rookie edge rusher  TJ Parker was involved in the beginning of a skirmish. 
 Safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson (right calf strain) worked to the side early in practice. 
 DT Deone Walker  sat out a second straight practice after tweaking his elbow. He said that he was fitted for a brace Monday and hoping to be back practicing Thursday with the brace. 
 The top training camp battles continued to see rotations, including left guard (Anderson/ Austin Corbett ).﻿ 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 
 The rain poured down at St. John Fisher University for the third time in the Bills' four training camp practices. The difficult weather lasted the entirety of the team's first practice wearing pads -- which was short-lived.

 The team took off the pads before 11-on-11 drills got underway, another noticeable Joe Brady change.

 "Coming out the first day of pads, and everyone's just adjusting and kind of thinking about all the pads," Brady said. 
 
"Today's more of the intentionality of ... we're coming off an off day. Let's wake up with the mentality that we got to put our pads on. Let's get used to it."

 Tight end Dawson Knox said he appreciates Brady trying to see things from the player perspective.

 There was a hint of risk due to slippery grass. The concrete track surrounding the field wasn't far from where the players were working in the red zone. The team appeared to avoid any major injury.

 "It kind of brings you back to just kind of being a kid ... playing football with your friends in the rain," tight end Dalton Kincaid said. 
 
"Hoping for some sunshine ahead."

 More observations :

 
 Brady did not offer a timeline for safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson , who suffered a lower calf strain Saturday, to return but said the Bills were "fortunate" it was not a more severe injury. Gardner-Johnson was not present at Monday's practice. 
 Safety Damar Hamlin took first-team reps initially in Gardner-Johnson's absence and then veteran Geno Stone had some time with the unit as well. 
 Second-year defensive tackle Deone Walker did not participate in practice. He worked to the side with athletic trainers during the individual periods. 
 Tight end Dalton Kincaid went down during 11-on-11 drills and received attention from athletic trainers but said after practice that he got hit by a knee in the "family jewels" and is OK. 
 Inside linebacker Dorian Williams took part in team drills for the first time during camp. 
 
 
 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Despite  the injury suffered Saturday  to projected starting safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson , the Bills' defense showed it can still come together in the face of adversity.

 Inside linebacker Terrel Bernard made his camp debut Saturday in 11-on-11 drills, pairing with rookie linebacker Kaleb Elarms-Orr . Linebacker Dorian Williams has not progressed yet to 11-on-11 work but was alongside Bernard in 7-on-7 drills. Elarms-Orr has seen opportunities with the absences, but Bernard getting more reps is a sign the unit is moving forward.

 

 Rookie safety Jalon Kilgore remains further down the depth chart but continues to make plays, including an interception.

 When it comes to defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard putting his defense together, OLB  Bradley Chubb noted one thing that stands out.

 "The difference I've seen in him versus other DCs I've been with is, when we're installing, he's installing with the reason why we're installing. It's never just putting a play in just to put a play in," Chubb said. "Each play has a purpose, has a reason, and he tells exactly what he wants out of us in that play. And when you got a guy like that, it's easy to play for because you know where you stand."

 More observations: 

 
 Saturday featured the first sunny day of training camp practice and the longest session yet. The team huddled together before a final set of 11-on-11 drills to end the practice. 
 Wide receiver Joshua Palmer stretched to make a nice catch near the sideline, bringing in the ball midstride, on a pass from quarterback Josh Allen . Palmer ran the short distance remaining into the end zone and then punted the ball into the air in celebration. The receiver getting into a rhythm would be a positive for the Bills after Palmer dealt with injuries last season. 
 The running backs room -- James Cook III , Ty Johnson and Ray Davis -- has been noticeably more involved as pass catchers in practices, which is something to keep an eye on if that production increases this season. 
 The Bills had full attendance at practice. 
 

 
 Thursday, July 30 
 The budding relationship between quarterback Josh Allen and wide receiver DJ Moore was on display once again during the second practice of training camp.

 Moore, the team's biggest offseason acquisition, had highlight catches on both days of camp: a sideline diving grab during the first practice and a deep pass for a touchdown on Thursday. Moore is already getting No. 1 receiver-type treatment from Allen and the first-team offense. Moore described the first two days of camp with the 2024 MVP as "really good."

title: 2026 Carolina Panthers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our updates from Panthers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Carolina Panthers ' camp is taking place in Charlotte, North Carolina, and we'll have the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Panthers camp. We will update this file often. Will QB Bryce Young and the Panthers take another step forward after making the playoffs in 2025? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 Legette suffers apparent stinger, avoids concussion 
Panthers wide receiver Xavier Legette suffered a "stinger" on a hard fall during Tuesday's practice, according to coach Dave Canales , who added that the third-year player does not have a concussion.
 Legette was trying to make a catch in the corner of the end zone when he came down hard on the back of his head. Trainers rushed to his side and Legette was later seen wiggling his fingers in the air in front of trainers before boarding a cart.

 It was the latest scare in what has been an injury-riddled start to training camp for the Panthers, who have already lost starting linebacker Nic Scourton and rookie wide receiver Chris Brazzell II for the season. Read more 

 
 

 Pickett to start Thursday's preseason game 
 Panthers quarterback Kenny Pickett will start Thursday night's Pro Football Hall of Fame Game against the Arizona Cardinals  ( 8 p.m. ET, NBC ), per ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter . Pickett, No. 2 on the depth chart behind  Bryce Young , will lead a Carolina team that doesn't plan to play any of its starters Thursday night, including rookie offensive tackle  Monroe Freeling .

 Panthers coach Dave Canales added Pickett, 28, to develop behind Young, the No. 1 pick of the 2023 draft. Pickett replaced 38-year-old Andy Dalton , who was traded in March to the Philadelphia Eagles for a 2027 seventh-round draft pick. -- ESPN Staff 

 
 Panthers VP says decision on Young deal 'collaborative' 
 The Panthers remain tight-lipped about the long-term contractual future of quarterback  Bryce Young  as he prepares to enter his fourth NFL season.

 Panthers executive vice president of football operations Brandt Tilis said Monday he felt Young "ascended" to a new level last season, while adding that the 25-year-old's ceiling is still "unknown."

 After being benched early in his second season, the No. 1 overall pick in 2023 responded by throwing for 3,011 yards with 23 touchdowns and 11 interceptions last year while going 8-8 as a starter and leading the Panthers to an NFC South championship. Read more 

 
 Fans show up for scrimmage; injuries cast a shadow 
The Panthers scrimmaged in front of approximately 40,000 fans at Bank of America Stadium on Friday night in their first appearance on their home turf since losing in the opening round of last season's playoffs. Injuries continue to be the story of the team's training camp with three other players kept out of the action.
 Tight end Tommy Tremble , defensive tackle Derrick Brown and linebacker Devin Lloyd all sat out.

 Coach Dave Canales said after the scrimmage that Tremble had "general soreness" in his right knee on which he wore a sleeve on Friday night, and Brown and Lloyd were taking their regularly scheduled "veteran days." Read more 

 

 
  Panthers WR Chris Brazzell to have season-ending knee surgery 

 After suffering a moderate lateral collateral ligament tear in his left knee in practice Wednesday, the team announced Thursday that  Chris Brazzell II  will undergo season-ending surgery. 

 The injuries are beginning to pile up in Carolina, and the third-round pick out of Tennessee is just the latest one. Read more 

 

 Rookie WR Chris Brazzell suffers LCL tear 
 Panthers rookie receiver Chris Brazzell II suffered a moderate lateral collateral ligament tear in his left knee in practice Wednesday and is expected to be sidelined for up to eight weeks, a league source told ESPN, confirming a report by The Athletic.

 The injury came on a noncontact play. Brazzell, who is competing for the Panthers WR3 role, will seek a second opinion.

 Brazzell, selected in the third round out of Tennessee by the Panthers this year, had missed two practices earlier this week because of soreness in that knee. Read more 

 
 TE Evans carted off during camp practice 
 Panthers second-year tight end  Mitchell Evans  was carted off the field on Tuesday with an ankle injury.

 Panthers coach Dave Canales said after practice that Evans got rolled up on and that the initial diagnosis indicates the injury is not viewed as serious.

 "They [the medical staff] are pretty optimistic," Canales said. "But we're going to do a full evaluation just to make sure there's nothing happening in there. ... I'll give you more information as we do the full evaluation." Read more 

 
 Panthers make three roster moves 
 Carolina on Saturday, July 25, signed defensive tackles Kyon Barrs and Elijah Garcia , and cornerback DeCarlos Nicholson , according to the team . All three players took part in a workout Friday.

 To make room for the three players on the Panthers roster, the team announced it waived tackle Derrell Bailey Jr. , linebacker Jared Bartlett , and cornerback Michael Reid .

 

 
 LB Scourton placed on injured reserve after knee injury 
 The Panthers have placed second-year outside linebacker Nic Scourton on injured reserve after he suffered a right knee injury during the first day of training camp Thursday.

 Scourton suffered a torn ACL in the knee, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Cameron Wolfe.

 It's a huge blow for the Panthers, who were counting on Scourton to be a top pass rusher opposite free agent addition Jaelan Phillips . Read more 

 

 
 David Tepper invests another $500M into stadium renovation 
 Panthers owner David Tepper is investing an additional $500 million into ongoing stadium renovations to improve overall fan experience with an eye toward potentially bringing the Super Bowl, NFL draft, 2031 Women's World Cup and other major sporting events to Charlotte, North Carolina.

 The investment coincides with the team announcing it has reached a long-term extension on a stadium naming rights deal Thursday with Bank of America. Read more 

 

 
 RT Moton sidelined indefinitely with blood clot in lung 
 Panthers starting right tackle Taylor Moton was diagnosed with a blood clot in his lung late last month and will miss regular-season time, the team announced Tuesday.

 Moton was placed on the non-football injury list along with cornerback Jaycee Horn before the start of training camp. Horn has a cut on his foot that required stitches but is expected to be activated early during training camp, the team said.

 Moton was placed on blood thinners after his diagnosis and is responding well to that treatment. He is being assessed daily by the Panthers' medical staff.  Read more 

 
 

 Panthers training camp preview 
 The Panthers are heading into the 2026 season as the reigning NFC South champions after finishing in a three-way tie at 8-9 last season. The division feels wide open for the taking again after several seasons of lackluster finishes (the last runaway winner of the division was the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2021).

 The Panthers, behind Young and coach Dave Canales, will be attempting to not only stay in the playoff mix again, but they're looking for their first winning season since 2017 as well. Read more

title: 2026 Chicago Bears training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Bears training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Chicago Bears ' camp is taking place in Lake Forest, Illinois, and Bears reporter Courtney Cronin has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Bears camp. We will update this file often. Will the defense step up and lead the Bears back to the NFC North title? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Bears news 
 
 New Bears safety Coby Bryant out 8-10 weeks with injury 
 Bears CB Johnson views 2026 as 'definitely a contract year' 
 Ben Johnson: Bears motivated to spurn 'regression' label 
 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 After the offense got off to a fast start during the Bears' first week of training camp, the defense has caught up and set the tone the last two days.

 Tuesday's two-hour practice featured a heavy dose of 11-on-11 periods and live tackling. The emphasis was on 13 personnel (3 TE, 1 WR, 1 RB), which leant itself to the offense establishing the run game early on.

 But the offense looked the sloppiest it has during any of the team's first six practices. There were dropped passes, pre-snap penalties and timing issues between quarterback Caleb Williams and his receivers.

 During the final period, the first-team offense began on its own 47-yard line trailing 28-23 with 54 seconds on the clock. After back-to-back false starts, Williams found himself being chased down by linebacker Devin Bush , who blitzed off the edge.

 Williams had three straight completions to Luther Burden III , Colston Loveland and Kalif Raymond but could not finish the drive in the end zone.

 With 3.2 seconds remaining, Williams launched a ball down the seam, where Burden went up in traffic to complete the play through multiple defenders and was subsequently blown up by Bush.

 "It was a last-minute play," Bush said. "Take a shot at the end zone. Our responsibility is to not let them in the end zone. Offense's responsibility is get the ball in the end zone. So just a competitive play and finished our practice in the two-minute drill."

 Burden was slow to get up but walked off the field on his own flanked by Williams and cornerback Tyrique Stevenson . A practice like this is an anomaly for the offense, but the lack of execution is something players know will be drilled down on in Tuesday afternoon meetings.

 "We're gonna go in there, clean up the film," Burden said. "You know, every day not gonna be a great day. I mean, you can strive for that, but it's camp. It's gonna be ups and downs. So that's the good part about it. We get to come back and watch it. We come back, be better, talk about it. Come back tomorrow, have a better day. That's what it's about."

 
 Braxton Jones was the first-team left tackle for a second straight practice. That's the first time since late last week when the Bears began rotating who would be with the starting O-line that a player got multiple days in a row with the first-teamers. 
 Cam Lewis will focus on playing safety while Coby Bryant (knee) is sidelined. Lewis, who was playing at nickel corner in place of Kyler Gordon , will be replaced by Jaylon Jones , Josh Blackwell and Malik Muhammad in the slot. Jones got the nickel reps with the 1s on Tuesday. 
 Dayo Odeyingbo worked from the interior of the D-line for most of the practice on pass rushing downs. He came away with an interception on a Tyson Bagent pass that was batted at the line of scrimmage. 
 Kyle Monangai worked his way back into team drills while recovering from a soft tissue injury. The running back got a handful of carries with the first-team offense in 11-on-11. 
 The first scuffle of training camp occurred between rookies Caden Barnett and Jordan van den Berg . The two were tangled up after a play at the end of practice when van den Berg tackled Barnett to the ground. 
 Running back  D'Andre Swift  called Williams his most improved teammate: "Just seeing his poise right now and his process," Swift said. "I get there pretty early, so I see the little things he's doing on the daily in his second year in the system. I just like his approach right now and his focus." 
 Former Saints and Dolphins offensive tackle Terron Armstead took in practice Tuesday. Armstead trained several Bears linemen, including Darnell Wright , Kiran Amegadjie and Theo Benedet this offseason. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 The Bears got substantial injury news during the first padded practice of training camp.

 According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, safety Coby Bryant is expected to miss eight to 10 weeks after injuring his left knee Monday.

 Bryant went down during receiver/defensive back one-on-ones and appeared visibly upset as he walked to a cart under his own power before being taken back into the facility. The Bears were practicing on the fields farthest away from Halas Hall, so getting carted back into the building isn't always indicative of an injury's severity, but according to Schefter, Bryant hyperextended the knee and sustained a bone bruise and small fracture.

 Bryant signed a three-year, $40 million contract with the Bears in free agency. With Elijah Hicks on the physically unable to perform list, Chicago is extremely thin at safety. Bryant's injury forced Cam Lewis , who had been taking most of his reps at nickel with the first-team defense, to shift back to safety opposite rookie Dillon Thieneman .

 More observations: 

 
 Coach Ben Johnson was eager to begin seeing who is standing out in the left tackle battle between Braxton Jones , Jedrick Wills Jr . and Kiran Amegadjie . One-on-ones will allow for coaches to determine who is separating from the pack. "We're judging the ability to block these defensive ends one-on-one, and then, you know, the ability to cut off on the back side of our wide zone scheme is huge for us," Johnson said. "There's things in and out, and I think each one of those guys is probably a little bit stronger in certain areas than the other guy. I think when we look at it, who is the most consistent player that we feel like is going to help us on a weekly basis?" 
 Shortly after Johnson announced  Kyle Monangai 's soft tissue injury, the running back returned to practice and went through stretching and individual drills. Johnson said Monangai's rehabilitation will be "on the shorter side." 
 Luther Burden III dominated his one-on-one matchups. Two catches made against great coverage stood out Monday, most notably a deep ball he caught with CB Tyrique Stevenson draped over him. "He'll give you everything," Stevenson said of Burden. "If you're too high and he wants to get under, he'll get up under and now you're chasing him across the field. If you're too low, he'll take the top off. Luther, to me, is a complete receiver. And he's aggressive to the ball. I would say he's just a complete receiver when it comes with the ball in his hands after the catch and everything." 
 Running back Salvon Ahmed continues to put his speed on display and broke off a big run during 11-on-11 work with the second-team offense. 
 Center Garrett Bradbury is earning rave reviews from Johnson, who called the eight-year vet "extremely impressive" with "elite" communication skills that allow him to be loud, decisive and dictate what he's seeing with the defense. "We're cooking right now with him out there," Johnson said. 
 
 
 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Weather forced the Bears to begin practice inside the Walter Payton Center before moving outdoors for team drills while the rain tapered off to a drizzle.

title: 2026 NFL training camp news, buzz, fantasy football updates
summary: Here's what we heard on the road at training camp for the Bears, Bucs, Chargers, Chiefs, Colts, Commanders, Dolphins, Jaguars, Falcons, Packers, Rams and Vikings.
full_text:
NFL training camps are underway ahead of the 2026 season , and Jeremy Fowler, Dan Graziano and Ben Solak are on the road for their respective annual camp tours. They have collectively stopped at camps for a dozen different teams so far: the Bears, Buccaneers, Chargers, Chiefs, Colts, Commanders, Dolphins, Jaguars, Falcons, Packers, Rams and Vikings. And they're not done, either, with roughly another 12 teams still on deck over the next week or so.

 At each stop, Jeremy, Dan and Ben have talked to players, coaches, execs and scouts to get the latest buzz. We compiled everything they saw and heard, including some nuggets that might be important for fantasy football managers.

 How is  Kyler Murray looking in Kevin O'Connell's offense? Is Aaron Donald any closer to making a decision about whether to un-retire? What's the latest on Patrick Mahomes ' injury recovery? And how are the Packers planning to survive without  Micah Parsons early in the season? Here's what we learned for each team.

 

 
 Jump to a team's camp notes: 
 ATL | CHI | GB | IND | JAX | KC 
 LAC |  LAR | MIA | MIN | TB | WSH 

 
 

 

 Graziano's notes from Los Angeles Chargers camp 
 Dates visited: Aug. 3 
 Location: El Segundo, California

 Best thing I saw/heard: Mike McDaniel had options. After losing his job as head coach of the Dolphins in January, McDaniel was contacted by several teams looking for new offensive coordinators. He ended up with the Chargers in large part because of the enticing prospect of working with quarterback Justin Herbert .

 "It's exceeded my expectations for sure," McDaniel said after Monday morning's practice. "He came in very motivated and he's been very focused the whole time, willing to try new things, which speaks to who he is as a seven-going-on-17-year vet."

 

 McDaniel started the offseason by adjusting Herbert's footwork -- particularly his shotgun stance, where his left foot is now the forward one instead of the right. McDaniel believes it's one of the ways he can help Herbert get the ball out quicker, which is a major point of emphasis this camp. McDaniel said he believed the Chargers have oftentimes asked too much of Herbert and that part of his job as a coordinator is to make Herbert's job easier by developing other parts of the offense around him. That said, McDaniel also recognizes that Herbert is different from any other QB he has ever worked with.

 "Well, he's a small forward in stature," McDaniel said. "Having a 6-6 quarterback can really benefit you in a ton of ways. I think he's one of those rare guys that has a very strong arm but can see the field so he can play with anticipation. And then on top of that, there's thousands of more blades of grass that he can access than a typical quarterback just because of his inherent gifts."

 Head coach Jim Harbaugh said McDaniel stood out to him this offseason among "nine or 10 tremendous offensive minds that were available" as the guy who could come in and take Herbert to the next level. Harbaugh, as most know, likes to speak in hyperbole when it comes to Herbert, but the coach said before Monday's practice that he has been struck by how quickly Herbert has advanced in the new offense.

 "There's Mike, with knowing this offense, and then Justin's right there in his hip pocket," Harbaugh said. "There's nobody in the organization that understands the details of what everybody's doing, players and maybe even coaches, better than Justin does. He's that meticulous. He's really smart and he really studies. The questions he's asking are like AP questions, like a guy who's been in this system for two or three or four years."

 Multiple people to whom I spoke said they believe this is the deepest roster the Chargers have had under Harbaugh. Watching practice, you could see that show up in the number of options Herbert has at wide receiver, tight end and running back. Herbert's protection fell apart last season when starting tackles Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt went down with injuries , but both are back healthy now, and the front office focused largely this offseason on deepening the offensive line.

 The Chargers believe Herbert is set up for success, and a lot of that is because of players McDaniel specifically targeted to help implement his system -- players such as blocking tight end Charlie Kolar , fullback Alec Ingold and center Tyler Biadasz . McDaniel did have options, and when he interviewed with the Chargers, he specifically wanted to know whether they'd be willing to engage in this level of overhaul at this point in Herbert's career.

 "Do you want to go all-in to something and how willing are you to target certain players?" McDaniel said. "And to their credit, I think Jim understands more than anybody that you don't do anything at the highest level, elite, if you're just toe-in-the-water."

 One key fantasy nugget: Keaton Mitchell , if healthy, should be a factor in this offense. Omarion Hampton , a 2025 first-round pick, is the No. 1 in a trio of running backs the Chargers like a lot. But they absolutely have a role planned for Mitchell, the speedy change-of-pace back they signed away from the Ravens in free agency. They think he can help in the passing game in particular but also as a complement to Hampton and Kimani Vidal .

 "He's as dynamic as they come with the ball in his hands in space," McDaniel told me. "He's a matchup issue for every defense. I think he has a lot of pass-game value that he hasn't been able to really represent in his career, but it's showing so far in camp. He's a playmaker that I'm very excited about."

 Best of the rest: 

 
 As mentioned, the two starting offensive tackles are back and healthy. But the Chargers did draft four offensive linemen and make some key free agent additions. The result is that the team feels very good about the depth on the line and what it has in reserve in case injuries strike again. The Chargers were planning an offseason push for free agent center Tyler Linderbaum , but they were excited to grab Biadasz when Washington cut him, getting a guy who fits what McDaniel needs without getting into a bidding war. They like rookie Travis Burke and veteran Kayode Awosika as players who can fill in at tackle should a need arise. And they're having a competition for the starting left guard spot, which could end up being rookie Jake Slaughter , veteran  Trey Pipkins III  or veteran Trevor Penning , but they feel good about having two of those three as backups no matter who ends up starting. 
 
 

 
 Don't expect another late-offseason veteran wide receiver addition like the one the Chargers made last year when they brought back Keenan Allen . They feel great about what rookie receiver  Brenen Thompson  has shown in camp and the improvements they've seen from Quentin Johnston , Tre' Harris and Derius Davis .  Latest Bengals stories 
 
 Joe Burrow, Bengals find camaraderie on unusual battlefield 
 Bengals DE Stewart out multiple weeks with hyperextended knee 
 Bengals' top storylines at training camp 
 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 The defense continues its strong start to training camp. That was punctuated by a two-play exchange that started with a pass deflection by CB  DJ Turner  on a deep ball intended for WR Ja'Marr Chase , before safety S Bryan Cook had a pick-six off QB Joe Burrow during a team drill. Coordinator Al Golden's group has looked nothing like the team that has struggled in each of the past two seasons.

 "I think as a defense, we have an edge," Golden said. "We gotta continue to have that edge. We haven't done anything."

 
 Bengals CB DJ Ivey took first-team reps with Dax Hill sidelined. Hill was dealing with a bit of tightness and was limited for precautionary reasons. 
 DT Jonathan Allen was not at practice in what appeared to be a vet rest day. Allen also missed a day last week before quickly returning. 
 Cincinnati released S Isaiah Nwokobia on Tuesday. He had not practiced in back-to-back days. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 The first day of pads belonged to the Bengals' defense. And in what has become a recurring theme, the defensive line was able to bring some good pressure. Boye Mafe continued to affect the quarterback and rookie Cashius Howell had a clean win off the edge against the second-team defense.

 The defense isn't letting any camp success get to their heads. "We haven't scratched the surface, which is the encouraging thing," said linebacker Barrett Carter . "Our floor right now is high. I'm not trying to jinx us or put expectations on us, but we're stacking days, and we just have to keep doing that. We're nowhere near where we can be."

 More observations: 

 
 Dalton Risner and  Orlando Brown Jr . spent a good amount of time decompressing in the locker room talking about how the day went for them. It was a detailed conversation, which Risner said was an example of the group being dialed in this early in camp. 
 Rookie wide receiver Colbie Young made a couple of good catches. The coaching staff has been adamant that the fourth-round pick out of Georgia can carve out a role on this year's offense. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Have a day, Boye Mafe . The recent Super Bowl winner was disruptive throughout Saturday's practice. He consistently produced pressure against Joe Burrow and the first-team offense, including getting into a passing lane and forcing an interception .

 It has continued a good first week for the defense. But Mafe, who helped the Seahawks win the Lombardi Trophy in February with the Seahawks, knows Cincinnati has a long way to go.

 "I feel like we're really just setting our standard," Mafe said. "You can't mistake activity for achievement." 

 More observations: 

 
 WR Tee Higgins did not practice today but was a close observer. The team has made it a point to limit his workload to avoid any major soft-tissue injuries, a strategy that worked last season. 
 Former Bengals defensive end Sam Hubbard, who retired after the 2024 season, stopped by Saturday's practice to see his old teammates. 
 Practice started indoors because of rain but eventually moved to the outdoor fields. 
 Cornerback DJ Turner had a good pass deflection on a deep ball intended for Ja'Marr Chase . But was notable was the defensive backs making sure to yell "Ball!" to let Turner know the passes was about to arrive. It was an example of the communication the secondary has displayed during the first week of camp. 
 WR Mitchell Tinsley made a diving catch during a red zone drill that appeared to knock the wind out of him. While he was shaken up a touch, his efforts didn't go unnoticed. Offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher made it a point to give Tinsley props for the effort. 
 

 

 

 Friday, July 31 
 Typically, the Bengals don't practice three days in a row during training camp, but this year, Cincinnati is opening camp with four straight practices. So to break things up, Friday was more of a walk-through as the team managed the workload and tried to avoid major injuries. The Bengals didn't even bring helmets out as they slowed the pace down for a private practice. The team spent a couple of team periods working on red zone drills, which is typically what they do on Fridays during the season.

 More observations: 

 
 Bengals defensive tackle Jonathan Allen returned to practice after a day off on Thursday.  
 Dexter Lawrence II  didn't participate in Friday's walk-through. But the Pro Bowler has had sterling attendance since the Bengals traded for him ahead of April's draft. 
 

 

 Thursday, July 30 
 Bengals TE Erick All Jr . is still limited as he comes off an ACL injury that kept him out for all of the 2025 season. But he's already been tested.

 Over the offseason, he was hit by a moped in Greece that launched him into the air and scraped his face. But that was the jolt he needed as he looks to return from the injury he sustained during his rookie season.

 "It was huge for my confidence," All said. "That did a lot of good things for the mental [health]."

 If All is healthy, he could be a big chess piece for a Cincinnati offense looking to be creative in its personnel usage.

 Thursday featured a couple of big catches, including one from undrafted rookie Noah Thomas , who leaped and took the ball off cornerback DJ Ivey 's back as they wrestled to the ground. It impressed Ja'Marr Chase , who is pleased to have Thomas and Colbie Young , another rookie receiver out of Georgia. 
 Last year's embattled rookie linebackers had some notable plays. First, Barrett Carter had a tackle for loss in a team drill. Then  Demetrius Knight Jr . picked off Joe Burrow in an 11-on-11 drill while lurking in coverage. That's a good sign for a unit with big question marks. 
 It might have flown under the radar, but rookie Cashius Howell had a really good rep against Cody Ford . Howell won cleanly off the edge with speed while running with the second-string defense. 
 

 

 Wednesday, July 29 
 Bengals running back Chase Brown is one of the players who could earn a contract extension. And if that happens, quarterback Joe Burrow sounds like he'll be thrilled. He raved about Brown's capabilities as an all-purpose back and advocated for the fourth-year player out of Illinois to be heavily involved in the offense.

 "Obviously we're going to try to get the ball in No. 1 ( Ja'Marr Chase 's) hands as many times as we can," Burrow said. "But I think a close second is Chase Brown just because of how explosive he is and the things he can do with the ball in his hands."

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 DT Dexter Lawrence II was another player who impressed Burrow. "He got back there pretty quick a couple of times," the quarterback said. "We're going to have to get that thing out. Made some blind throws today because of how big he is. 
 Nearly a year removed from his turf toe injury, Burrow expects to keep playing with a protective plate in his shoe. "The foot feels great,"…

title: Joe Burrow, Bengals find camaraderie on unusual battlefield
summary: Center Ted Karras brought a chessboard into the locker room, and it has become a hit.
full_text:
CINCINNATI --  Cincinnati Bengals  quarterback  Joe Burrow looked like he had the game sealed.

 His queen was advancing up the board. His rook, flanking the left side, was in a solid position. What unfolded after a bad move by his opponent early in the game seemed inevitable.

 "He had me dead to rights," said William Wagner , the Bengals' long-snapper.

 But Wagner battled. He made one defensive move with his king, and just like that, they had a stalemate.

 Cincinnati's first week of training camp has featured a few spirited practices, a noted practice scuffle and an intense edge from a team sick of missing the playoffs. But as it has looked to put the rest of the AFC North in check in 2026, the first days of the season have also featured a chessboard.

 Like other team activities this offseason, the game has allowed the Bengals to unwind and spend downtime at the facility and also increase the chemistry needed to become a great team. And it's a window into the mindset of a teammate.

 "It is fun because chess is like a personality game, you know?" said Bengals offensive tackle Andrew Coker . "It's like, what are you thinking? Are you trying to go? Are you playing defensive? Playing the long game? Trying to win now? I like it."

 Cincinnati can thank center Ted Karras and the addition of more offensive linemen this offseason. In April's draft, the Bengals selected center  Connor Lew  (No. 128) and offensive tackle Brian Parker II  (No. 189), which stretched the seating arrangement inside the locker room farther down the left wall.

 

 Annoyed by the lack of proximity, Karras devised a plan. He wanted to add a table to add a gathering space for the position group. Bengals left guard Dylan Fairchild , a rookie last season, found a brown, circular table on Facebook Marketplace for roughly $300.

 But along with a place to watch practice film, Karras felt like something was missing.

 "I just wanted something to do," Karras said.

 So he brought in the chessboard.

 After the team practiced Thursday, Karras and Coker played the inaugural game. As they shifted pieces around the board, a crowd gathered. Other offensive linemen started to watch. Eventually Burrow and fellow quarterback Joe Flacco joined the gallery.

 The pressure was on.

 "They see moves that you probably should make and you may or may not make it and then they react," said Coker, who used two pawns-turned-queens to beat Karras. "Or they make a noise. You're like, 'Did I make the wrong move or something?'"

 Tight end Erick All Jr . was one of the interested parties. For the bulk of his college career, he was at Michigan along with Wagner and Bengals cornerbacks DJ Turner II and Dax Hill . Chessboards sprawled in the cafeteria. Wagner reminded him of one story that he forgot.

 One year, All was locked into a match with then-Michigan coach Jim Harbaugh, an avid chess player. Harbaugh was noted for taking his time before making his next move. And All was getting concerned looking at the clock.

 

 "The team meeting was about to start and he was like, 'Don't move. Stay here,'" All recalled. "We were like five minutes late to this meeting, playing chess, in a game that we didn't even get to finish."

 All is considered one of the best chess players in the locker room. All, who has progressed well in his first year back from a knee injury he suffered in 2024, estimates his highest ever Elo rating -- a skill level rating where the average person is typically between 800 and 900 -- was around 980. But he believes Burrow still holds the crown as the locker room's best (Burrow, a longtime player, declined to divulge his Elo rating).

 But for the Bengals, what matters most is the camaraderie being fostered, especially ahead of an important season. The Bengals have missed the playoffs three years in a row after advancing to the Super Bowl in 2021.

 "It felt good, the guys all gathering around the table," All said. "It's a good way to bring guys [together]. And you got to be smart. You got to know your way around the board to play. You just can't be making senseless moves."

 Over the course of the season, players can expect to see more games on the table. Karras said he'll plan on bringing in Catan at some point to play during lighter days. When the workload is heavy and rigorous, Karras said he'll slide the games under the table.

 "I don't want to be 'Gaming Guy' and we're going against [ Dexter Lawrence II ] today," Karras said.

 But after the first extended session of camp wrapped up Saturday, the chessboard was sitting at the edge of the table. The pieces were on the board, waiting to be deployed for the next battle.

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Quarterback Shedeur Sanders , leading the No. 1 offense in Cleveland's quarterback competition today, led a two-minute drill that ended in a field goal.

 It marked the second straight day Sanders led a successful two-minute drill to end practice.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Wide receiver KC Concepcion was at practice after avoiding a serious shoulder injury on Monday but was limited to individual drills. 
 Eleven players did not practice: tight end Joe Royer (personal), cornerbacks Myles Bryant and Damarri Mathis , fullback Michael Burton , linebacker Carson Schwesinger , defensive tackles Mike Hall Jr ., Kalia Davis , Mason Graham and Maliek Collins (PUP); and offensive linemen Kendrick Green and Teven Jenkins . 
 Safety Christopher Edmonds intercepted quarterback Dillon Gabriel in 7-on-7s; it was Edmonds' third pick in training camp, the most of any defender.

 Before practice, Cleveland signed cornerback Tyler Hall and waived offensive tackle Jack Conley .

 On the first practice with pads for the Browns, quarterback Shedeur Sanders ended the day on a high note for Cleveland's offense. Running the No. 2 offense in the ongoing quarterback competition with Deshaun Watson , Sanders connected with wide receiver Gage Larvadain for a deep touchdown on a slot fade to end a two-minute drill in the end zone.
