 Three of those picks were thrown by Deshaun Watson , who now has six interceptions in four practices, with  Christopher Edmonds  getting two and safety Donovan McMillon getting another. Rookie safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren made a strong play on the first interception, dislodging a ball from tight end Jack Stoll that Edmonds caught off the ricochet.

 Shedeur Sanders  was also intercepted for the first time in training camp, as he underthrew a deep pass to wide receiver Jerry Jeudy and was picked off by cornerback D'Angelo Ross .

 Dillon Gabriel was also intercepted by linebacker Reid Carrico in a red zone drill.

 The three quarterbacks, though, had success in the red zone drills, with each throwing multiple short touchdown passes.

 "It's multiple -- they're doing all types of different stuff, showing us different things," Watson said of Cleveland's defense before practice. "It's really good, especially for the quarterbacks, running backs and O-line, just protectionwise. They're showing us different things every time, and each group is getting different looks."

 Tight end Harold Fannin Jr . returned to practice Saturday after missing Friday's sessions for personal reasons. 
 Cornerback Myles Harden returned to practice after leaving Friday's session early. 
 Linebacker Carson Schwesinger was present but not practicing Saturday. Offensive lineman Teven Jenkins (undisclosed), tight end Joe Royer (personal), defensive tackle Kalia Davis (undisclosed) and wide receiver Jamari Thrash (undisclosed) also did not practice. 
 
 
 Friday, July 31 
 Browns rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston was one of the standouts from the spring offseason workout program and has continued stacking strong performances in training camp. He had one of the catches of camp, leaping over a defensive back along the sideline to bring in a pass from quarterback Shedeur Sanders in 7-on-7s.

 The No. 39 pick out of Washington in the 2026 draft, Boston gives Cleveland a size dimension at 6-foot-4 and 215 pounds that the offense lacked in the 2025 season. He has been working with the second-team offense when the Browns break into two fields to maximize reps but is expected to have a big role as a rookie.

 Quarterback Deshaun Watson took first-team reps Friday and threw his third interception in as many practices when he was picked off by linebacker Quincy Williams over the middle of the field. 
 Browns owner Jimmy Haslam said that despite Cleveland's projected 5.5-win total, he expects the team to improve from its 5-12 season in 2025. "I'll take the over," Haslam said.

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action.  What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at the Cowboys' camp. We will update this file often. Will Dallas turn around the NFL's worst defense from 2025? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Cowboys camp 
 
 Cowboys' Dak Prescott not shying away from setting lofty goals 
 Jones optimistic about Cowboys, likes 'what we put together' 
 Source: Ex-Cowboys QB Will Grier returns as offensive assistant 
 Quieter offseason has Cowboys focused on the right things 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Sometimes coaches can be inventive when it comes to putting players through drills. On Tuesday, wide receivers coach Junior Adams had CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens catching passes off the Jugs machine during a special teams portion of practice while wearing what looked like a mosquito net or beekeeper's hat.

 The goal is to limit the receiver's vision and force him to concentrate longer on the catch. Lamb dropped one pass but figured it out. The first pass went through Pickens' hands, and he was finished.

 Longtime tight ends coach Mike Pope, who had a stint with the Cowboys, said he had 478 different drills for his tight ends. He would throw ice water at shirtless players while wearing a helmet. He had them wear swim goggles to limit their peripheral vision.

 Let's see if Adams has more tricks in his bag.

 More observations: 

 
 Defensive end  Donovan Ezeiruaku was tossed from practice for fighting. Brian Schottenheimer abhors fighting in practice because if a player throws a punch in a game, he gets ejected. A lesson to be learned for Ezeiruaku. 
 With linebacker  DeMarvion Overshown battling a sore leg (a source said it was nothing to do with his surgically repaired knee), rookie Jaishawn Barham worked with the first-team defense next to Dee Winters . 
 Quarterback  Dak Prescott went 13-of-17 in team drills and would have been better if not for drops by Lamb and tight end  Jake Ferguson . He tried to stretch the field once with a throwback down the field to Pickens, who drew a flag on cornerback  Shavon Revel  at the goal line for pass interference. 
 Ferguson had two excellent catches, however, adjusting on a slightly underthrown seam ball from Prescott and later securing a lower pass with one hand before getting it under control. 
 Cornerback  Cobie Durant came up with the defensive play of the day, knocking away a deep ball from Prescott to wideout  Marquez Valdes-Scantling . Safety Alijah Clark was tangled up on the play and limped off to the medical tent and did not return. 
 

 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 No, there is not going to be a playcaller controversy when it comes to the Cowboys this season, but coach Brian Schottenheimer gave the controls to coordinator Klayton Adams for two periods in Monday's practice, including red zone work.

 The result? Four touchdowns in a six-play span, including one to Ryan Flournoy where the receiver wrestled the ball away from cornerback  DaRon Bland for the score from Dak Prescott .

 "[Bland] actually guarded it great," Flournoy said. "I just had to win on that. I dropped slant before that so I had to make it up. Yeah, definitely great defense by DB. I just had to show strong hands."

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Second-year CB Shavon Revel Jr.  had a solid day, breaking up Prescott throws to CeeDee Lamb  and Flournoy, and blanketing George Pickens on a fade in the end zone. He had a pass interference penalty, reaching too early on a throw to Pickens, but it might have been the best practice Revel has had. 
 CB Cobie Durant picked off Prescott, undercutting a throw to Lamb near the goal line in which he dropped off another receiver and came up with the interception. 
 TE Jake Ferguson was back at practice after missing Saturday for personal reasons. He displayed strong hands on a TD catch in the back of the end zone while being covered by S Markquese Bell . 
 NFL officials were on hand for practice, but backup QB Joe Milton III took it into his own hands when an official did not throw a flag on rookie CB Devin Moore on a contested throw to Lamb in the end zone. The pass came on the defensive sideline, so perhaps there was some influence there, but Moore was aggressive on the play in a good way. 
 Prescott was 12-of-21 in team drills Monday after starting 3-of-7 with the Durant pick. 
 TE Princeton Fant left practice early after colliding with RB Israel Abanikanda . 
 

 
 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 The red zone is an area the Cowboys want to see a lot of offensive improvement in in 2026, and Saturday's practice had plenty of work from inside the 20.

 Dak Prescott had touchdown passes to CeeDee Lamb on the post, two to Ryan Flournoy (dig, slot fade) and a bullet of a throw low to the outside that receiver  George Pickens  corralled for the score.

 There was one interception when a Prescott checkdown was tipped by running back  Jaydon Blue into the arms of safety  Malik Hooker .

 Prescott finished the day unofficially 11-of-18 in team drills.

 Last year, the Cowboys converted a touchdown on 37-of-65 red zone drives. So, what makes a good red zone offense?

 "Finishing in the end zone, executing when you need to, third downs, sometimes on first (down)," Lamb said. "Just being able to not really bat ourselves in the foot, those self-inflicted wounds or penalties that'll really bring us back or kill our momentum. And again, finishing in the end zone."

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 It's hard not to notice rookie linebacker  Jaishawn Barham . He is seeing some work with the first-team defense so far. He is active in the run game, filling holes, but he also showed good feel for zone work, knocking down a Prescott pass near the goal line. 
 With Jalen Thompson (hip flexor) and P.J. Locke (knee) not practicing, safeties Alijah Clark and Markquese Bell shared the work with the first-team defense. 
 The catch of the day belonged to undrafted rookie Camden Brown on a fade from Sam Howell . The pass to the back pylon was in a perfect spot and Brown controlled the ball as he was going to the ground. 
 Brandon Aubrey went 5-for-6 on field goal attempts, missing wide right from 44 yards. 
 T.J. Bass has yet to play center in a game in his career, but he is currently the backup to Cooper Beebe . So far, no off-kilter shotgun snaps. Bass' versatility is a plus for the offensive line. 
 

 

 Friday, July 31 

 Tyler Booker knew Cowboys' first-round pick Caleb Downs before any of his teammates. They were together for a year at Alabama before Downs transferred to Ohio State following the retirement of Crimson Tide head coach Nick Saban. Downs quickly earned rave reviews at Alabama, earning a starting spot as a true freshman during spring practice.

 Now four years later, Booker, the Cowboys' top pick in 2025, sees similarities in Downs' assimilation to the Cowboys.

 "Same guy. And that's not to say that he hasn't grown since I knew him as a freshman at Alabama," Booker said. "It just shows you how much of a grown man he was at Alabama. Not many guys start during spring ball, let alone in that secondary coached by Coach Saban. So first and foremost see him out there starting at that secondary during spring ball, and then to see how he played and raised the level of play to everybody else on that side of the ball at Alabama, I just knew he was…

The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action.  Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Broncos camp 
 
 Payton to talk to Taysom Hill about interest in Broncos 
 Broncos QB Bo Nix won't be afraid to run on repaired ankle 
 How will Broncos' Sean Payton adjust to not calling plays? 
 Cooper practices Wednesday despite legal troubles 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 Edge rusher Nik Bonitto limped off the practice field Tuesday after he suffered what appeared to be a lower left leg injury in a 9-on-7 run-game drill. Bonitto left the field with a trainer as well as one of the team doctors and did not return. After practice, Broncos coach Sean Payton would say only "he'll be fine, no updates."

 Bonitto has led the team in sacks in each of the past two seasons -- 13.5 in 2024 and 14.0 in 2025 - helping the Broncos lead the league and establish single-season franchise records in each campaign. Jonah Elliss and Jonathon Cooper took most of the snaps with the starters at the edge spots after Bonitto left practice, with second-year man Que Robinson getting more work throughout the day as well.

 It was the second consecutive day the Broncos had a starter leave practice. Center Luke Wattenberg , who dealt with a shoulder injury last season, left Monday's practice and did not practice Tuesday.

 More observations: 

 
 Add Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle to the list of those who have noticed Marvin Mims Jr .'s work this training camp. Mims made another leaping grab Tuesday -- this time in one-on-ones -- and Waddle was quick to praise it all after practice. "Man, Marv -- I'm a big fan of Marvin Mims, I'm not going to lie. He's very explosive, I love watching him work, love being in meetings (with him), picking his brain. Marvin's a big play always ready to happen, you've got to respect that kind of speed." 
 Wide receiver Courtland Sutton was held out of practice Tuesday for rest, as Payton had said this week he would begin to give some of the veteran players scheduled days off. Sutton was the first, but Payton said he has a group of players who have been scheduled for days off in the weeks to come. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton lamented with a laugh about how fans "certainly only cheer for one side of the ball" when watching the team's practices. But on Monday, cornerback Riley Moss made the kind of defensive play that gets folks on their feet.

 During team drills, Moss jumped alongside wide receiver Courtland Sutton on a deep throw from Bo Nix up the left sideline and snatched the ball away from Sutton as the two hit the ground. Few players in the league get tested more in practice and in games than Moss given that he plays across from four-time Pro Bowl selection Pat Surtain II -- the league's Defensive Player of the Year in 2023. But Sean Payton said Moss' play Monday is indicative to the kind of camp Moss is having as the corner enters the last year of his rookie deal.

 "Man he competes his tail off, I love that about him," Payton said. " ... He's moving around well right now."

 Moss continues to play at a high-enough level to continue to hold off Jahdae Barron  -- Denver's first-round pick in 2025. Safety Talanoa Hufanga said Monday that Moss is "one of the most athletic corners I've ever been around."

 More observations: 

 
 Considering that he was the 20th pick of the 2025 draft, Barron's progress is often a topic of queries pointed at Payton. The Broncos continue to carve out snaps for the second-year defensive back, even as Moss continues to improve. Barron is currently lining up at outside corner in some sets, as the nickel in others and plays at linebacker in the dime. If the Broncos do not re-sign Moss to the market-value deal he might command next offseason, Barron is poised to be next in line. 
 On a team with few roster spots available and almost no traditional camp battles for starting jobs, Sam Ehlinger continues to push Jarrett Stidham to be the team's No. 2 quarterback. Ehlinger has consistently moved the offense via limited snaps in team drills in and while Stidham continues to get most of the work with the second-team offense behind Nix, Ehlinger's work in the preseason and the practices to come will bear watching. 
 Center Luke Wattenberg walked off the field after being knocked down in one-on-one drills and did not return. After practice Payton said Wattenberg "should be fine," but Wattenberg did miss time last season with a shoulder injury. 
 
 
 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 After the Broncos tinkered with the idea this offseason to move Jonah Elliss from outside linebacker to inside linebacker, the first three days of training camp have reaffirmed the decision to leave Elliss right where he is as part of the team's pass rush.

 No matter the future of Jonathon Cooper , who was arrested twice on domestic violence charges this offseason, Elliss is expected to push for more playing time. He has been consistently impactful in practices. And coach Sean Payton has said he is glad they didn't move Elliss inside.

 "For me, it felt like man, we're taking a position that's harder to find and moving him to a position that we think might be a little bit easier to replace," Payton said. " ... I just think we felt like man, he's really ascending as an edge player."

 Elliss continues to push for more than 318 snaps he played on defense last season.

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Another day, another big play for wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr . Mims turned a Bo Nix scramble into a 50-yard touchdown reception in team drills. With Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle in the top two receivers spots, the quest for touches for the other receivers is already crowded with Mims, Troy Franklin and Pat Bryant among those pushing for snaps. Asked how he will make those decisions, Payton invoked Mims' name unprompted: "Just reliability, consistency, I mean, I've said this before about Mims ... I just feel like, man, more touches (for him)... it's a body of work thing.'' 
 The Broncos players will have their first day off training camp Sunday, and Payton said Wednesday will be the first practice in full pads that goes to the two-and-a-half hour mark. 
 
 
 Friday, July 31 
 It is never safe to draw conclusions from the early days of training camp, but Broncos tight end Evan Engram has already had more big plays in three days of practice than he might have had all of last season. The trend continued Friday, as he had two explosive catch-and-runs on deep balls in team drills.

 Engram had a 50 receptions last season -- his first with the Broncos -- but averaged only 9.2 yards per catch and had just two receptions longer than 20 yards. First-year playcaller Davis Webb had two stints as a quarterback with the New York Giants during Engram's time there and that previous familiarity might be manifesting on the practice field as Webb goes through his first camp as an offensive coordinator.

 "I would say yes to some degree, he's trying to find different ways where he might have a matchup, and that's a good thing," coach Sean Payton said of Engram-Webb dynamic. "Now it's just about executing ... [Engram] is one other piece…

title: 2026 Detroit Lions training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Lions training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Detroit Lions camp is taking place in Allen Park, Mich., and Lions reporter Eric Woodyard has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Lions camp. We will update this file often. Can Dan Campbell & Co. get Detroit back in the playoffs in 2026? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Lions camp 
 
 Ex-All Pro LB Devin White joins Lions on 1-year deal 
 Campbell: Robinson deal won't 'hurt' contract talks with Gibbs 
 Campbell: CB Arnold's release 'unfortunate' but for the best 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Tuesday marked Day 2 of padded practices and veteran LB Devin White continued to get acclimated to the defense alongside guys like All-Pro Jack Campbell . White was signed as a free agent on Aug. 1 to add depth after rookie linebacker  Jimmy Rolder went down with a hamstring injury earlier in camp. He has received limited reps in practices so far but has been doing additional conditioning drills on the side with trainers to keep in shape. "Right now, they've got a plan for me and I'm trusting in the plan," White said. "So, whenever they're ready for me to stop doing reps on the side, running and getting more reps in the team period, I'm going to be ready for it."

 More observations: 

 
 Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs missed his sixth straight practice as his hold-in for a contract extension continues but was on the field watching. Ahead of Tuesday's practice, the Atlanta Falcons reached a record-setting three-year extension with RB Bijan Robinson worth up to $75 million, which now likely sets the stage for Gibbs to reach an extension soon. Campbell feels it's "certainly not gonna hurt" with the process of negotiating. "It's not gonna hurt. But we'll see. Look, I'm anxious to get Gibbs back out there," Campbell said. "Every day that goes by, that's another day that you feel like you miss with him and getting him out there with the guys and him doing his part. But there again, it'll get done when it gets done." 
 LB Malcolm Rodriguez left practice early to be evaluated for an ankle injury. 
 The Lions have placed TE Anthony Firkser on injured reserve list and signed TE Zach Horton . Firkser will miss time with a fractured fibula after being carted off the field in practice on Monday. 
 Lions RB Sione Vaki missed Tuesday's practice after getting poked in the eye and suffering a broken nose during a freak accident at practice Monday, according to Campbell. Vaki will also miss time. "We think he'll be OK," Campbell said. "He's just gonna need a minute here. It's just one of those freak things. Somehow a hand gets through the face mask. It was unbelievable."﻿ 
 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 The Lions started padded practices on Monday for the first time in training camp. Head coach Dan Campbell anticipated the intensity increasing with pads on. That sentiment proved correct as players showed more aggression in training for Day 5.

 "I told the players last night that by the end of this week, this roster will begin to separate itself," Campbell said. "This is where we'll find out. We're about to get four really, really good days of pads, and this is Day 1 just to kind of break them in for the other three."

 More observations: 

 
 Star running back Jahmyr Gibbs missed his fifth consecutive practice as his hold-in continues while looking to reach a new deal. However, he was spotted roaming the sidelines for the second straight day, chatting with teammates  Amon-Ra St. Brown , Jameson Williams and Jared Goff on the sidelines. "I think it's good to see. He got a little work inside and to be able to come out and be around the guys, I think that's always gonna be important," Campbell said of Gibbs. "Look, he's still part of us and our players love him. We love him and he's a part of what we do, so it's always good to see him." 
 Injured Lions safeties Kerby Joseph (knee) and Brian Branch (Achilles) were both spotted doing individual rehab/conditioning drills on the side with trainers during practice. 
 Lions rookie LB Jimmy Rolder (hamstring) will be "out for a while," but Campbell says it's not a season-ending injury. 
 Lions rookie edge Derrick Moore is expected to miss 7-10 days with a "minor strain" in his groin. 
 The Lions signed TE Nick Muse and released WR Tarik Black . 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 2 
 The Lions signed free agent linebacker  Devin White to add depth after rookie Jimmy Rolder exited Friday's practice early with a leg injury. Rolder, a fourth-round selection out of Michigan, was off to promising start but could miss some time. Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard still feels Rolder will "absolutely" contribute this season, but the defense could also benefit from White's veteran presence.

 "The urgency's real this year. It's not just lip service," Sheppard said ahead of Sunday's practice. "And, that's what we did. The front office and Dan do a great job going out and it's nonstop. It's always evolving. How can we get better? How can we improve?

 "And like I said, it's not just, 'Oh, go out and get this flash guy.' No. How can we improve the competitive depth situation right now as far as training camp is concerned? And, Devin definitely does that with his championship pedigree."

 

 More observations: 

 
 DT Alim McNeill returned to practice after leaving early on Friday to be evaluated for a neck injury. 
 TE Miles Kitselman (leg) and DE Derrick Moore (groin) left practice to be evaluated for their injuries. 
 RB Jahmyr Gibbs missed his fourth consecutive practice as he awaits a new deal but was spotted outside with the team for the first time since camp started. Lions WR Jameson Williams described Gibbs as "the best of the best" following practice as they were spotted communicating in between on-field drills. Williams feels Gibbs should be the NFL's highest-paid running back. "I wouldn't even say look at the stats, look at the film," Williams said. "Nobody close. He's the best." 
 

 

 Friday, July 31 

 Although it's unclear on when Lions All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph will be back, he remains "super optimistic" that he can return to the field early in the season as he continues to deal with a knee injury that sidelined him for the last 11 games of the 2025 season.

 "I never gave up," Joseph said. "All I do is work. If you see me outside, I'm working."

 This offseason, Joseph has continued to train in hopes of returning sooner than later. For that, Joseph, who said he was baptized in late May, is relying on his faith which he said has changed his perspective on life and football.

 "I had told y'all, I didn't need to do nothing else, nothing more. I just needed to strengthen my relationship with God because God is going to take care of the rest."

 Joseph has been at training camp practices but the Lions have given no timeline for when he'll be back.

 Also, Lions star running back  Jahmyr Gibbs  missed his third day of practice as the apparent hold-in continues while seeking a new deal .

 Head coach Dan Campbell mentioned earlier this week that Gibbs was dealing with a "little bit of a back" issue during conditioning tests but clarified that it's nothing to worry about ahead of Friday's session.

 "No, I don't think it's severe," Campbell said. Gibbs has continued to communicate with teammates, such as wideout  Amon-Ra St. Brown . He is also showing up to the team facility although he's not practicing as players understand the significance of his move, which hasn't…

title: 2026 Green Bay Packers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Packers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Green Bay Packers ' camp is taking place in Green Bay, Wisconsin, and Packers reporter Rob Demovsky has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Packers camp. We will update this file often. Will the revamped WR corps help QB Jordan Love and the offense take another step? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news out of Packers' camp 
 
 Micah Parsons: Playing vs. Cowboys in Week 6 'realistic' 
 Packers RT changes last name to Bako-Bewele to honor heritage 
 Packers star TE Tucker Kraft activated off PUP after ACL recovery 
 Better, worse or the same: Packers defense 
 Packers CEO: Team needs financial bump to stay competitive 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 If there were any questions about how new defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon plans to come up with a pass rush until Micah Parsons returns from his torn left  ACL, the first six training camp practices have offered a glimpse.

 
It's been blitz, blitz, blitz.

 
"Linebackers, safeties, corners, nickels," cornerback Benjamin St-Juste said. "Pretty much everybody."

 
St-Juste, who has been working mostly with the No. 2 defense, had what would have been a sack if tackling was allowed. He also had one on Monday. So did rookie cornerback Brandon Cisse , who has been working with the No. 1 defense. Another cornerback, Jaylin Simpson , had a QB pressure during Tuesday's practice.

 
"Feel like Micah Parsons a little bit," Simpson said.

 
It's not just the corners. Safety  Evan Williams got into the act with a sack of Jordan Love and a pressure to force an incompletion, while safety  Kitan Oladapo got home and forced a scramble. Linebacker Edgerrin Cooper has also been a regular blitzer.

 
Gannon was not blitz heavy as coach of the Cardinals the past three seasons. They ranked 19th, 17th and 32nd in the NFL in blitz rate. Before that, as the Eagles' defensive coordinator, Gannon's units ranked 22nd and 30th in blitz percentage. But he might have to be now -- at least until Parsons is available.

 
"He's got the personnel here to do it," St-Juste said."

 More observations: 

 
 It was the first day for one-on-one pass block/pass rush drills, and in the featured matchup, new left tackle Jordan Morgan blocked Lukas Van Ness on three straight reps. Van Ness tried a power rush, a speed rush and an inside move, and Morgan turned away all three. Morgan, however, did lose a rep against Barryn Sorrell . 
 Speaking of Sorrell, the second-year edge had perhaps his best day. He not only went 2-0 in the one-on-one drill, but he had a pick-six of Love on a backside screen for Josh Jacobs . Sorrell perfectly timed the play, and plucked Love's pass out of the air. "They ran a play like two plays later, and I was out there and I told Josh, 'Not again. Not again,'" Sorrell said. "Then next thing you know, it happened." 
 No wonder defensive tackle Anthony Campbell is so good at batting down passes (see Sunday's and Monday's camp reports). He won all four of his reps in the one-on-one pass rushing drill Tuesday. 
 Short on tight ends because of injuries, the Packers signed two of them: McCallan Castles and Drew Biber . They have been without Luke Musgrave (neck), Luke Lachey (foot) and RJ Maryland (hamstring) plus Tucker Kraft (ACL recovery) has been limited to individual drills only. The Packers then waived/injured Lachey and Maryland. Without Musgrave and Kraft, Josh Whyle , who had five catches in eight games last season, has worked as the No. 1 tight end. 
 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 Patience may be the operative word when it comes to kicker Trey Smack . The rookie had another uneven day on Monday, the first practice in full pads and the second in which the Packers kicked field goals during live periods.

 After going 3-for-5 in windy conditions on Sunday, Smack had a 5-for-8 day in slightly calmer conditions on Monday.

 It started with a miss wide right from 33 yards. He then made from 40, 43 and 48 before missing badly right from 55. The bigger tests came during end-of-game simulations in which the offense was down 28-26 with 50 seconds left from its own 30. With the No. 1s, Smack missed a 52-yarder that clanked off the left upright, but he then connected from 33 and 51 yards after drives by the second- and third-stringers.

 The sixth-round pick from Florida has a two-day mark of 8-for-13. He's currently the only kicker on the roster.

 "I'd like to have some patience here, but at the end of the day, any player, if he's costing us opportunities to win football games, then we're going to have to look at that," general manager Brian Gutekunst said at the start of camp. "But again, we really have a lot of confidence in Trey and what he's going to be able to do, but he is a rookie kicker and he's got a lot to learn and earn before he gets there."

 More observations: 

 
 There were no skirmishes or big hits in the first practice with full pads. It appears coach Matt LaFleur's message got through, especially as it pertained to the quarterbacks -- something he was previously unhappy with. "That's the one thing that I've been probably most disappointed with is how many guys we've had in the quarterback's lap," LaFleur said before practice. "That was definitely stressed this morning. We had a couple instances yesterday in practice when we got guys that just veer off. You can't get close to them. There's going to be a time and a place for that, and that'll be in our first preseason game." 
 There were a few plays that would've ended with a sack but instead were allowed to continue. One of those may have been on a 60-yard touchdown from Jordan Love to wide-open receiver  Jayden Reed , when linebacker Edgerrin Cooper might have gotten to Love, and another in which edge Brenton Cox Jr . may have gotten home. 
 A year ago, Bo Melton was trying to learn the cornerback role. This year, he's back at his natural receiver spot and on Monday made his best play of camp -- an over-the-shoulder catch from Tyrod Taylor down the right sideline against cornerback Jaylin Simpson . 
 While Love and Taylor both hit some deep shots, the defense had their share of wins, too. Safety Evan Williams and cornerback Brandon Cisse knocked the ball away from Christian Watson on what would have been a deep completion from Love. Watson may have dropped it, but Williams said, "I'd like to think I got a hand in there. I don't know if it was on the ball as much as just raking through his arm a little bit." 
 Cisse worked almost exclusively with the No. 1 defense. Cornerback Carrington Valentine did not practice after dropping out Sunday with a hamstring injury. Tight end RJ Maryland (hamstring) and guard Aaron Banks (knee/load management) did not practice. Tackle Brant Banks (hamstring) returned. 
 For the fourth time in camp and third time in the past two practices, defensive tackle Anthony Campbell batted down a pass at the line. 
 Normally, the quarterbacks throw into nets early in practice. On Monday, they instead threw to tight end  Tucker Kraft , who is looking to get in some extra reps until he's cleared for more than just individual drills as he comes back from a torn right ACL. 
 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 2 
 Given what his lower left leg looked like before he had to be carted off the field in Week 17 against the Baltimore Ravens , cornerback Kamal Hadden barely flinched when he looked down at the pinkie finger on his right hand and saw that it was bent sideways.

 After an…

title: 2026 Houston Texans training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Houston Texans training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Houston Texans ' camp is taking place in Houston at at NRG Park., and Texans reporter D.J. Bien-Aime has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Texans camp 
 
 Houston bringing back former No. 1 pick Clowney 
 Texans have 'productive' contract talks with Stroud 
 

 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 Texans wideout Jayden Higgins is starting to blossom as he's entering Year 2. When Pro Bowl wideout Nico Collins  was asked about Higgins' progression he said "He's hooping right now, and I can't wait to see him rock out when it really matters."

 During Tuesday's practice, Higgins made multiple catches with All-Pro cornerback  Derek Stingley Jr . in coverage. One of those receptions occurred during a team third-down period for a 20-yard gain. The other one was during 1-on-1s -- where Stingley tried to aggressively jam Higgins, but he avoided the powerful jab and broke free for an easy toss from quarterback C.J. Stroud .

 Early in camp, Stroud said he expected Higgins to have a "dominant" Year 2, and so far we are starting to see it.

 Other observation:  

 Linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair was slow to get up after a collision with tight end Dalton Schultz . Al-Shaair was fine shortly after.

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 This was Day 1 of padded practices, and the defense shined. Quarterback C.J. Stroud  was forced to hold the ball longer than he would like as the secondary coverage was stout.

 Stroud occasionally scrambled more than usual to buy time to make throws and the defensive line forced a few sacks. Safety Calen Bullock intercepted Stroud.

 Also coach DeMeco Ryans used exotic blitzes throughout the day, and the offense sometimes had answers and other times didn't. Ryans deemed the first day in full pads as "successful." 

 Other observation: 

 First-round pick Keylan Rutledge is adding an extra juice of aggression to the unit. He got into a mini tussle with defensive end Danielle Hunter after a successful run play by running back Woody Marks .

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Saturday's padless practice featured more back and forth from the offense and defense. Some periods the defense dominated and others, the offense was able to counter their blitzing.

 The Texans start padded practices on Monday and that will be a "big part" of the evaluation process for the team according to coach DeMeco Ryans.

 The fourth-year head coach said: "There's a lot of all-stars in shorts," and later added the staff wouldn't be fooled by what players have done without pads.

 Another observation: 

 
 Cornerback Derek Stingley Jr collided with linebacker Henry To'oTo'o and was slow to get up, but he shook it off and was back on the field. 
 

 

 Friday, July 31 
 It was mainly walk-throughs for the Texans. It's a theme that's been consistent for coach DeMeco Ryans throughout the offseason -- where he has focused on helping his team mentally work toward executing deep in the playoffs.

 "I've grown as a head coach," Ryans said in June. "For me, it's more so now about how much smarter can we play as a team. How can we be more elite on our execution? Our communication, can it be louder? Can we echo it more? Can we truly be tied together every time we line up? That's what I've seen when I talk about the process of us this year being better."

 Saturday's practice will be the first day with fans in attendance since training camp has opened. That will be a longer practice with more intensity compared to today's practice that was roughly a little over an hour.

 

 

 Thursday, July 30 
 The passing attack was centered around the quick game time to throw on Day 2 of practice. Quarterback C.J. Stroud was quick and decisive with his throws with all but one of his throws being made under 2.8 seconds, and his only rep over three seconds was when he extended the play and tried to find wideout Jayden Higgins in the back of the end zone.

 It fell incomplete, but the majority of his throws came with precision and decisiveness. Stroud was able to connect a few times with Higgins, who's development in Year 2 will be huge for the offense.

 Other observation:  

 
 Backup cornerback Alijah Huzzie was able to make a nice interception off of backup QB  Davis Mills  -- where took the ball away from the intended receiver. 
 
 
 Wednesday, July 29 
 The Texans were more forthcoming regarding contract discussions than normal. General manager Nick Caserio said there's a "possibility" the team and quarterback C.J. Stroud can reach a contract extension. Stroud isn't focused much on contract discussions; he's letting his agent handle it as he is "keeping the main thing the main thing."

 Stroud is going into Year 4 and is eligible for an extension for the first time in his career. Coach DeMeco Ryans said he doesn't get into a lot of deep discussions with guys when it comes to contract situations.

 But he added, "I truly believe you get the contract by what you do on the field. It doesn't matter what you say, what I say. It's about how you perform on the field, and if you're worthy of getting a contract and you deserve it, it'll happen for you."

 Other observation: 

 
 CB Kamari Lassiter intercepted Stroud with a diving catch and then punted the ball in celebration. That was the most exciting play on a relatively quiet morning.

title: 2026 Indianapolis Colts training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Colts training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Indianapolis Colts ' camp is taking place in Grand Park Sports Campus, Westfield, Indiana, and Colts reporter Stephen Holder has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Colts camp. We will update this file often. Will quarterback  Daniel Jones return to early-2025 form after a serious injury? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Colts stories 
 
 Tons at stake as Colts' Daniel Jones enters proving ground 
 Colts won't give Richardson away 
 DT DeForest Buckner back at practice after neck surgery 
 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 One week into camp and perhaps the biggest question is not a question at all.

 Quarterback Daniel Jones has not missed a single snap with the first-team offense and has not taken any days off from practice. This comes in spite of him only recently being fully cleared to practice in full-team drills following his Achilles tendon tear in December. If there were any uncertainties entering this camp, Jones has put them to rest.

 "I've felt good through the whole camp so far," Jones said. "I knew I would. You try to push yourself in the rehab in preparation for camp, knowing what to expect. I felt really good and I stay on the recovery part of it to make sure I'm available and out here every day."

 The Colts are five practices in and there are no known plans to pull back on Jones' workload.

 
 Play of the day: Tight end Tyler Warren hauled in a leaping catch on a deep ball from Jones, taking the ball away from safety Cam Bynum . 
 Cornerback Sauce Gardner missed Tuesday's practice with an illness, according to a team spokesman. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward have been making life difficult for the team's wide receivers so far in camp, much to the Colts' contentment.

 Gardner and Ward are expected to be among the best cornerback combos in the league this season if they can both remain on the field. That was not the case last season, when they spent just one full game on the field together because of respective injuries.

 The length of both players has been especially challenging for the receivers, a group that is trying to find its way with the No. 3 spot still up for grabs.

 "When you can go up against two of the best in the league in practice every day, it's going to make everybody better," coach Shane Steichen said.

 

 
 Steichen said he still does not have any clarity on when No. 1 receiver Alec Pierce might return to the lineup after offseason ankle surgery. Pierce, according to GM Chris Ballard, will spend "a week or two" on the physically unable to perform list. But it's not clear that he's closer even as the Colts begin their second week of camp. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 The Colts spent most of Saturday's workout focused on red zone play, with the offense and defense more or less playing to a draw in terms of success. Among the highlights was tight end Tyler Warren 's leaping catch in the end zone for a touchdown from quarterback Daniel Jones . Another impressive completion came when Jones delivered a strike to receiver Josh Downs in the corner of the end zone.

 But the defense held its own, too, forcing Jones and quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr . to scramble out of the pocket multiple times in 7-on-7 and in full-team periods.

 Additionally, cornerback Sauce Gardner had an athletic pass deflection against Downs to stop a red zone threat.

 More observations: 

 
 Coach Shane Steichen missed practice with an undisclosed personal matter. 
 WR Nick Westbrook-Ikhine emphasized his intent to be a reliable blocker for running back Jonathan Taylor , a quality he said he learned early in his career while blocking for Derrick Henry during their time together with the Tennessee Titans . "That's something you've definitely got to take pride in," he said. 
 

 

 Friday, July 31 

 Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon spoke to reporters for the first time in several months and revealed the details of her address to the team this week. On the heels of last season's massive collapse -- a seven-game losing streak to end the Colts' season -- Irsay-Gordon emphasized the need to finish.

 "As we reflected on last season, this one phrase just kept coming to my mind," she said. "And that was 'Find a way.' So that was the mantra that we settled on for this season. And we came to 'find a way' because we thought about what are the qualities that successful people have? And those qualities are consistency, those qualities are resilience."

 The Colts lost quarterback Daniel Jones and players such as  Sauce Gardner and DeForest Buckner down the stretch last season. But Irsay-Gordon emphasized that injuries would not be a cop-out this season, when general manager Chris Ballard and coach Shane Steichen are considered to be on the hot seat.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Rookie middle linebacker CJ Allen returned to the lineup after sustaining a calf tweak during his preparation for camp last week. He spent the first two days of camp on the physically unable to perform list but immediately stepped into the starting lineup on Friday. 
 The Colts endured underwhelming quarterback play on Friday from Jones, Anthony Richardson Sr . and Riley Leonard with errant throws, bobbled snaps and questionable decisions ruling the day. 
 

 

 Thursday, July 30 

 Cornerback Charvarius Ward has had a strong start to camp, something that is especially notable given where he was just seven months ago: On the verge of retirement.

 Ward previously addressed his change of heart, deciding to return after the 2024 death of his infant daughter and a series of concussions in 2025 nearly pushed him to step away from the NFL. He now says he was "probably 85% sure I was going to retire. But I found a different why, a different purpose. Doing it for Junior [his son], doing it for Amani, my daughter. They bring me joy. They bring a smile to my face."

 Ward, 30, added, "I feel good, I've got a lot of energy. I feel like I still belong out here."

 More observations: 

 
 The Colts are taking a closer look at second-year safety Hunter Wohler , who sustained a season-ending injury in camp as a rookie last year. He's in a competition with rookie A.J. Haulcy , who was impressive in the spring and looked to have the edge at strong safety. This will be a position battle to watch. 
 The Colts have a legitimate kicking competition between Spencer Shrader , who had a season-ending knee injury last season, and former Saints kicker Blake Grupe , who had a strong finish to the season in relief of Shrader. Both seem likely to be on an NFL roster this season, regardless of who sticks in Indy. 
 

 

 Wednesday, July 29 
 The last time running back Jonathan Taylor was entering a contract year, he effectively staged a hold-in during training camp, opting out of practice and citing an ankle injury. This time, Taylor is again seeking a new deal, but he was primed and ready to roll on Wednesday, the first day of camp.

 "I have faith," Taylor said. "There've been some good conversations and I have faith between my agent and the front office. Like I said, I've already said I would love to be a Colt for life. So, I have faith that things are moving in the right direction."

 Taylor, who rushed for 1,585 yards last season, is scheduled to become a free agent in the spring.

title: 2026 Jacksonville Jaguars training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Jaguars training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action.  Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Jaguars' camp 
 
 Jaguars' Travis Hunter feeling faster after 10-pound weight gain 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Very good day for the defense on Tuesday in the Jaguars' second day in full pads.

 Safeties Antonio Johnson and Eric Murray and cornerback Jarrian Jones intercepted passes, Jones broke up another in the end zone, and linebacker Branson Combs broke up a pass on the goal line. Cornerback Jabbar Muhammad also had tight coverage on Travis Hunter on a throw into the end zone and forced an incompletion.

 Johnson's interception came off Trevor Lawrence while Murray and Jones picked off Nick Mullens .

 More observations: 

 
 Hunter had 17 snaps (10 defense, 7 offense) in 11-on-11 work. He has totaled 86 snaps (51 defense, 35 offense) through six practices. 
 LB Jared Bartlett was taken off the field after suffering a leg injury, which leaves the team down two linebackers ( Jack Kiser suffered a right knee injury on the first day of camp). The team is also limiting  Foyesade Oluokun 's snaps in team work, so the Jaguars could be looking to add at that spot. 
 RB Chris Rodriguez Jr . did not participate in Tuesday's practice as part of the team's plan to ramp up his participation. Rodriguez, who missed almost all of the spring with a left foot injury, did participate in Monday's practice. 
 DE Arik Armstead had a veteran day off on Tuesday, his second of camp. 
 

 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Anton Harrison , who has started 48 games at right tackle since being drafted 27th overall in 2023, has spent the past three practices working at left tackle as part of the Jaguars' philosophy of cross-training offensive linemen.

 Coach Liam Coen didn't rule out that being a permanent change, though.

 "If that ends up sticking, then hopefully that's a good thing for us," Coen said after Monday's practice. "And I think he's put together five good practices so far that you're pleased with seeing the consistency."

 Monday's practice was the first in full pads and Harrison won all four of his one-on-one pass rush reps, including two against defensive end Josh Hines-Allen , the franchise's sack leader (61).

 Cole Van Lanen was the team's starting left tackle at the end of the 2025 season and the Jaguars signed him to three-year, $51 million extension in January. However, he has yet to practice because he's still recovering from a knee injury he suffered in the regular-season finale. He is expected to return at some point in camp.

 Walker Little  -- who lost the starting job at left tackle to Van Lanen last season -- had been the left tackle for the first two camp practices and is now working at right tackle.

 

 More observations: 

 
 WR Brian Thomas Jr . has followed up his impressive spring with a good start to camp. He had the play of the day on Monday with a one-handed catch down the sideline in 11-on-11. CB Montaric Brown had sticky coverage but Thomas grabbed Trevor Lawrence 's throw with his right arm while fending off Brown with his left. 
 Relatively quiet day for CB/WR Travis Hunter . He had 13 snaps in 11-on-11 (seven on defense and six on offense). He was targeted once by QB Nick Mullens , but there was a miscommunication on the route. Hunter cut the route short while Mullens threw long. 
 

 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 2 
 Travis Hunter had one of the most impressive training camp practices of his career on Sunday, making two catches on offense and intercepting a pass on defense.

 His first catch came on a deep over route on a throw from Trevor Lawrence . He had a step on cornerback Jarrian Jones when he caught the ball and accelerated down the sideline for what would have been a big gain.

 He made his second catch, also from Lawrence, over his left shoulder down the right sideline with a defensive back on his back.

 "The deep reception was awesome to see," offensive coordinator Grant Udinski said. "He's continued to progress from a route technique fundamental standpoint, but also a knowledge of the offense and just the system in general.

 "When he has the ball in his hands, he can create something special. He can make guys miss. He has a great awareness of defenders and space out there on the field, but he also has great ball skills. So those things kind of pop off the tape."

 Hunter intercepted Nick Mullens ' pass to tight end Quintin Morris , jumping in front of the throw and returning the ball for what would have been a touchdown.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 RB Chris Rodriguez Jr . participated in 11-on-11 work for the first time in camp. His snaps were limited but he did get two carries as part of a gradual ramp-up of participating that coach Liam Coen said would be the plan. Rodriguez missed the spring after undergoing surgery on his left foot. 
 WR Parker Washington had one of the plays of the day when he made a sliding catch in the end zone on a deep throw from Lawrence during an 11-on-11 move-the-ball period. 
 The Jaguars will be in full pads for the first time on Monday. 
 

 

 Friday, July 31 
 Cornerback Jarrian Jones had the best performance of any defensive player so far in camp with a pair of interceptions and a pass breakup on Friday. Jones intercepted quarterback  Trevor Lawrence 's sideline pass to receiver Parker Washington during red zone 7-on-7 work and also picked off  Nick Mullens ' throw to receiver Josh Cameron during 11-on-11 work. He also broke up Mullen's pass intended for receiver CJ Williams in 11-on-11.

 With Montaric Brown and Travis Hunter locked in as the starting corners, Jones is competing with Jourdan Lewis to be the team's third cornerback. Lewis and Jones can each play outside and inside, making both valuable reserves.

 "[Jones] got his hands on a lot of balls today," head coach Liam Coen said. "When he plays with anticipation and just plays free and he's not overthinking it and we're not maybe putting him in positions to overthink, he's able to just go play. And he's a physical dude at the line of scrimmage. He likes to be up front and challenge people in their faces. And so we've got to continue to put him in positions that he can be successful, but I've been really pleased with Jarrian."

 

 More observations: 

 
 CB/WR Hunter played 15 snaps in 11-on-11 Friday (seven on offense, eight on defense). Had one catch on two targets. 
 WR Brian Thomas Jr . had two TD catches Lawrence and got open deep for a third but Lawrence overthrew him. All came in 11-on-11 work. 
 TE Nate Boerkircher , the team's second-round pick (and their first of the draft because of the Hunter trade), made his first catch of camp in any of the 11-on-11 drills, snagging a throw from Lawrence. Lawrence also targeted him in the end zone on a throw that S Caleb Ransaw broke up. 
 It was a good day for DE Travon Walker , who would have had a sack after beating RT Chuma Edoga  and batted a pass down at the line of scrimmage.

title: 2026 Kansas City Chiefs training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Chiefs training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Kansas City Chiefs ' camp is taking place at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, Missouri, and Chiefs reporter Nate Taylor has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Chiefs camp. We will update this file often. Can coach Andy Reid get the Chiefs back into the playoffs? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Chiefs camp 
 
 Rookie wideout Cyrus Allen an early star of Chiefs training camp 
 Chiefs' Reid: Eric Bieniemy's wife out of ICU, 'doing great' 
 Chiefs' Mahomes fully cleared for camp, feeling 'amazing' 
 As training camp opens, Chiefs point to brighter future in 2026 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 For the second consecutive day in pads, Kahlil Benson , the undrafted rookie right tackle from Indiana, performed well, even better than Monday, after once again receiving all of the repetitions with the first-team offense.

 In the first 11-on-11 period, Benson showed strong run-blocking skills by executing a double-team to move defensive tackle Khyiris Tonga back. The repetition finished with Benson also blocking linebacker Nick Bolton , which created more space on the right side of the field for running back Kenneth Walker III . A few minutes later, Benson blocked defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah in pass protection for quarterback Patrick Mahomes to connect with receiver Tyquan Thornton for a completion for more than 30 yards.

 "He's done great," Walker said of Benson. "We've got pads on now and you get to see how well he's doing out there. He's going to have a great impact on this team."

 Benson's work, on the field and in meetings, has pushed him to have true competition with Jaylon Moore , the five-year veteran, for the starting right tackle role.

 In the final 11-on-11 period, Benson didn't lose any of the five repetitions with the first-team offense. His matchups included Anudike-Uzomah, pass rusher Chris Jones and rookie defensive end R Mason Thomas .

 "We'll give you a chance here to learn, but if you start making [mistakes] consistently, then we've got a problem," Reid said Monday of Benson. "But he's been doing a good job. There's a hiccup here or there, but he fixes them normally."

 More observations: 

 
 The players who missed Tuesday's practice were cornerback Kristian Fulton (hip), defensive end Ashton Gillotte (strained right hamstring), defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee) and receivers Cyrus Allen (left shin) and Xavier Worthy (sprained right shoulder). 
 Receiver Rashee Rice (right knee) participated in 7-on-7 repetitions for the second straight day, this time catching a short pass from Mahomes against zone coverage. For the first time in camp, cornerback  L'Jarius Sneed , a six-year veteran, participated in 1-on-1 drills and 7-on-7 repetitions. 
 Joe Bleymaier said he has talked with offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy the past few days. For more than a week, Bleymaier, the pass game coordinator, has taken over Bieniemy's duties as offensive coordinator during his absence. He left the Chiefs after his wife, Mia Bieniemy, 57, was hospitalized in stable condition last week after being allegedly shot by the couple's son, Elijah Zion Bieniemy, 27, at the family's home in Virginia. "We miss EB, obviously," Bleymaier said. "It was great to hear from him, just on a personal standpoint. You're so devastated for him. He's been reaching out more and more lately with some of the football stuff, so that's kind of brought a little sense of normalcy back. As far as the [acting] offensive coordinator, calling in the plays and just making sure some of the administration stuff is handled has been the biggest thing." 
 One of Mahomes' best repetitions was during the first 11-on-11 period, when he, under center Creed Humphrey , rolled to the right on a play-action pass, completing an intermediate throw to Thornton while on the move. "We're not going to put any limitations on what Patrick can do rather than maybe emphasizing what we're going to try to do more," Bleymaier said of Mahomes, who had surgery in December to repair the torn ACL and LCL in his left knee. "We're really trying to eliminate holding him back -- or 'Let's not put him in this situation.' Everything is open. -- under center, rolling left or right, the whole playbook." 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 Among young players, the biggest winner from the Chiefs' first padded practice was rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods , the second of the Chiefs' first-round picks.

 In the 1-on-1 period, Woods had highlight repetitions, winning quickly in both of his matchups against backup guard Hunter Nourzad , a three-year player. When Woods went against right guard Trey Smith , a two-time Pro Bowler and a five-year veteran, the teammates split their two repetitions. The rookie used his quickness to push Smith back by gaining leverage using his right hand.

 "Peter is really talented, man, in terms of his hand utilization, speed, power," Smith said after practice. "He's really sort of the full package type of guy. He's young and he's figuring out the game, but he has a willingness to learn.

 "I've really enjoyed the way he's stepped into this program. He definitely has an outstanding future. I'm just really excited to help him in his development where I can."

 Selected with the 29th pick, which the Chiefs gained from the Los Angeles Chargers through the trade involving cornerback Trent McDuffie , Woods has been impressive in creating havoc at times for running backs by bursting through the offensive line just a second after the snap. The Chiefs are hoping Woods can be effective in 1-on-1 matchups while playing next to star pass rusher Chris Jones .

 "I've liked what I've seen," coach Andy Reid said of Woods. "He's an explosive kid, he's smart and he's learning, trying to hone in on some of the techniques we're asking him to do. I like his effort. He's got a ways to go, but you sure like the tools."

 On offense, left tackle Josh Simmons , a second-year player, was able to demonstrate his improvements. In 1-on-1 repetitions against defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah , Simmons stonewalled his teammate multiple times. Even rookie defensive end R Mason Thomas , who is known for his speed, was unable to get around Simmons.

 "Josh is just so freaking talented," Smith said. "He's really aspiring to be a great player. He's hungry for it. He's really been putting a lot of work in, and he's going to continue to develop. He's a great dude. I'm really excited to keep watching him grow."

 The lone pass rusher who was able to push Simmons back with a powerful bull rush was defensive end George Karlaftis .

 "Josh is a great player," Karlaftis said. "He's strong as an ox and he's got feet like a ballerina. He's very talented. We've had our battles and we've talked. This is what this period is for, for getting better."

 The players who missed Monday's practice were defensive end Ashton Gillotte (strained right hamstring), defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee) and receivers Cyrus Allen (left shin) and Xavier Worthy (sprained right shoulder). Reid said he expects Allen and Worthy to return to practice later this week. Receiver Rashee Rice (right knee) participated in one 7-on-7 repetition late in Monday's practice.

title: 2026 Los Angeles Chargers training camp: Latest intel, updates

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Los Angeles Chargers camp is taking place at The Bolt in El Segundo, California, and Chargers reporter Kris Rhim has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Chargers camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 
 Latest from Chargers camp 
 
 Players with the most at stake during Chargers' training camp 
 Tracking 2026 NFL hold-ins: Tuipulotu 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 The Chargers had their first major injury scare Tuesday as left tackle Rashawn Slater appeared to sustain an injury to his left leg at practice. Slater went to the medical tent with a trainer and then did some on-field testing but didn't return to practice. Branson Taylor and Trey Pipkins III rotated at tackle in his absence.

 Slater ruptured the patella tendon in his left knee during last year's training camp, which forced him to miss the entire season. He appeared in good spirits after practice, walking around and taking pictures with his family.

 Quarterback Justin Herbert said that Slater told him he was healthy enough to return to the field.

 "He said he wanted to be out there, so I think that's okay," Herbert said.

 

 Other observations: 

 
 OLB Tuli Tuipulotu participated in one 7-on-7 rep but did not take part in the remainder of team drills, marking his sixth straight practice with limited participation as his contract situation remains unresolved. 
 Coach Jim Harbaugh said that Kayode Awosika is leading the competition to start at left guard, but added that Pipkins, Jake Slaughter and Taylor are all in the mix. Harbaugh said that he'd like to name a starter after the next ten practices. 
 The offense came out sharp, with Herbert completing his first eight passes before safety RJ Mickens broke up a pass. From there, the offense and defense traded wins throughout the rest of practice. 
 S Kendall Williamson intercepted Herbert on a pass that was intended for wide receiver Ladd McConkey . "That was nice. He snagged it," Derwin James Jr . said. 
 OLB  Nadame Tucker  had one of his best practices of camp, consistently generating pressure and recording three would-be sacks. 
 DT Teair Tart was disruptive throughout, including what likely would have been at least one sack. The Chargers' interior defensive line generated pressure throughout the day. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Monday's practice was one of the better days for the defense, as they were constantly disruptive throughout. Undrafted cornerbacks Rodney Shelley and Avery Smith were among the stars. Smith continued his strong start to camp with another good day, as he intercepted quarterback DJ Uiagalele i and had an impressive pass breakup on a Justin Herbert pass. Shelley was sticky in coverage throughout and had a few pass breakups, celebrating after each.

 The rookies will have their first NFL training camp practice in pads on Tuesday at the University of San Diego, a chance to affirm the way they've been playing.

 

 Other observations:

 
 Edge rusher  Tuli Tuipulotu continued to not participate in team drills, continuing his limited participation as his contract situation remains unresolved. 
 Rookie Jake Slaughter and Kayode Awosika split reps at left guard as the competition for that spot continues. 
 Second-year wide receiver  KeAndre Lambert-Smith , who has been quiet so far, made one of the top highlights of the day with impressive downfield catch while cornerback Deane Leonard was draped in coverage. 
 Quentin Johnston also produced another offensive highlight, tracking a perfectly placed deep ball from Herbert over the outstretched arms of safety Derwin James Jr. along one sideline. 
 
 
 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Coach Jim Harbaugh declined to say whether outside linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu 's absence from team drills at practice is contract-related, saying only the situation is being "handled internally" and repeatedly describing Tuipulotu as "ramping up."

 Tuipulotu hasn't taken part in team drills amid contract negotiations since camp began this week, as he is heading into the final year of his rookie contract. He finished sixth in the NFL in sacks last season.

 Without Tuipulotu again Saturday, rookie Akheem Mesidor flashed, looking explosive coming off of the edge throughout practice.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Saturday marked perhaps the highest-energy practice as the Chargers offense had its best day this week. Wide receivers Ladd McConkey and Derius Davis caught deep passes that energized the crowd at the Chargers facility. 
 Cornerback Donte Jackson was active in coverage with a couple of pass breakups, causing fans to cheer in reaction. 
 
 

 Friday, July 31 

 Friday's practice was at half-speed, walkthrough pace, but the most significant development came at left guard.  Trey Pipkins III  began with the first group blocking for quarterback Justin Herbert , the first time he's done so this week. Throughout camp and the offseason program,  Kayode Awosika , Trevor Penning  and rookie Jake Slaughter have rotated at left guard, with Awosika getting most of the reps with Herbert.

 Coach Jim Harbaugh said earlier this offseason that the race for a starter at left guard would be between these four players. This is the first time that Pipkins has gotten reps with the top group.

 Still, offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel cautioned against looking too much into the rep distribution, noting that the real evaluation will come with padded practices next week.

 "It's much different when you have 300 pounds of mass on your edge," McDaniel said, "and a subtle 6-inch step determines whether or not you can actually execute that block."

 Other observations:  

 
 Tuli Tuipulotu continued not to practice amid ongoing contract negotiations. He went through individual drills, worked off to the side with a trainer and watched practice. 
 Wide receivers Quentin Johnston and Ladd McConkey said that McDaniel has changed the way they run routes, particularly by emphasizing how quickly they finish the top of a route and locate the football. "We weren't all the way used to running routes like that," Johnston said. 
 

 
 

 Thursday, July 30 
 Tuli Tuipulotu didn't practice for the second straight day amid ongoing contract negotiations, but he did more on the field work with teammates than on the opening day of camp. On Thursday, Tuipulotu wore a helmet and jersey and went through individual drills with the team before working off to the side with a trainer. On Wednesday, he was in a T-shirt and shorts and worked off to the side with a trainer.

 "We miss him out there," defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary said. "We miss how vocal he is and the plays that he makes."

 More observations: 

 
 It's difficult for lineman to truly have an impact without pads, but defensive tackle Justin Eboigbe made plays Thursday that drew praises from defensive line coach Mike Elston throughout the day. The Chargers are hopeful Eboigbe takes a step as a pass rusher in his third season. 
 Wide receivers Quentin Johnston , Ladd McConkey and Brenen Thompson were active in the passing offense and were quarterback  Justin Herbert 's favorite targets on Day 2. 
 

 
 Wednesday, July 29 
 Chargers outside linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu was the only player not to practice on Day 1 of training camp. The team has not officially disclosed the reason for his absence, but with extension talks ongoing, it appears to be contract related.

 Safety  Derwin…

title: 2026 Las Vegas Raiders training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Raiders training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Las Vegas Raiders  camp is taking place at Intermountain Health Performance Center in Henderson, Nevada, and Raiders reporter Ryan McFadden has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Raiders camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 
 

 Latest news from Raiders camp 
 
 Maxx Crosby's approaching Raiders training camp with intensity 
 Three-time Pro Bowl guard Andrus Peat announces retirement 
 Cousins gets nod over Mendoza to open Raiders camp 
 What's next for Crosby, WR and CB rooms? 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 Through six practices, rookie wide receiver Malik Benson has made a strong case for meaningful snaps this fall.

 In a fairly thin wide receiver room, Benson has been a shining star, and that was the case on Tuesday. His and quarterback  Fernando Mendoza 's connection was on point. Mendoza repeatedly completed throws to Benson on crossing and comeback routes.

 During the one-on-one period, Benson matched up with fellow rookie cornerback Jermod McCoy on a few reps, in which the former Oregon pass catcher showed off his footwork and separation ability to make catches.

 Wide receivers Jalen Nailor and Tre Tucker are essentially options one and two in the room. Benson has emerged as WR3, outplaying Jack Bech and  Dont'e Thornton Jr . thus far. For wide receiver coach Zach Azzanni, the biggest improvement he has seen from Benson has been route running.

 "He's gotten a lot better at it," Azzanni said. "He's got a long way to go, but I'm pleased with where he's at because I knew he had the skill set to do it."

 Other observations: 

 
 Tight end Michael Mayer did not practice after injuring his nose on Monday. Mayer, who was not in uniform, observed practice from the sideline. Tight end Carter Runyon was also absent for the fourth straight practice. 
 Offensive line coach Rick Dennison believes starting right tackle DJ Glaze , who struggled last season, still has untapped potential. "He does have great length, and he uses his arm length well, and he's working really hard at it. He's made some progress," Dennison said. 
 Starting inside linebacker Nakobe Dean said his body feels great after not participating during OTAs and mandatory minicamp. He added that his decision to come to Las Vegas over the Dallas Cowboys was because of a "gut feeling" that the Raiders would be a better situation. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Fernando Mendoza had an up-and-down practice Monday, but coach Klint Kubiak understands the rookie will not be perfect all the time.

 "There will never be a perfect game or practice," Kubiak said. "I think he is doing a good job. I don't expect him to be perfect right now."

 The lowlights of Mendoza's performance included a few off-target throws during the team period and the one-on-one period between defensive backs and wide receivers. In 11-on-11, Mendoza's pass to Malik Benson in the middle of the field was slightly high and put the rookie wide receiver in a bad position to be nearly hit by safety Tristin McCollum .

 On the next play, he threw an incomplete pass to wide receiver Phillip Dorsett II .

 Mendoza also had snap issues, struggling to maintain control of the ball, but he managed to salvage the play. Kubiak said it's an issue he wants Mendoza to clean up.

 "That's a part of playing the position," Kubiak said. "... That's why the quarterback has to be one of the best athletes on the field. He has to be able to grab a low snap and be able to jump on it when it's over his head."

 

 Mendoza did bounce back toward the end of practice. His best throw was to Benson on a crossing route that led to a big gain. Later, he quickly threw the ball to wideout Shedrick Jackson on a slant.

 Still, Kubiak said it's too early to determine how well Mendoza can handle adversity.

 "There are 60-to-80 plays in a game. There are going to be ups and downs," Kubiak said. "What quarterback is gonna get the other 10 players playing at their best, that's what we're looking for."

 Another observation: 

 
 Tight end Michael Mayer left practice early because of a busted nose, but Kubiak said Mayer should be fine. 
 
 
 Sunday, Aug. 2 
 Sunday featured quarterback  Fernando Mendoza 's worst performance of training camp, as the defense was overpowering throughout the morning.

 During 11-on-11 work, Mendoza attempted a deep pass to rookie wide receiver Malik Benson . However, Mendoza's pass was underthrown, and cornerback Decamerion Richardson deflected the ball. When the Raiders were practicing two-minute situations, Mendoza and the second-team offense had pre-snap issues, prompting a timeout and the second team's replacement with the third team.

 Mendoza also threw his first interception of camp. In the 7-on-7 period, defensive back Greedy Vance intercepted Mendoza's pass attempt to wide receiver  Phillip Dorsett II . Vance perfectly read the pass and jumped in front of Dorsett to secure the ball.

 The offense did make some plays. Kirk Cousins and Brock Bowers connected on a few big throws in the middle of the field. Undrafted rookie running back Roman Hemby had a nice run down the middle. And  Aidan O'Connell  had the play of the day, throwing a touchdown pass to wide receiver E.J. Williams Jr.

 But for the most part, the defense had the upper hand. Linebacker Quay Walker and second-year defensive tackle  JJ Pegues  each recorded a sack. Defensive end Maxx Crosby was a force against the run. In the two-minute period, he quickly blew past right tackle DJ Glaze to stop running back Ashton Jeanty for a loss of yards. Rookie defensive end Keyron Crawford even had a nice run stop on Hemby while playing with the second team.

 Edge rusher Kwity Paye returned after leaving Friday's practice early. Reserve tight end Carter Runyon was the only player absent from practice.

 Raiders rookie cornerback  Jermod McCoy 's workload picked up, and he looked more comfortable on the field. He broke up O'Connell's pass to Williams early in practice. However, he was called for defensive pass interference while defending wide receiver  Shedrick Jackson .

If someone's making plays one day and you're not, the plays will come. Don't stress, because when you stress and try to force a play, that's when bad things happen."

 Right tackle Austin Jackson , tight end Greg Dulcich and safety Lonnie Johnson Jr . did not participate in Tuesday's practice because of what Hafley described as "day to day" injuries.  Willis did throw an interception off a tipped pass, but the ball placement certainly could've been better. He also missed a throw to a wide open Caleb Douglas , who got hands on the ball but couldn't come down with it. But Willis has flashed some touch over the past few practices.

 Linebacker Tyrel Dodson returned an interception for a touchdown in team drills, tracking the ball after it deflected off tight end Cole Turner 's hands. In Turner's defense, the ball from Willis was far too low.

 "(Last practice) we beat the offense, today they got us back," rookie cornerback Chris Johnson said. "So we're looking forward to taking the lead back tomorrow."

Douglas capped his day with a touchdown grab in the corner of the endzone during red-zone work, on another ball from Willis. His explosive athleticism was never a question; his next test will be remaining focused once pads come on next week.
