 Defensive tackle Zach Sieler beat rookie offensive lineman Kadyn Proctor for a sack on the final play of practice. Speaking afterward, Proctor said moments like that are a learning experience for him, and he appreciates competing with a veteran like Sieler. 
 Running back Donovan Edwards cut back and broke contain for a 15- to 20-yard touchdown run during red-zone work. He never quite built on an exciting sophomore season at Michigan, but he flashed some of his explosiveness on that play. 
 Willis scored on a designed quarterback run during red-zone drills. He's largely remained in the pocket during both spring and training camp practices, but he will certainly be utilized as a runner once the regular season begins.

 Quarterback Kyler Murray had by far his best day of training camp Saturday, pinpointing a series of downfield throws in traffic while taking the majority of the Vikings' first-team reps as his competition with J.J. McCarthy continues.

 Receiver Justin Jefferson , asked what he has seen from quarterbacks this week, said: "Improvement." Jefferson later said he hopes McCarthy will benefit from the competition no matter how it turns out.

 Left tackle Christian Darrisaw took his first veteran's rest day of camp Friday, part of the Vikings' plan to keep his left knee healthy following a season in which lingering soreness from an October 2024 injury limited him to 10 games.

title: What McCarthy-Murray QB battle means for Vikings' locker room
summary: While J.J. McCarthy and Kyler Murray compete for the starting job, their teammates are focused on helping both of them succeed.
full_text:
EAGAN, Minn. -- NFL teams rarely conduct the kind of quarterback competition the Minnesota Vikings have engaged in this summer, and there are some good reasons why. 

 From a practical sense, there aren't enough starting-caliber quarterbacks around the league for many teams to pit one against another. Practice reps are at a premium as coaches install complicated offenses. 

 Then there is also the possibility of unintended consequences -- namely that human nature will push players to support their personal favorite. 

 

 Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell has cited the team's culture and leadership as bulwarks against any drama that his competition between Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy could otherwise create. During the first week of camp, ESPN asked four of the Vikings' eight 2025 captains how they were maintaining neutrality in the locker room, assuming they were. 

 If anything, what emerged was a sense that they, too, are being judged on how they perform during the process.

 "Some people from the outside might have some noise and say the team's going to be divided and it's going to be this or that," safety Joshua Metellus said. "And our job as captains and leaders is to make sure the team is connected and knows that at the end of the day, there is competition in every room. This is just the one that's highlighted the most.

 "So it's just more about getting the guys to understand what we're here for and understanding that we're here to get them better. So we have to be on our stuff on the defensive side to make sure they can get good looks, and it's not one-sided."

 

 In his 10th season, running back Aaron Jones Sr. had never entered a training camp without an established starting quarterback. He spent six seasons in Green Bay playing with Aaron Rodgers before the Packers transitioned to Jordan Love in 2023. Sam Darnold took almost every first-team practice rep when Jones arrived in Minnesota for the 2024 season, and McCarthy was understood to be the top quarterback when camp began in 2025

 This summer, Jones said he has tried to remember how his performance -- and that of the rest of the offensive huddle -- could ultimately impact the competition's outcome.

 "I just want to make sure that each guy's putting their best foot forward for both guys," Jones said. "They're in a battle, so every rep is important for both of them. Dropped balls and different things like that, they matter. So everybody being at their best for all of our quarterbacks. And it'll make us that much better in the end, no matter who's back there calling the shots when the season comes, and it holds us accountable in a way.

 "Not that you ever want to go to camp with a quarterback battle or anything like that, but it raises the level of everybody's play."

 

 There is no doubt, however, that many players developed a personal affinity for McCarthy during the previous two years, drawn either by his connective personality or his efforts to overcome a rookie season lost to injury. They know that even in his third season, he is only 23 years old with 10 games and 243 pass attempts to his professional career. During an appearance this spring on the Green Light podcast, Vikings tackle Brian O'Neill said of McCarthy: "I love that kid. If I was judged after my first 10 games in the NFL, I'm not playing right now."

 Last week, O'Neill said he is absorbed more with micro issues related to the competition. 

 "Nobody's asking me, 'Hey go do this with them, go do this with them, go do this with whoever,'" he said. "It's about playing and obviously working through it if there's any difference in the cadence in the huddle or how it goes on the field working through that, but my job is to make it right for either of them. So that's kind of all I can focus on."

 Murray, on the other hand, is much quieter than McCarthy and less familiar with his surroundings. Whereas McCarthy might sprint 40 yards downfield to celebrate a big completion during practice, Murray is more likely to be waiting at the line of scrimmage to fist-bump the receiver. And as a veteran, Murray seems aware that everything he says publicly will be scrutinized for deeper meaning.

 On the first day of camp, in fact, Murray did not directly answer a question about which Vikings players he worked out with during his summer break. (NFL reporter Jordan Schultz posted video  on July 24 of Murray and receiver Jordan Addison throwing near Dallas.)

 Perhaps the most important voice is receiver Justin Jefferson , who has chosen his words carefully throughout the process. He has said repeatedly that it "doesn't matter" which quarterback O'Connell ultimately selects. 

 "It's a competition," Jefferson said. "It's all on who comes to practice and who's the better guy. At this point, it's still early in training camp for any of us to understand or know who's the No. 1 guy. So it's just all about pouring into both of them and making sure that whoever's the guy at the end of the day, we're not starting over or starting fresh."

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The New England Patriots ' camp is taking place in Foxborough, Massachusetts, and Patriots reporter Mike Reiss has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Patriots camp. We will update this file often. Will Drake Maye  start another MVP-like campaign in Year 3? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Patriots camp 
 
 A.J. Brown on injury: 'Thumb out of place, you keep going' 
 Patriots' Brown knows Vrabel's rip comes from 'great place' 
 Kraft: Patriots' Gonzalez has offer to be 'highest-paid' CB ever 
 Too many receivers? A look at the Patriots' crowded WR room 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Rookie outside linebacker Gabe Jacas answered questions from reporters Tuesday for the first time since missing the entire spring and signing a contract two days into training camp, saying he wasn't looking back.

 "First and foremost, I just want to say how grateful I am to be here," the second-round pick from Illinois told the assembled media after the ninth practice of training camp. "It was a long journey, but I'm just glad to be part of this organization. It's a blessing to be at practice and run around."

 Jacas underwent a procedure on his left knee in May, which led to his absence and contract impasse. His contract includes an injury waiver that protects the team if his knee isn't healthy through his first three seasons.

 He returned to practice for the first time Saturday and has been gradually increasing his workload since, which also includes one-on-one punt-protection work with coach Mike Vrabel. When asked about his knee, Jacas said he's "100%" and that he doesn't have long-range concerns.

 The Patriots have had eight-year veteran Dre'Mont Jones and second-year player Elijah Ponder as their starting outside linebackers in training camp, with nine-year veteran Harold Landry III  -- a starter in 2025 -- opening on the physically unable to perform list.

 The 6-foot-4, 261-pound Jacas, who wears Vrabel's old No. 50, projects as a top backup.

 "I will tell you this, he looks like an outside linebacker," Vrabel told Sirius XM NFL Radio. "I saw him in uniform and said, 'Well, this is kind of what they're supposed to look like.'"

 

 More observations: 

 
 Ponder had a pass breakup after dropping into coverage and getting in a passing lane to make life hard on QB Drake Maye , who was looking for TE Hunter Henry . 
 Backup QB Tommy DeVito had one of the highlight plays, delivering a deep pass (40ish yards) to WR Mack Hollins along the right sideline (CB Channing Canada closest in coverage). 
 Two-minute offense, which culminated with bringing the field goal unit onto the field, was part of the end-of-practice script. The first- and second-unit offenses were successful. 
 Kicker Andy Borregales was 7-of-7 overall. 
 Undrafted LB Khalil Jacobs (Missouri) repping ahead of veteran LB K.J. Britt on the punt-protection unit was notable, as Jacobs has also been getting some reps ahead of Britt on defense recently. 
 Second-year WR Kyle Williams , who had hobbled off Saturday and didn't participate Monday, returned to what looked like a full workload. 
 WR  Kayshon Boutte 's knack for tracking the football down the field showed up again, with him adjusting to snare a deep pass from DeVito. 
 Punt return was the primary special teams focus of the day, with Marcus Jones ,  DeMario "Pop" Douglas , Romeo Doubs , Efton Chism III and Kobe Prentice the returners. 
 Former quarterback Brian Hoyer was present, watching practice from the field with his son, Garrett. 
 Former receiver Danny Amendola was present and then took part in a USAA "combine" event. "Guys look good, man. I love the receiving corps. Drake Maye looks great," he told reporters. "Guys are flying around, the energy was high, it was great to see." 
 

 

 

 
 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Wide receiver Romeo Doubs ' transition from the Green Bay Packers to the New England Patriots has flown a bit under the radar since the arrival of A.J. Brown in early June.

 So, in a sense, it was fitting that on the day Doubs was scheduled to visit reporters after practice that Brown was once again dominating headlines (he dislocated his left thumb but practiced through it).

 He seems just fine with it.

 "The process has been really good," the soft-spoken Doubs said . "I love where I am, I love where our team is, I love the intensity of camp practices and things of that nature."

 Though Brown is the clear-cut No. 1 receiver, the 6-foot-2, 210-pound Doubs has most often lined up alongside him as the No. 2 option. That's what many projected after the Patriots signed Doubs to a four-year, $68 million base-value contract in March as an unrestricted free agent.

 The Patriots' top seven receivers are worthy of roster spots -- Brown, Doubs, Kayshon Boutte , Mack Hollins ,  DeMario "Pop" Douglas ,  Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III -- making it one of the most competitive positions on the roster.

 Doubs had a touchdown catch Monday as the team worked mostly in the red zone, with practice moved inside due to rain.

 Of his chemistry with Drake Maye, he said: "It's growing. It's a day-to-day grind. It takes a certain amount of trust. I'm glad to be around a guy like Drake. He's a leader. He's poised."

 Maye credited Doubs for learning the offense since his arrival, noting it was different than what he was accustomed to with the Packers.

 "He hasn't been in an offense like that has some decision-making [for receivers]. I think he's getting better and better as he's gotten through OTAs and even in camp, he's making some great plays for us. He's kind of shifty and has a little wiggle to him that I didn't really expect throwing to him in camp."

 More observations: 

 
 RB Terrell Jennings , who opened camp on the non-football injury list, passed his physical and practiced for the first time. He joins 2025 undrafted free agent Lan Larison , 2026 seventh-round draft pick Jam Miller and 2026 undrafted free agent Myles Montgomery in the competition for a roster spot behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson . 
 DT Milton Williams said rookie OLB Gabe Jacas , who hadn't been with the team in the spring and signed his contract two days into training camp, has been getting ribbed by coach Mike Vrabel in meetings, and he's handling it in stride. Williams said Jacas has been called in front of the team about five times by Vrabel, and he recently lightened the mood with a joke. 
 Kyle Williams, who hobbled off the field late in Saturday's practice, did not participate Monday. 
 Vrabel wore a scout-team linebacker jersey at one point in a walk-through portion of practice, and when he filled a gap to make a "tackle," he had a mock celebration by thrusting his right arm in the air. 
 Rookie CB Karon Prunty (fifth round, Wake Forest) had a pass breakup on a play in which Maye attempted to connect with Brown on a deep ball, which had the defense buzzing. 
 Prunty was in coverage on the final play of practice, when backup QB Tommy DeVito threw a fade to Boutte in the end zone, with the receiver flashing late hands for an impressive tight-window TD. 
 Undrafted WR Nick DeGennaro (James Madison) and Prunty had a shared-catch play on a deep ball from No. 3 QB Behren Morton along the right sideline. DeGennaro came away with the football after a lengthy period of time, but it's hard to say what an official might have ruled in a game. 
 Starting inside linebacker Christian…

 2026 New York Giants training camp preview 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 In his quest to make the roster, Tuesday was an important practice for Odell Beckham Jr . For the first time this summer he worked with the first-team offense for most of the day.

 Beckham caught a pair of passes and had another would've-been touchdown grab in a strong performance.

 Beckham worked alongside Darnell Mooney and Braxton Berrios on a day when Darius Slayton and Malachi Fields seemed to have their workloads limited. Malik Nabers continues to participate in individual drills but mostly stands around and watches when the team breaks into live periods.

 "Just probably worked out that way [Tuesday]," coach John Harbaugh said of Beckham working with the first team. "He ... I don't know, worked out that way."

 Regardless, Beckham continues to get open consistently. He might not look like Prime Odell, but he still can play and create separation.

 More observations: 

 
 Wide receiver  JuJu Smith-Schuster  sat out practice with knee swelling, according to Harbaugh. Smith-Schuster is also fighting for a roster spot. Look out for wide receiver Dalen Cambre . He had another strong day with three catches in live drills, including a touchdown from Jameis Winston on a rub route at the goal line. Cambre worked his way onto the Giants' roster in the second half of last season and played well on special teams. 
 The penalties that plagued the Giants on Monday were again a problem early in Tuesday's practice. They committed five more penalties in the second padded practice of the summer, including four in the first few live drills. 
 Rookie guard Francis Mauigoa had his ups and downs in one-on-ones. He got the better of Abdul Carter on their first matchup but was spun around after they immediately ran it back. Mauigoa did recover. Still, Carter beat him cleanly at the onset. 
 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 It was a rough day for the Giants' offense in pouring rain on the first day in full pads. The performance was really an extension of the early part of training camp for Jaxson Dart  & Co.

 A lot of penalties. Too many mental mistakes. Not enough positive plays. 
 
Dart threw an interception into the hands of safety Jevon Holland when the ball slipped out of the quarterback's hand while throwing. The Giants failed to score a touchdown on any of their drives and committed nine offensive penalties, everything from delay of games to endless false starts to holding by a wide receiver.

 "I think two things," coach John Harbaugh said. "I mean, I think you've got the elements a little bit, and you've got the first day in pads. So, it's not really unexpected, but we'll be working on it."

 Harbaugh added that he generally believes the offense is ahead of the defense early in camp. That seems not to be the case with his sloppy Giants as they digest new schemes.

 Other observations:  

 
 It was another strong practice from first-round pick Arvell Reese . The rookie linebacker had a run stop early in practice and later a sack when he beat left tackle Andrew Thomas . "The rookie has been impressive. Kid has a real chance to be special," veteran defensive tackle DJ Reader said. 
 Cornerback Deonte Banks is flashing early this summer. The former first-round pick has provided sticky coverage on receivers throughout camp. Monday's practice was no different. He tipped a pass that resulted in an interception by linebacker Micah McFadden . Banks later had Darius Slayton blanketed but dropped an interception that hit him in the chest. After some struggles, maybe Banks has it figured out? 
 
 
 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 It has been a quiet start to training camp from Odell Beckham Jr .

 Until Saturday.

 On the day when the Giants had their largest crowd of the summer at The Greenbrier in West Virginia, Beckham made the biggest play of the day. And received the biggest ovation of the summer to date.

 The veteran receiver made a leaping grab over a defender in the back of the end zone for a touchdown from quarterback Jameis Winston during 11-on-11 drills. It sent the crowd of approximately 2,000 fans into a frenzy and served as a reminder of what used to be.

 It was a big play for Beckham, who is battling for a roster spot with several other veterans. Braxton Berrios has stood out the most of the group this camp, until Saturday.

 "There's a lot of really good football players in our room right now," wide receiver Darius Slayton said. "From a competition-level standpoint, it's ... raised the competition level."

 Other observations: 

 
 Malik Nabers was back on the practice field after a day of rest Friday. He looked good running routes. This is a positive sign as he recovers from a serious knee injury that required multiple surgeries."[Saturday] seemed like a good day from what I can tell," coach John Harbaugh said. 
 Jaxson Dart and the offense have struggled the past few days. Saturday was an up-and-down practice for the second-year quarterback learning a new offense. It began with a feathery deep ball down the left sideline to Malachi Fields . Two plays later, Dart had a pass tipped by linebacker Tremaine Edmunds and intercepted by Paulson Adebo . Later, he had a bad interception to Edmunds and hit tight end Theo Johnson on a deep ball. Overall, Dart went 22-of-33 in live drills. 
 The Giants have the day off Sunday and return Monday for the first full practice with pads, which is the closest to real football we'll see before the preseason. Harbaugh said the Giants won't tackle to the ground. It will be "wrap and release," but it will be more physical. "It's almost that time," outside linebacker Kayvon Thibodeaux said. 
 

 

 Friday, July 31 

 Second-year linebacker Abdul Carter has enjoyed a strong start to training camp. It has him thinking big.

 His goal: "Be Defensive Player of the Year, for sure."

 Can it be this year?

 "Absolutely," he said.

 Why?

 "Just my process. I know who I can be and the belief in myself. I know what I'm capable of and I know if I put the work in and believe in myself, trust in myself, trust in my teammates, trust in my coaches, I can be whoever I want to be."

 Lofty goal after 4.0 sacks as a rookie. But Carter feels he learned a lot from last year, when he was benched twice for missing and being late to meetings. He thinks he hit his stride late in the season and can carry it into the next year.

 Other observations: 

 
 Second-year defensive lineman Darius Alexander ended practice with a leaping interception of Jaxson Dart near the line of scrimmage. The Giants were in field goal range at the time and it ended a sloppy practice that was filled with penalties on both sides of the ball. 
 Kicking update: It was Ben Sauls ' turn Friday and he made eight of his 10 field goal attempts. 
 
 

 Thursday, July 30 
 Pass rusher  Abdul Carter reminded everyone why he…

title: 2026 New York Jets training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Jets training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  New York Jets  camp is taking place at the Atlantic Health Training Facility in Florham Park, New Jersey, and Jets reporter Rich Cimini has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Jets camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football, and which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Jets camp 
 
 Rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq to miss time after hernia setback 
 Jets' Smith rues being 'distraction' after dispute with girlfriend 
 2026 Jets training camp preview 
 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 For months, the Jets have been boasting about their tight-end depth. They will get a chance to show it off in the coming weeks.

 First-round pick Kenyon Sadiq suffered a setback from May hernia surgery and will be sidelined "a little bit," according to coach Aaron Glenn.

 Translation: He probably will miss at least a chunk of the preseason, affording more opportunities for Mason Taylor , Jeremy Ruckert and Jelani Woods .

 Ruckert capitalized Tuesday, making a team-high four receptions in practice. It was a mixed day for Taylor, who had one catch and one drop. He also was the targeted receiver on a Geno Smith pass that was intercepted.

 "I see him breaking out this year," Glenn said of Taylor, a 2025 second-round pick who made a team-high 44 receptions for 369 yards last season.

 The Jets surprised the draft world when they picked Sadiq 16th overall, one year after taking Taylor. Ruckert was a 2022 third-round pick. Yes, they've invested heavily at tight end.

 This year's plan is to use more two-tight end packages, integrating Sadiq's elite speed and versatility into the offensive equation. Those plans will be on hold. While the Jets are "very confident" that Sadiq will be back for Week 1, per Glenn, they will have to adjust on the fly with Taylor, Ruckert and Woods.

 Other observations: 

 
 The starting defense made an interception for the second day in a row. This time it was CB Brandon Stephens , who snared a Smith pass that was deflected downfield. After going interception-less for the entire 2025 season, unprecedented in NFL history, it would be an understatement to say the Jets are emphasizing takeaways. 
 It was a nice day for the running backs, especially Breece Hall and Braelon Allen , both of whom busted long runs in the second padded practice. Allen, who had knee surgery last season, came to camp at 244 pounds, slightly above his ideal playing weight (240). Allen said he's been looking forward to this season from the moment he got off the operating table. 
 WR Isaiah Williams doesn't generate much fanfare for his offense -- he's known for this kick returning -- but he made the catch of the day, a falling-down, over-the-shoulder grab. "He's a dude," Glenn said. In Glenn-speak, that's a high compliment. 
 Backup MLB Kiko Mauigoa made a big downfield hit, jarring the ball loose from rookie WR Omar Cooper Jr . Mauigoa is getting a chance to solidify himself as Demario Davis ' understudy. 
 Kingsley Enagbare didn't practice -- on Monday, he got stepped on -- leaving the defense thin on the edge. They're already without Joseph Ossai (PUP list). It afforded for more reps for Will McDonald IV . Enagbare's injury isn't serious, per Glenn. 
 No practice Wednesday, their third off day out of the first eight days in camp. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 There was an unusual occurrence on the practice field -- an interception by the defense, the first of training camp for the starters.

 Former All-Pro safety  Minkah Fitzpatrick , one of the Jets' marquee additions, picked off Geno Smith 's first pass in 11-on-11 drills -- a noteworthy feat, considering last season's ignominy.

 You may have heard: The Jets were the first team in NFL history to go an entire season without intercepting a pass. We're talking about almost a full century; the league started tracking interceptions in 1933.

 The defensive backs, in particular, are determined to end the embarrassing slump. They dream about getting takeaways.

 "Shoot, I tell that to myself, even in my sleep," cornerback  Brandon Stephens  said after practice.

 It's one of the big reasons why they traded for Fitzpatrick and gave him a three-year, $40 million contract . Since entering the league in 2018, he's tied for ninth in interceptions (21).

 "He's extremely smart and he loves football -- and at safety, that's what you're looking for," coach Aaron Glenn said of Fitzpatrick. "Look, I've had some good safeties in my career. Early on, I like exactly where he's at."

 Fitzpatrick can line up in multiple spots. On his interception, he was in the deep middle. He got an assist from LB Demario Davis , who got nice depth in his pass drop. It forced Smith into an overthrow, with the pass going directly to Fitzpatrick.

 An easy pick -- if there is such a thing for this defense.

 Other observations:  

 
 Injury updates: Rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq , who participated in the first three practices after offseason hernia surgery, got a rest day as part of his maintenance program. NT T'Vondre Sweat (hamstring), DE Joseph Ossai (undisclosed) and rookie CB D'Angelo Ponds (calf) still haven't practiced. They will be sidelined at least another week, per Glenn. Sweat is on the non-football injury list, Ossai the PUP list. 
 There were several dropped passes in wet, rainy conditions -- the first practice in pads. One player who didn't struggle was rookie WR  Omar Cooper Jr ., who made a terrific, over-the-shoulder catch on a deep ball from Smith. Cooper is expected to have a significant role. 
 RT Armand Membou is having a strong camp. After a solid rookie year, the 2025 first-round pick is poised for a breakout. Glenn praised his mindset, saying he noticed in last season's exit meeting that Membou "was on a mission and you saw it on his face. There was no B.S." Membou's daily battles with rookie DE David Bailey are must-see. 
 CB Azareye'h Thomas changed his number in the offseason, dropping 23 and opting for 1, famously worn by Sauce Gardner for three-plus seasons. Thomas recognizes the pressure that comes with that number, but he didn't make the switch because he wants to be the next Sauce. He cited his faith, saying he plays "for an audience of one" -- God. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 

 Geno Smith pitched a perfect practice on Saturday.

 The Jets' starting quarterback completed every pass in 11-on-11 periods (11-for-11) and did the same in 7-on-7 (4-for-4). Yes, it was a non-contact unpadded practice, and, yes, most of the reps came in the red zone -- favorable circumstances for a quarterback. But let's not lose sight of the big picture. Any time a Jets quarterback can go an entire practice without the ball hitting the ground ... well, let's just say it's noteworthy.

 Coach Aaron Glenn credited offensive coordinator Frank Reich and quarterbacks coach Bill Musgrave with helping Smith to a quick start.

 "I think he and Frank are on the same page," Glenn said after practice. "Our quarterbacks coach is doing a hell of a job, teaching him and actually expanding his knowledge as far as what we're trying to do. And one good thing about Geno is, for as long as he's been in this league, he's still learning. I think that's a good trait for any player, that we don't know it all and we can pick up something new from a new coach."

 Smith's primary target was WR Garrett Wilson (five catches in 11-on-11), who came alive after two quiet practices. WR Adonai Mitchell , who caught two of Smith's four…

title: 2026 Philadelphia Eagles training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Eagles training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Philadelphia Eagles camp is taking place in the Jefferson Health Training Complex, and Eagles reporter Tim McManus has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and -- of course -- the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Eagles camp. We will update this file often. How will quarterback  Jalen Hurts fare in the reimagined offense? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Eagles camp 
 
 Eagles, DT Carter agree to four-year, $152M extension 
 2026 Philadelphia Eagles training camp preview 
 Eagles coach Nick Sirianni adjusting to offseason changes 
 
 
 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Eagles receivers DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon both missed practice with hamstring injuries. The team is not expressing any long-term concern with either player. Still, these are meaningful reps -- especially for a rookie. Lemon missed minicamp as well with a hamstring injury. He has served primarily as the starting slot receiver when healthy but hasn't produced many splash moments to date. It's important Jalen Hurts gets as many snaps as possible with his skill players as the offense breaks in a new system in the post A.J. Brown era.

 Other observations:  

 
 Standout right tackle Lane Johnson was absent (excused/not injury related) for the third straight practice. The team declined to provide further details given that it is a personal matter. Rookie Markel Bell received first-team reps in his absence and appeared to hold his own. 
 With a number of starters missing, it wasn't a big surprise the offense sputtered. Penalties made for a clunky, rhythmless practice with few highlights. 
 It's important to note that new plays are being installed in the early portion of camp, so it makes sense why the offensive operation can look rough in spots. It's no coincidence that the offense's breakout day on Monday was a review of plays that had been installed previously. In other words, patience is required. 
 Linebacker Jihaad Campbell had perhaps his strongest showing of the summer. He sliced into the backfield to stifle a pitch to Saquon Barkley . Moments later, he fired in on a blitz and delivered a hit on would-be blocker Tank Bigsby that sent Bigsby flying to the turf. 
 In that same series, DT Byron Young got free on a pass rush, forcing a Cam Jurgens holding penalty. Between Jalen Carter , Jordan Davis , Moro Ojomo , Young and others, the defensive tackle spot appears to be in superb shape. 
 
 
 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Quarterback Jalen Hurts had his best day of camp to date. It started with a deep sideline throw to Dontayvion Wicks followed by a dot to Elijah Moore down the right seam. Hurts lit it up in the red zone, finding DeVonta Smith for a pair of touchdowns before running in for another score moments later, leading to a leaping celebration with Saquon Barkley and other teammates. There was one notable blemish on the day -- a short pass to Moore that was jumped by Quinyon Mitchell for a pick-six -- but the practice was defined by sharp, on-time throws, including one deep over the middle that led to a highlight diving catch by Darius Cooper .

 Other observations: 

 
 Right tackle Lane Johnson (excused/not injury related) was absent for a second straight practice. Rookie receiver Makai Lemon did not participate in team drills after taking part in individual drills earlier in the session. 
 The second-team defense got work against the first-team offense. Credit linebacker Chance Campbell for sniffing out a Barkley run to the outside and darting into the backfield to make a stop. 
 Andy Dalton appeared to outplay Tanner McKee as the battle for the No. 2 QB spot continues. Dalton fired a completion over the middle to Johnny Wilson with Jihaad Campbell looming in coverage. McKee underthrew Wilson later in the session and appeared to hold onto the ball for too long at times in the red zone. 
 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 The Eagles' defense flexed its muscles, making for some tough sledding for Jalen Hurts  & Co. over the one-hour, 40-minute session. Hurts had two passes batted at the line of scrimmage to start the session -- first by Zack Baun , then Jalen Carter . That set the tone for a day defined by heavy pressure and little flow to the pass game.

 Carter, fresh off signing a mega-extension , was a problem, and the same can be said for Jalyx Hunt , who has spent much of training camp to date in the backfield.

 Other observations: 

 
 Jeremiah Trotter Jr . got the nod at starting linebacker in Jihaad Campbell 's absence (excused/not injury-related) and made his presence felt, showing good anticipation to disrupt the short-to-intermediate passing game. 
 Safety Andrew Mukuba and rookie receiver Makai Lemon collided over the middle of the field going after what proved to be a Hurts incompletion. Fortunately, no one was injured on the play. Lemon has seen plenty of action as the primary slot receiver but has had a relatively quiet start to camp. 
 Receiver Dontayvion Wicks had another quality practice. He made a contested catch over the middle and muscled through Michael Carter II for some yards after the catch. 
 

 

 Thursday, July 30 
 New Eagles receiver Dontayvion Wicks made the play of the day and may have earned more of Jalen Hurts ' trust in the process. Near the end of Thursday's practice, Hurts unfurled a pass deep down the field to Wicks, who was double covered by defensive backs Cole Wisniewski and Jakorian Bennett . Wicks elevated over both of them and secured the catch.

 The former Packer is trying to solidify his spot as the No. 2 wideout in this offense alongside DeVonta Smith . Coach Nick Sirianni has clearly taken a liking to him, comparing Wicks to the accomplished Keenan Allen .

 Other observations:  

 
 There is a heavy amount of misdirection in Sean Mannion's offense. It helped open up big holes for the running backs Thursday, with Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby taking advantage for sizable gains. Bigsby brings some juice and likely earned some more playing time in 2026 after averaging 5.9 yards per attempt for the Eagles last season. 
 Rookie QB Cole Payton came down to earth following a strong performance Wednesday, throwing interceptions on back-to-back plays. 
 Second-year corner Mac McWilliams muscled an Andy Dalton pass away from running back Elijah Mitchell for the breakup. Credit veteran corner Jonathan Jones for blanketing DeVonta Smith down the field to force an incompletion. 
 
 

 Wednesday, July 29 
 There were some encouraging signs from the Eagles' new-look offense on Day 1 of camp. The learning curve they're working through is obvious -- there was one sequence where a pre-snap penalty was followed by a botched running play when  Jalen Hurts and Saquon Barkley were on different pages. But there were also moments where things clicked, like on a hookup between Hurts and DeVonta Smith where Hurts dropped to his right and zipped a strike to his now-No. 1 receiver down the left seam with Quinyon Mitchell tight in coverage.

 Hurts worked primarily under center and targeted the middle of the field a good amount, departures from how he has generally operated to this point in the NFL. There was enough good mixed in to consider it a positive opening to the summer.

 More observations: 

 
 Quarterbacks Tanner McKee and Andy Dalton split second-team reps. The two rotated days as the primary backup in the spring. This is developing into an interesting competition. If the Eagles feel comfortable having either in that role, it would…

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Pittsburgh Steelers ' camp is taking place in Latrobe, Pennsylvania, and Steelers reporter Brooke Pryor has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Steelers camp. We will update this file often. How will coach Mike McCarthy shape this roster and the offense in his first year in Pittsburgh? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Steelers camp 
 
 Steelers' Broderick Jones cleared after eight months (neck) 
 Rodgers: 'Zero debate' 2026 will be last season 
 Jalen Ramsey, Joey Porter Jr. placed on PUP list 
 Steelers revamp wide receiver unit 
 Rodgers reunites with family ahead of final NFL season 
 
 
 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Midway through an individual period of the Steelers' Tuesday practice, the "Monday Night Football" jingle interrupted the Drake song that had been playing over the speakers on the St. Vincent College practice fields.

 The players paused, processing what they were hearing, then dropped everything and ran to the 5-yard line at the other end of the field. Center Zach Frazier snapped the ball as soon as the first-team offense lined up against the first-team defense, kicking off a series of five quick red zone plays.

 The offense scored just once as Mason Rudolph hit Ben Skowronek in the end zone, while the defense got three stops and was flagged for pass interference in the end zone. As soon as those five snaps were over, the DJ resumed playing Drake, and the players went back to their individual drill stations to finish the period.

 That officially marked the first "Mojo Moment" of coach Mike McCarthy's Steelers tenure.

 "I think that period is awesome because it simulates a real game," defensive lineman Sebastian Joseph-Day said. "Down 14-0, what are you going to do? A sudden change, and now you're on your 5-yard line, you got to get a stop. What do you do? And I feel like that is really going to help us prepare for those moments."

 Named for the Austin Powers movie franchise, the surprise drill Mojo Moment is a midpractice pop quiz. It can come at any time, and it's meant to ingrain the importance of staying ready in the players.

 "If you're prepared, then it's an easy test," safety DeShon Elliott said.

 McCarthy did it during practices in Dallas, too. Elliott remembers waiting out a rain delay against the Cowboys a couple of years ago. The Mojo Moment drill would've come in handy then, he said.

 "You got to sit inside a little bit, and then you got to come back out and get started right now," Elliott said. "So I think that's what he was trying to simulate, just being able to go out there and see who can really [tough it out] when it's time to in situations like that."

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Cornerback Jamel Dean had an up-and-down practice. He was burned a couple of times, including by Roman Wilson on a slant in the end zone for a score in an 11-on-11 period. On the very next play, DK Metcalf beat him on a quick out for a score, too. But Dean responded with two pass breakups in the practice-ending two-minute drill, each as he guarded Wilson in tight coverage. 
 Elliott is still working his way back from a season-ending knee injury suffered midway through last season, but he plans to ramp up his practice participation next week. "I really feel good," he said. "I feel fast, explosive, cutting, making plays. It's a process. I'll be ready Week 1." 
 After a relatively mild first day in pads Monday, the Steelers were noticeably more energetic and chippy in Tuesday's practice before Wednesday's light walk-through day. Joseph-Day and tackle Troy Fautanu got into a verbal altercation at the end of a one-on-one pass rush period when Joseph-Day took exception to where Fautanu lined up. McCarthy, though, wanted his team to turn up the intensity Tuesday, and he said as much in team meetings before practice. "Just picking up the urgency, picking up the physicality and things like that," running back Rico Dowdle said of McCarthy's message. "He talked about that before practice, and I think it came out today." 
 

 
 Monday, Aug. 3 
 The Steelers' Monday morning meeting featured a different kind of film study before their first day in pads. Instead of practice footage, coach Mike McCarthy pulled up the viral video of tight end Pat Freiermuth pulling a kid out from the crush of fans crowding the fence in an attempt to get autographs from players after Saturday's practice.

 "That was hilarious," quarterback Will Howard said of the video, adding that they dubbed Freiermuth the "unsung hero of the week" for his quick thinking to protect the young fan.

 "Situational awareness. We talk about it all the time. On and off the field."

 A scrum broke out between a couple of adults Saturday as Freiermuth and his teammates worked the autograph line, a hallmark of the Steelers' practices at St. Vincent College. Freiermuth noticed a child in front of him and snagged him, lifting him up and over the mesh fence as the the shoving escalated.

 "I just saw a bunch of people tumbling down and fighting," Freiermuth said. "I looked down at the kid I was signing for, and he looked a little scared, so it was the least I could do."

 Freiermuth also joked the fans weren't fighting over his autograph, but instead they wanted one from Howard.

 "If you're going to fight for an autograph, it can't be Will Howard's," he said with a laugh. While Howard was quick to say he doesn't condone fans -- especially adults -- fighting over his autograph, he added that the fan element of Steelers training camp is part of what makes it special.

 "Yeah, it's crazy," Howard said. "It's a good feeling to be wanted. And at this point, I just want to give them something to cheer about because I really haven't been able to go out in the field and give them any product to really cheer for."

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 The defense won each of the practice-ending two-minute drills. The first came as linebacker Patrick Queen picked off Aaron Rodgers in the end zone on a pass that appeared to be intended for running back Rico Dowdle . On the second, Howard's final heave to the end zone on fourth down was broken up by rookie cornerback Daylen Everette . 
 Despite coach Mike McCarthy saying he was "absolutely" a fan of backs-on-backers, the Steelers' first day of padded practice didn't feature that physical drill. Instead, the Steelers had an offensive line vs. pass rush period during 7-on-7. 
 Wide receiver Cole Burgess left practice on a cart after appearing to injure his knee as he tried to catch a deep pass from Howard. Earlier in the day, Burgess hauled in a deep ball from rookie quarterback Drew Allar . 
 First-round pick Max Iheanachor worked primarily as the second-team right tackle throughout practice and turned in a solid performance. "He's making strides every single day, and he works really hard," said left tackle Troy Fautanu , who was the team's 2024 first-round pick. "I'm excited for him and for the rest of the training camp and how it plays out." 
 Rodgers told Mike Silver of The Athletic that he expected to play in the Steelers' two home preseason games. McCarthy seemingly confirmed the plan, though said it hasn't been finalized. "He'd like to play," McCarthy said Monday morning. "I would like to see him play, but we won't make a decision until we get all the way up to it because there's more that goes into that, just having one player play. It's the…

title: 'Tempered': Inside Mike McCarthy's new vision for Steelers
summary: Pittsburgh's new coach is blending sports science and the city's steel-making roots to forge a different camp culture.
full_text:
LATROBE, Pa. -- After leaving their first team meeting of the 2026 training camp Wednesday morning, the Pittsburgh Steelers found new shirts hanging in their lockers at St. Vincent College.

 "Tempered" stretched across the black shirt in gold lettering, and the back expanded on the definition of the slogan: "More than talented. More than tough. Tempered."

 "[It's about] the parallels between the city of Pittsburgh, the Steel Mill industry, the tempering process of how steel was built -- and still is today -- and the parallels between coming together as a football team," coach Mike McCarthy told ESPN.

 McCarthy said as much to his team in their first meeting, that they should be a reflection of the city's gritty heritage. It's why McCarthy chose "tempered" as the defining word of his first training camp as the Steelers' new head coach.

 

 "We have to be tough, hard, and this is a blue-collar town," Steelers guard Spencer Anderson said, relaying what McCarthy told them. "Button up, bring your lunch pail and let's go, because that's always where we've been since 1933. ... Can't fold under the heat. And when the heat comes, you got to make steel -- or I guess do the right things, so to speak."

 But tempered in McCarthy's use has dual meanings. Not only can it mean toughened and made resilient, but it can also mean being controlled. To McCarthy, tempered isn't just about raw strength. It's about being controlled in the approach to building that strength. And through a week of training camp, McCarthy's practices have been deliberately, even scientifically, tempered to train the mind as much as the body.

 "Everything's calculated," McCarthy said, adding that he relies on GPS data on devices worn by players to help construct his practice plan. "Everything's regulated. There's obviously science behind it. We're in tune with the conditioning of our players. The commitment the players made in the spring was evident. ... This is all by design. There's history behind it. ... Everybody has a genetic background that you pay attention to. Some guys can rev higher than others. And so this is part of the process."

 Through five practices, the differences between McCarthy's approach and former coach Mike Tomlin's are palpable. One isn't necessarily better than the other, players stressed, but the practices are different.

 "We're used to a hundred miles an hour, nonstop, and we're kind of dead tired by the end of practice," Anderson said. "But now we can kind of temper it down, and we still have maybe 10% left in the tank. But obviously don't tell [McCarthy] I said that."

 Part of that, of course, is the team is still in its ramp-up period with shorter practices as mandated by the collective bargaining agreement. But McCarthy is also heavily reliant on sports science in formulating his practice plans. That's why Monday's practice, the Steelers' first in pads, was noticeably less physical than the first padded practices in the Tomlin era (2007 to 2025).

 

 "It did feel different when I'm used to all that physical," Pittsburgh running back Jaylen Warren said Monday. "But I understand why we don't do it, and the philosophy behind it. Just adapting to it. ... At the end of the day, we're trying to keep guys up, keep them healthy. The season's the most important thing and winning is the most important thing."

 Warren told reporters Saturday he was certain that even with McCarthy's changes, the team would still go through the signature backs-on-backers drill. During Tomlin's tenure, it was a highlight of padded practices, often beginning with the first one, in which running backs and linebackers matched up in a one-on-one battle. Monday, though, the running backs and linebackers didn't square off. Instead, the offensive linemen and pass rushers went against one another while the skill position players worked in a 7-on-7 period.

 "As long as we have it, I'm prepared," Warren said of backs-on-backers. "I'm trusting the process that they got us going through, so I ain't complaining about nothing."

 McCarthy, who said he is "absolutely" a fan of backs-on-backers, might still have the drill in a future padded practice, but one thing he won't have is live tackling. While most of the league also spurns live tackling in camp, Tomlin embraced it in his ultra-physical late afternoon practices.

 "The only thing that's different is we don't want to go to the ground and risk injury, but I think everything else will look the same," McCarthy said, affirming that his practices would still be plenty physical.

 To coach tackling without actually doing it, McCarthy and his staff are breaking down the basic elements of the skill. In fact, the majority of McCarthy's early practices are all about the fundamentals -- the "Steelers Six" -- coached through meticulously scripted and executed individual periods. That's a departure from a Tomlin era that featured extensive team periods and always opened with "Seven Shots," an intense goal line competition.

 

 "A lot of Coach T's camps, it was a lot of team periods and mano-a-mano type of thing, but this is kind of more, get good work, working smart and hard," Anderson said. "Not to say that we weren't working smart back then, but it's just Coach McCarthy explains to us that he's a big sports science guy, so he'll never run us into the ground or do things that'll make us feel like we're dead tired. I think it's a good balance of work and taking care of us."

 Through five practices, McCarthy's training camp hasn't featured a single goal-line team period. Instead, in addition to the extensive individual periods, McCarthy has emphasized situational football -- working first on two-minute offense and then beginning the second week of camp with third and fourth downs. By stressing those situations in his up-tempo practices, McCarthy is strengthening the team's nervous system and mental fortitude.

 "Everybody talks about the physical and the mental stress of a physical camp," McCarthy said, explaining the cadence of his practices. "Well, what the hell about the nervous system? Who's training that? How are you tapping that? How are you pushing that? Where are you getting that at? Where's the mental toughness? Where's the emotional toughness? How do you train that on a football field? This is all by design."

 And though McCarthy's approach is an adjustment for players who grew accustomed to Tomlin's camps, many are embracing change.

 "I got to," said Cam Heyward, the longest-tenured Steeler. "The dinosaurs didn't, and look what happened to them."

title: 2026 Seattle Seahawks training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Seahawks training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Seattle Seahawks ' camp is taking place in Renton, Washington, and Seahawks reporter Brady Henderson has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Seahawks camp. We will update this file often. What is new with the defending Super Bowl champions? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp previews for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Seahawks camp 
 
 WR Tory Horton healthy after cracking tibia last season 
 Seattle Pro Bowl DL Williams confirms deal talks 
 Seattle's Nick Emmanwori has ankle surgery, expected to play W1 
 Who are the Khoslas? Meet the family set to buy the Seahawks 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 As Brian Fleury prepares to call plays for the first time, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald is trying to help his new offensive coordinator by hindering him.

 "Mike is doing a great job of putting me through the wringer in terms of challenging situations," Fleury said Tuesday. "We go through different ones every day. For some reason, we're always down by a touchdown with 50 seconds left and no timeouts. I don't know who's burning through the timeouts, but it definitely helps me adjust to those situations."

 When Klint Kubiak left to become the  Las Vegas Raiders ' head coach a day after Seattle's Super Bowl LX victory, Macdonald initially thought he'd likely find his next OC by promoting from within. He wanted offensive continuity, and when he interviewed Fleury -- who came from a similar West Coast system in San Francisco to what the Seahawks ran under Kubiak -- he realized how aligned they were in their vision and mentality.

 It was enough to make up for his absence of playcalling experience, but as Fleury readily admits, "doing it for the first time at this level is going to present some challenges."

 While much of Seattle's playbook will remain the same, one likely change will be an increase in shifts and motions. The time those can take off the play clock increases the need for an offense to operate efficiently between each snap. That begins with Fleury getting his playcalls out on time.

 "I try to make it harder on myself," Fleury said. "There's a lot of thought that'll go into it beforehand, going into a game. You'll have stuff all laid out on your sheet, but I try and challenge myself at times just to think off the top of my head and see if I can get it out on time for the sake of the quarterbacks and the playcall. We're practicing all the time."

 More observations: 

 
 After Riq Woolen 's departure in free agency, No. 3 cornerback is among the jobs that's up for grabs on Seattle's defense. The competition is on between incumbent Nehemiah Pritchett and free agent addition Noah Igbinoghene . "I think Nehemiah's doing a great job and I think as we go, you'll see who else shows up and just wait for the opportunity," defensive coordinator Aden Durde said. "I think the games and when we go against different people, that will really show itself. When we put pads on and you have to tackle and you have to play our style, we'll find out." 
 Igbinoghene, a 2020 first-round pick who can play inside and on the perimeter, blew up a run play Tuesday when he blitzed from the slot. "I think he's shown up a lot on early-down football, coming up, hitting the run, doing some great things in man," Durde said. "I think he's shown some great things." 
 Third-round pick Julian Neal could enter the No. 3 cornerback competition, but he has missed the past week with an undisclosed injury. Macdonald has described it as a "shorter-term" issue. 
 Also still sidelined Tuesday were WR Jake Bobo , DL Mike Morris , LBs Jamie Sheriff and Chris Paul Jr ., and FB Robbie Ouzts . RB Jacardia Wright didn't practice after injuring his foot Monday. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 The play of the day on Monday was one that Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald had been wanting to see.

 With Seattle's No. 1 offense facing the No. 2 defense in an 11-on-11 session, Sam Darnold found Rashid Shaheed deep down the middle of the field for a touchdown. Shaheed had gained more than a step on speedy rookie cornerback Michael Dansby , and Darnold hit him in perfect stride.

 "We got it thrown over our head finally, so that was a good wakeup call for us on defense," Macdonald said. "But that's definitely a point of emphasis after this first week is trying to get Rashid the ball on some of those deeper targets."

 The Seahawks might not have claimed the NFC's No. 1 seed last year or won Super Bowl LX if it weren't for their midseason acquisition of Shaheed, whom they re-signed in March to a three-year, $51 million deal. But his playmaking mostly came on special teams, where he scored three return touchdowns.

 His offensive production -- an average of 29.3 scrimmage yards over 12 games with Seattle -- left something to be desired, especially considering he had previously played for then-coordinator Klint Kubiak in New Orleans.

 While the playbook wasn't new to Shaheed, the quarterback was, and their lack of familiarity may have played some role in the receiver's underwhelming production. Even on the biggest offensive play he made for Seattle -- a 51-yard catch in the NFC Championship Game -- their timing was off by a hair, as Shaheed had to break his stride just enough to allow the cornerback he had beaten to catch back up and prevent a touchdown.

 The two couldn't connect on a pair of deep throws in the Super Bowl, one of which was sightly overthrown.

 But they did on Monday.

 "There's way more banked reps underneath our belt," Macdonald said of Darnold and Shaheed, who got together for throwing sessions over the summer in Southern California, where both are from. "I think both guys are in a really good place. Kind of the challenge of camp is, how far can we take it? Really, that's what we're focusing on right now, is how far can we take that relationship? How far can we take his route tree? How great of a timing can we create with those two guys?"

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Macdonald said the undisclosed injury that has kept rookie CB Julian Neal out for the last few days is a "shorter-term" issue. 
 Also remaining out Monday were WR Jake Bobo , DL Mike Morris , LBs Jamie Sheriff and Chris Paul Jr ., OLB Jared Ivey and FB Robbie Ouzts . "We're going to try to find some more information with Robbie's situation," Macdonald said. "I'll just leave it at that right now. We'll have an update for you sooner than later." 
 Macdonald recently lauded CB Devon Witherspoon for continuing to bring his usual enthusiasm despite his unsettled contract situation. He gave similar praise Monday to DT Leonard Williams , who recently said that his agents and the Seahawks have talked about an extension. "To be able to manage that and still be a person that he is every day and be the asset that he is for the rest of his teammates and put the football product on the field like he is every day, it's pretty remarkable," Macdonald said. "Spoon's doing the same thing. You really just tip your cap to him, honestly." 
 The Seahawks got a visit Monday from San Antonio Spurs coach Mitch Johnson and several other members of that organization. Johnson is a Seattle native and Seahawks fan. Macdonald said they share an alignment in "how we want to run our programs" as well as the experience of having taken over for a legendary coach (Pete Carroll in Seattle, Gregg Popovich in San Antonio). 
 Among the ex-Seahawks in attendance was Duane Brown , Seattle's left tackle from 2017 to…

title: 2026 Tennessee Titans training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Titans training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Tennessee Titans ' camp is taking place at the Vanderbilt Health Football Center, and Titans reporter Turron Davenport has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Titans camp. We will update this file often. We are looking at who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football, and which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Titans news: 

 
 Will Levis: There aren't 32 QBs better than me 
 Titans WRs join Cam Ward in Miami to build chemistry 
 2026 Titans training camp preview 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 The middle linebacker competition is heating up. James Williams Sr . has strung three consecutive standout days.

 Williams said he's lost about 20 pounds this offseason. The converted safety looked like a defensive back on a jumping one-handed interception of a Mitchell Trubisky pass during team period. Williams got a pass breakup later in practice when Trubisky went to tight end  Kylen Granson  on an out-breaking route.

 Titans defensive coordinator Gus Bradley spoke glowingly of Williams before practice.

 "We like those guys that have played safety in their career and move them down the linebacker," Bradley said. "That pass coverage part of it, that safety background that he has, I think allows him to be a little bit more instinctive."

 Williams worked alongside rookie linebacker Anthony Hill Jr . mostly. Hill added a couple of interceptions as well, both off Trubisky. One of the interceptions came because Trubisky hit his hand on an offensive lineman's helmet.

 Other observations:  

 
 DT  Jeffery Simmons and OL  Austin Schlottmann with some extracurricular after a play. Simmons swung at  JC Latham in the scrum before Tanzel Smart grabbed Simmons. Coach Robert Saleh didn't like it. Stopped practice and gathered the group for a cool-down talk. Simmons was forced to work on a side field with Brian Bell (strength coach) and wasn't allowed to return to practice. 
 QB  Cam Ward connected with WR  Carnell Tate on a beautiful pass for the play of the day. Tate ran a post and Ward launched a deep pass that traveled at least 50 yards in the air. Tate showed explosiveness as he pulled away from Alontae Taylor to run down the ball for the touchdown. 
 One-on-ones were a little different for WRs/DBs under Saleh. It's more like seven-on-sevens but only allowing man defense. Saleh said he uses this format to facilitate more authentic route running instead of the unreasonably long-developing routes. The offensive line versus defensive line setup was the same as normal. 
 Backup QB  Will Levis and WR  Bryce Oliver connected on two deep passes. Levis worked a play-action pass to Oliver on a deep crossing route. Oliver caught the pass in between the safety and cornerback Keydrain Calligan . Oliver made a jumping catch on a go route from Levis later in the day. 
 LT  Dan Moore Jr . left practice during the second team period. Saleh acknowledged after practice that Moore was hurt, but he didn't have any specifics regarding the injury immediately after practice. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 The first day of pads had a really good pace and tempo. Both the offense and defense did a good job keeping each other off the ground for the most part.

 The defense had big hits from cornerback Nazeeh Johnson and linebacker Sean Brown , and quarterback  Cam Ward had two hiccups throwing across his body while rolling out -- resulting in interceptions.

 Coach Robert Saleh said the throws across the body are non-negotiable, especially the shallow ones. Safety  Amani Hooker came up with the first interception as a result of what Saleh said was a "poor decision" by Ward. Saleh called the second interception an elite play by defensive lineman  Jermaine Johnson II .

 Ward did have a couple of nice spot throws to  Wan'Dale Robinson  between defenders during team period. He also connected with veteran receiver Calvin Ridley on a well-placed pass to towards the sideline.

 Other observations:  

 
 WR  Elic Ayomanor continues to have a solid camp. He beat Micah Robinson at the line of scrimmage and caught a deep pass in the end zone from  Mitchell Trubisky . The two almost connected on another deep pass but Robinson was called for pass interference. Ayomanor caught a pass on a deep in-breaking route from Ward also. Saleh credited Ayomanor for the offseason preparation and confidence he's playing with. 
 Defensive line coach Aaron Whitecotton didn't like the lack of intensity during individual period, so he made the group do pushups. The defensive line goes nonstop during that period. Whitecotton has them do a lot of work on the sled and with bags but at a very fast pace. 
 JC Latham took part in the first team period but worked with a trainer on the third field for the remaining ones. Latham's absence allowed Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson to get some valuable reps as he competes with Austin Deculus for the swing tackle spot. 
 
 

 

 

 Saturday, Aug.1  
 The Titans hosted fans at training camp for the first time this summer, and they got to see a pretty solid day from quarterback  Cam Ward .

 Ward and Elic Ayomanor connected on a couple of deep passes along the sideline. It's clear Ward trusts Ayomanor to win in jump ball situations, as the second-year tandem has found success on those 50-50 passes in the three practices open to the media.

 Ward was sharp in team and 7-on-7 periods highlighted by a couple of three-completion streaks before giving way to  Mitchell Trubisky .

 Ayomanor has had a solid couple of days, making a living catching passes on deep in-breaking routes in addition to his big plays down the field. He is noticeably bigger and playing with more confidence this camp.

 More observations: 

 
 Offensive tackle  JC Latham returned to practice and took part in the first team period before sitting out the final two. Latham is working to improve his mental approach to the game. He hired a mental coach late last season and is working to better process the game and not let one bad play carryover to the next snap. 
 

 

 Thursday, July 30 

 The defense won the day, highlighted by two interceptions.

 Cedric Gray picked off a pass from Cam Ward that bounced off  Wan'Dale Robinson 's hands along the sideline during the first team period. James Williams Sr . got the other turnover when he stepped in front of a  Mitchell Trubisky  pass intended for Xavier Restrepo .  Jeffery Simmons and the defensive line forced multiple throwaways by Ward during both team periods, as well.

 The offense did come up with a big play when Ward found Elic Ayomanor for a long touchdown. Ward was under pressure but side armed a pass down the field, and Ayomanor skied over  Cor'Dale Flott  to make the catch before outracing the safety to the end zone. Bryce Oliver also came up with a long play when he caught a pass of over 60 yards from Trubisky with Joshua Williams in coverage. Other than those two plays, it was mostly quick passes, and the defense was all over it.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Right tackle JC Latham came off the PUP list and worked on a third field with the team's training staff. Latham is noticeably bigger after reporting to camp with a slimmed down physique last year. Coach Robert Saleh said Latham is expected to be a full participant when the team practices again Saturday (Friday is a walk thru closed to media). 
 Calvin Ridley appears to be feeling better after dealing with a stomach bug that limited him in practice Wednesday. Ridley took part in team…

title: 2026 Washington Commanders training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Commanders training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Washington Commanders camp is taking place in Ashburn, Virginia, and Commanders reporter John Keim has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Commanders camp. We will update this file often. Can Washington bounce back from an injury-plagued 2025 season? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Commanders camp 
 
 Daniels finds voice, aims to fill leadership void 
 Commanders tab ex-All-Pro WR Wes Welker to coach tight ends 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels continues to remind anyone watching practice of what he can do as a passer. Just in case last season caused anyone to forget.

 Daniels, who played in only four full games last year because of injuries, has looked sharp throughout the first week of training camp and Tuesday was no exception.

 Among the highlights:

 
 A deep out to receiver Terry McLaurin in which Daniels threw in rhythm for a nice completion. 
 He extended a play to his right, then threw back to the middle for tight end Ben Sinnott . Daniels kept his eyes upfield and, despite throwing back toward the middle, did not put the ball in danger and Sinnott caught the ball as he slid. 
 Two plays later he threw a perfect ball over a defender to Jaylin Lane , running a post route on the left side. The 5-foot-10 Lane needed to leap to finish the catch, but he jumped too soon and dropped the pass. 
 Daniels found receiver Luke McCaffrey running down the middle of the field for another long completion. A corner was covering McCaffrey and a safety closed fast, but the ball was delivered into the tight window. 
 

 Overall, Daniels, the NFC offensive rookie of the year in 2024, has looked sharp in camp.

 "With him, it's really easy," tight end Chig Okonkwo said. "You just got to be where you're supposed to be and he'll find you with that, with the accurate ball."

 

 Other observations: 

 
 Undrafted free agent Drew Stevens , battling Jake Moody for the placekicking job, has had a good camp thus far. On Tuesday, Stevens made all five of his field goals, ranging from 33-56 yards, while Moody missed two of those attempts. Moody missed from 49 and 56 yards. He also missed from 48 yards to cap one full-team drill, while Stevens didn't miss any of his three attempts to punctuate a series. 
 Right guard Sam Cosmi and left tackle Laremy Tunsil did not practice Tuesday. After a two-hour practice in pads Monday, it was considered a recovery day for Tunsil. Cosmi practiced Monday as well, though at one point appeared to be shaken up. 
 Receiver Dyami Brown had two nice catches -- one in which he worked back to the ball while draped by a corner and later on a slant pass. Brown helped Washington on screens two years ago. 
 Newly signed corner Fabian Moreau participated in practice after agreeing to a deal Monday night. He was a third-round pick by Washington in 2017 but left the team after the 2020 season. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 First-round pick Sonny Styles made his presence felt on the first play from scrimmage -- and the first day with pads.

 On an inside handoff to running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt , Styles filled the hole and popped the running back. Washington doesn't do live tackling so Styles then let up, but the impact was felt.

 Through the early part of camp, Styles has stood out because of his length and speed. He has been solid in coverage, particularly when in zone. He broke up a pass to receiver Jaylin Lane in one zone look Monday.

 Styles also showed what he could do as a blitzer, getting paired vs. running back Jeremy McNichols on one pressure -- and using his speed and power to attack his outside shoulder and win the rep. Styles has worked often alongside Frankie Luvu .

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Corner Trey Amos (fractured fibula) and punter Tress Way (biceps), both of whom are on the physically unable to perform list, will be re-evaluated Thursday. There's optimism about their progress. 
 Quarterback Jayden Daniels made a terrific throw on the run to the back of the end zone for tight end Chig Okonkwo in a red zone drill. Okonkwo was in the back of the end zone with corner Ahkello Witherspoon directly in front of him. Daniels threw the ball to Okonkwo's right, and the tight end waited until the last second to reach over for the ball so Witherspoon wouldn't be able to react. 
 Corner Mike Sainristil broke up passes to the corner of the end zone on consecutive plays. Receiver Terry McLaurin made a nice catch in the corner and tapped both feet in-bounds as fans in attendance cheered. 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Washington Commanders tight end John Bates will miss "a couple of weeks" after suffering a strained hamstring in practice Thursday, coach Dan Quinn said Saturday.

 Bates has been one of the NFL's best blocking tight ends and a player Washington values greatly. It does have some depth at the position with Chig Okonkwo , Ben Sinnott as well as Colson Yankoff . 

 Center Nick Allegretti will miss "the next week or so," according to Quinn, after straining a calf muscle on Wednesday, the first day of camp.

 The good news for Washington: receiver  Treylon Burks  returned to practice after missing Thursday because of a foot issue.

 Allegretti's situation also highlights Washington's center depth. He's started four games at center in his career -- a position he considers his most natural -- but 35 at guard. But backup Julian Good-Jones has played two snaps in his career and the third center is rookie sixth-round pick Matt Gulbin .

 "It does give you a window into where people are at," Quinn said.

 Quinn said because they don't view Allegretti's situation as long-term, the team is not in the market to add another veteran. However, after practice, the Commanders had two other linemen working on snaps and initial blocks at center: third-year lineman Brandon Coleman and first-year guard Tyler Cooper .

 Washington's coaches have said in the past that Coleman, who has started at left tackle and left guard in his first two seasons, could play all five line spots. He is currently battling Chris Paul for the starting left guard position.

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 The Commanders ran a drill simulating a late-game field goal attempt -- after running a play. The field goal unit had to sprint on the field and get in position for the kick. In this drill, incumbent Jake Moody made all three field goals while Drew Stevens made two, missing from 46 yards. Earlier, during another drill, Moody made all six of his field goal attempts while Stevens missed one. 
 Sinnott had a mixed day with two drops -- one coming on a perfect pass from Jayden Daniels into a narrow window. But Sinnott also made multiple catches. 
 One area Daniels has excelled at: getting through his progression in time so if he dumps the ball to his checkdown, that player has room to run. It happened again today with running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt . 
 Linebacker Sonny Styles showed his length and speed. He broke up one pass in zone, using his long arms to close on the ball. Another time he flashed to the area where the ball was thrown. Had there been live hitting, he would have hit the target as the ball arrived. 
 
 
 Thursday, July 30 
 Washington's tight ends have been far more active as a group than they had been the previous two seasons.

 Newly-signed Chig Okonkwo can be used all over, with wide receiver  Terry McLaurin saying…
